new.title: Lamech calls his wives to hear his boast of vengeance
new.speaker: Lamech
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Summons to hear, as recorded at Numbers 16:8 and Joshua 3:9; his seventy-times-seven vengeance contrasts Matthew 18:22.

new.title: Abram refuses Sodom's spoils but reserves his allies' share
new.speaker: Abram
new.note: Oath answering the king's request (ot-genesis-v14-21); stipulates portions for the young men and Eshcol, Aunan and Mamre.

new.title: Abraham tells Sarah to hurry and bake cakes for the visitors
new.speaker: Abraham
new.note: Hospitality order within the household; nearby records cover only 18:1–5.

new.title: Lot urges the visitors to lodge and wash in his house
new.speaker: Lot
new.note: Invitation pressed again in 19:3; Abraham's comparable offer is recorded (ot-genesis-v18-4, Laban's at ot-genesis-v24-31).

new.title: Lot begs the angel to let him flee to the nearby city
new.speaker: Lot
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request granted in 19:21; requests to messengers are recorded (ot-judges-v6-18). Omit if treated as prayer to God.

new.title: Abimelech tells Sarah to speak the truth in all things
new.speaker: Abimelech, king of Gerar
new.note: Rebuke after restoring her with a thousand didrachms; no record covers 20:16.

new.title: Abraham asks Abimelech to accept seven ewe lambs as witness
new.speaker: Abraham
new.note: Witness that Abraham dug the well, sealing the oath at the Well of Swearing (21:31).

new.title: The Hittites invite Abraham to bury his dead in their tombs
new.speaker: the sons of Heth
new.note: An offer like Ephron's, which the catalogue keeps as Study Context (ot-genesis-v23-11).

new.title: Abraham charges his servant to take Isaac a wife from his kindred
new.speaker: Abraham
new.recipient: his servant, the elder of his house
new.note: The oath's content; ot-genesis-v24-2 stops mid-sentence at 24:2 (alternatively extend it). Recounted 24:37–40.

new.title: Abraham's servant recounts his master's charge to seek Isaac's wife
new.speaker: Abraham's servant, recounting Abraham
new.note: Recount of 24:3–4; the catalogue keeps his other recounts separately (ot-genesis-v24-43, -45). Or link as Additional Scripture.

new.title: Abraham's servant asks Rebekah's family for a clear answer
new.speaker: Abraham's servant
new.note: 'Tell me... that I may turn to the right hand or to the left'; their reply is ot-genesis-v24-51.

new.title: Abraham gives his concubines' sons gifts and sends them east
new.speaker: Abraham
new.note: Estate settled in his lifetime: everything to Isaac, gifts to the others, who are sent away from Isaac.

new.title: Jacob tells the shepherds to water the sheep and pasture them
new.speaker: Jacob
new.recipient: the shepherds at the well near Harran
new.note: They decline until all the flocks are gathered (29:8).

new.title: Jacob offers to serve Laban seven years for Rachel
new.speaker: Jacob
new.note: Bride-service terms Laban accepts in 29:19 (ot-genesis-v29-19); such proposals are recorded (ot-genesis-v30-32).

new.title: Laban tells Jacob to finish Leah's week and serve seven more years
new.speaker: Laban
new.note: Laban's terms after the substitution of Leah; Jacob complies (29:28).

new.title: Leah tells Jacob to come in to her, hired with mandrakes
new.speaker: Leah
new.note: Follows the exchange recorded at ot-genesis-v30-14 (30:14–15).

new.title: Laban again asks Jacob to name his wages
new.speaker: Laban
new.note: A second wage negotiation; could instead be linked to ot-genesis-v29-15 as a parallel.

new.title: Jacob summons Rachel and Leah to the field
new.speaker: Jacob
new.note: Private summons before he recounts God's command to return (31:5–13); compare ot-genesis-v49-1.

new.title: Jacob invites Laban's search and sentences whoever has the gods
new.speaker: Jacob
new.note: 'Identify what is yours... take it'; the rash death sentence unknowingly falls on Rachel (31:34).

new.title: Laban forbids Jacob to mistreat his daughters or take other wives
new.speaker: Laban
new.note: Context verse, not flagged as candidate; a term of the Mizpah covenant with God as witness.

new.title: Laban and Jacob bind themselves not to cross the heap for harm
new.speaker: Laban; Jacob swears to it
new.note: Boundary term of the covenant proposed at ot-genesis-v31-44; God judges between them and Jacob swears (31:53).

new.title: Do not eat the sinew on the broad part of the thigh
new.speaker: the Torah narrative
new.note: Rambam N183 is not itemized anywhere; only broad Study Context torah-genesis-32-25. Narrated custom; origin follows Torah-requirement practice.

new.title: Dinah's brothers deceitfully demand that every Shechemite male be circumcised
new.speaker: Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers
new.note: Their condition for intermarriage, spoken with deceit (34:13); 34:14 is context.

new.title: Hamor and Shechem urge their townsmen to be circumcised
new.speaker: Hamor and Shechem
new.note: Core of the gate speech; neither ot-genesis-v34-21 nor ot-genesis-v34-23 records the circumcision demand.

new.title: Joseph tells his brothers to hear his dream
new.speaker: Joseph
new.note: A call to listen; compare ot-genesis-v49-1 and ot-judges-v9-7.

new.title: Joseph's brothers ask Jacob to identify the bloodstained tunic
new.speaker: Joseph's brothers
new.note: Deceptive request; echoed by Tamar's 'See to whom these belong' (38:25).

new.title: Judah tells Tamar to remain a widow until Shelah grows up
new.speaker: Judah
new.note: Deferral of the levirate duty; Judah privately fears for Shelah. Background to ot-genesis-v38-24.

new.title: Tamar demands Judah's ring, necklace and staff as a pledge
new.speaker: Tamar
new.note: Pledge terms behind ot-genesis-v38-23; Judah's proposition is ot-genesis-v38-16.

new.title: Judah sends the Adullamite with the goat to recover his pledge
new.speaker: Judah
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse). Payment promised in 38:17; the pledge demand is first-pass finding Genesis 38:17–18.

new.title: Tamar asks Judah to identify the owner of the pledge
new.speaker: Tamar
new.note: Context verse, not flagged as candidate; her appeal overturns the order at ot-genesis-v38-24.

new.title: Potiphar sets Joseph over his house and all he owns
new.speaker: Potiphar
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Narrated appointment (39:6 in batch); compare AUD-01-41-40. Same pattern: chief jailer at 39:22 and 40:4.

new.title: Potiphar's wife repeatedly demands that Joseph lie with her
new.speaker: Potiphar's wife
new.note: Chapter 39 has no records; compare ot-2-samuel-v13-11. Joseph refuses it as sin before God (39:9).

new.title: Pharaoh summons Joseph from the prison
new.speaker: Pharaoh
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Royal summons, like first-pass Exodus 7:11; the similar summons of Egypt's interpreters (41:8) is also unrecorded.

new.title: Jacob refuses to let Benjamin go down to Egypt
new.speaker: Jacob
new.note: Answers Reuben's offer (ot-genesis-v42-37); recounted at 44:27–29 and reversed at 43:13.

new.title: Judah tells Jacob they will not return without Benjamin
new.speaker: Judah
new.note: Quotes Joseph's warning (compare ot-genesis-v42-20); his second plea is ot-genesis-v43-8.

new.title: Joseph's brothers propose death for whoever has the cup
new.speaker: Joseph's brothers
new.note: Self-imposed penalty, modified by the steward in ot-genesis-v44-10; compare Jacob's sentence at 31:32.

new.title: Joseph rules that the cup's holder stays and the rest go home
new.speaker: Joseph
new.note: Joseph's verdict restating the steward's terms (ot-genesis-v44-10); it prompts Judah's plea.

new.title: Judah asks to speak and begs Joseph not to be angry
new.speaker: Judah
new.note: Opens Judah's plea (44:18–34); compare ot-genesis-v31-35, 'Do not take it badly, my lord'.

new.title: Jacob sends Judah ahead to meet Joseph
new.speaker: Jacob (Israel)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: A sending with a task, like ot-genesis-v37-13; Joseph comes out to meet them (46:29).

new.title: Joseph coaches his brothers to tell Pharaoh they keep livestock
new.speaker: Joseph
new.recipient: his brothers and his father's household
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Aimed at settlement in Goshen, since every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians; chapter has only torah-genesis-46-1.

new.title: Joseph's brothers ask Pharaoh to let them live in Goshen
new.speaker: Joseph's brothers
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request granted in 47:5–6 (ot-genesis-v47-5); it follows Joseph's coaching (first-pass Genesis 46:33–34).

new.title: Jacob charges his sons to bury him in the Machpelah cave
new.speaker: Jacob
new.note: Distinct from ot-genesis-v47-29 (Joseph alone); fulfilled in 50:12–13. 49:26–27 are blessings, out of scope.

new.title: Joseph orders the embalmers to prepare Jacob for burial
new.speaker: Joseph
new.note: Reported order; no record covers 50:1–3.

new.title: Joseph asks Pharaoh's court to request leave to bury Jacob
new.speaker: Joseph
new.note: Request precedes Pharaoh's permission (ot-genesis-v50-6) and cites Jacob's oath (ot-genesis-v47-29).

new.title: Pharaoh orders the Hebrew midwives to kill newborn boys
new.speaker: the king of Egypt (Pharaoh)
new.recipient: the Hebrew midwives Sepphora and Puah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The 1:16 order is unrecorded; only the later river decree (ot-exodus-v1-22) is itemized. The midwives refuse (1:17).

new.title: Pharaoh's daughter sends her attendant to fetch the basket
new.speaker: Pharaoh's daughter
new.note: Reported order that rescues Moses; her next directions are ot-exodus-v2-8.

new.title: Moses' sister offers to fetch a Hebrew nurse for Pharaoh's daughter
new.speaker: Moses' sister
new.note: Proposal answered by 'Go' in ot-exodus-v2-8; the catalogue records similar proposals (Genesis 16:2, 30:3).

new.title: Pharaoh sends Moses and Aaron back to their work
new.speaker: Pharaoh, king of Egypt
new.note: Direct order ('Each of you, go back to your work') preceding ot-exodus-v5-5.

new.title: The taskmasters press Israel to complete the full daily quota
new.speaker: Pharaoh's taskmasters
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Distinct from Pharaoh's orders (5:7–9) and the relayed edict (ot-exodus-v5-11).

new.title: Pharaoh summons Egypt's wise men and sorcerers to match the sign
new.speaker: Pharaoh
new.recipient: the wise men and sorcerers of Egypt
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported summons without quoted speech; the similar summons in Genesis 41:8 is also unrecorded.

new.title: The Lord sends Moses, staff in hand, to Pharaoh at the river
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: Occasion-specific orders (morning, riverbank, staff) and the blood warning; only broad torah-exodus-7-14. Demand repeats F003; C0063 is generic.

new.title: The Lord sends Moses to demand release under threat of frogs
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: Frog warning precedes C0083 (8:1); only broad torah-exodus-7-14. 'Let My people go' repeats F003.

new.title: Pharaoh asks Moses and Aaron to pray away the frogs
new.speaker: Pharaoh
new.note: Like the later request ot-exodus-v10-17; no record covers 8:4.

new.title: Moses invites Pharaoh to set the time for removing the frogs
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: 'Appoint a time for me' with a promise of removal; Pharaoh answers 'Tomorrow' (8:6).

new.title: The Lord sends Moses at dawn to warn Pharaoh of hail
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: Sending and demand (9:13) precede F004's shelter warning (9:19); only broad torah-exodus-9-13.

new.title: Pharaoh confesses and asks Moses to pray for the hail to stop
new.speaker: Pharaoh
new.note: Request unrecorded; cf. ot-exodus-v10-17. 9:29 is Moses' promise.

new.title: The Egyptians urge Israel to leave the land quickly
new.speaker: the Egyptians
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Fulfils Moses' word in 11:8; distinct from Pharaoh's own dismissal (ot-exodus-v12-31).

new.title: Let no leaven be seen with you within all your borders
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: Rambam N200 (no leaven seen) is missing; C0109 (12:19) itemizes only N201 (none found in houses).

new.title: Moses appoints leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: Reported appointment carrying out ot-exodus-v18-20; cf. C0956 (Deuteronomy 1:13).

new.title: The Lord tells Moses to set the ordinances before Israel
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Heading charge like ot-exodus-v19-6 ('words you shall speak'); only broad torah-exodus-21-1 covers it.

new.title: Repay double when the stolen animal is found alive with the thief
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: C0188 (21:37) covers fourfold and fivefold restitution; the double-payment case is unitemized.

new.title: A thief caught stealing entrusted goods repays double
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Base case of the deposit law; C0193–C0195 cover the thief-not-found procedure (22:7–8).

new.title: Do not pervert the justice due to the poor in his cause
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam N278 is missing; C0218 (23:2) is general and C0219 (23:3) forbids favouring the poor.

new.title: Israel pledges to do all that the Lord has spoken
new.speaker: the people of Israel
new.note: Communal covenant pledge, cf. ot-nehemiah-v10-32 (Law); the same pledge at 19:8 is outside candidate list.

new.title: Carry out the priests' ordination over seven days
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Seven-day ordination charge to Moses; C0459 (Leviticus 8:33) covers the priests' attendance, C0326 only successors.

new.title: Keep the Sabbaths as the lasting sign between God and Israel
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Sabbath-as-covenant-sign command is unitemized; C0354 covers only the death penalty (31:14–15). Cf. ot-ezekiel-v20-20.

new.title: Aaron proclaims a feast of the Lord before the calf
new.speaker: Aaron
new.note: Outside candidate list: public proclamation between ot-exodus-v32-2 and C0355; recording it does not approve it. 32:6 is narrative.

new.title: Moses makes Israel drink the ground calf in water
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); an imposed act rather than spoken words.

new.title: Offer firstfruit grain as roasted crushed groats with oil and frankincense
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: The firstfruits grain offering is unitemized; C0391 covers only leaven-and-honey firstfruits (2:11–12).

new.title: Eat the priests' grain portion unleavened; never bake it with leaven
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam N124 is missing; C0389 (2:11) bars leaven in the altar offering, not in the priests' portion.

new.title: Give oven- and pan-cooked grain offerings to the officiating priest
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Allocation rule unitemized (cf. C0446, the hide to the officiating priest, 7:8). 7:11 is a heading.

new.title: Share uncooked grain offerings equally among all Aaron's sons
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Companion allocation rule to 7:9; unitemized.

new.title: Use fat of carcasses and torn animals for work, never as food
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Distinct permission and prohibition; unitemized.

new.title: The right foreleg goes to the priest who offers blood and fat
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Officiating-priest allocation like C0446 (7:8); C0324 assigns the portions only to the priests generally.

new.title: Eat the breast and foreleg in a clean place with your household
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: Sons and daughters may share these portions (cf. Numbers 18:11, also unitemized); C0324 sets only the due.

new.title: Treat a prolonged or irregular flow of blood as menstrual uncleanness
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses and Aaron
new.recipient: a woman with a prolonged flow, and Israel
new.note: The woman's prolonged flow (15:25–30) has no itemized record; the male counterpart is C0533–C1239.

new.title: After touching a woman with a flow: wash, bathe, await evening
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses and Aaron
new.note: Mirrors C0534–C0536 for the male discharge.

new.title: Count seven days after a prolonged flow ceases before cleansing
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses and Aaron
new.recipient: a woman healed of a prolonged flow
new.note: Counterpart of C0539 (15:13) for the woman.

new.title: Bring two turtledoves or pigeons to the priest on the eighth day
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses and Aaron
new.recipient: a woman healed of a prolonged flow
new.note: Rambam P75 (offering of the woman with a flow) is missing; counterpart of C0542.

new.title: Priest: offer her birds as sin and burnt offerings for atonement
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses and Aaron
new.note: Counterpart of C1239 (15:15).

new.title: Station the two goats before the Lord at the Tent's entrance
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Precedes the lot (C0551); C1224 covers only the living goat.

new.title: Do not follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Frames Lev 18; same as 18:30 and 20:23 (only topical S094). C0241 (Ex 23:24) concerns idolatrous practices.

new.title: Keep God's statutes and judgments; whoever does them shall live by them
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Quoted at Rom 10:5 and Gal 3:12 but cited nowhere. Later repeats (18:26, 30; 19:37; 20:8; 22:31; 25:18; 26:3) could link here.

new.title: Priests: be holy to God and do not profane his name
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam N76 (one bathed that day may not serve) is not itemized; nearest C0671 (22:6–7) concerns eating.

new.title: A priest's lodger or hired worker may not eat holy things
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam N134 is not itemized.

new.title: A priest's purchased or house-born slaves may eat his holy food
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses

new.title: A priest's daughter married to an outsider may not eat holy portions
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam N137 is not itemized.

new.title: A returning childless priest's daughter may again eat her father's food
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Widowed or divorced and childless, she returns to her father's house.

new.title: Hallow God's name among the sons of Israel
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam P9 (sanctify the Name) is not itemized; the text says God will be sanctified among Israel.

new.title: Arrange the twelve loaves in two rows of six on the table
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Missing step between C0705 (bake, 24:5) and C0706 (eat, 24:9).

new.title: Put pure frankincense and salt on the rows as a memorial
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses

new.title: Do not wrong your neighbour when buying or selling
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam P245 and N250 are not itemized; C0605 (19:13) and C0603 (19:11) are general.

new.title: Do not oppress one another, but fear your God
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam N251 (wronging with words) is not itemized; the text repeats 25:14 after the pricing rules.

new.title: Do not let a foreign owner work an Israelite harshly
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
new.note: Rambam N260 is not itemized; C0735 (25:43, same wording) addresses an Israelite master.

new.title: Return a consecrated purchased field to its original owner at Jubilee
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Completes C0751 (27:22–23); compare C0720.

new.title: Present the Levites before the Lord as a gift from Israel
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: The presentation itself is missing between C0837 (8:10) and C0839 (8:12).

new.title: Separate the Levites as God's own and send them to Tent service
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Consecration-day separation and induction; compare C0781 (3:41) for the firstborn exchange.

new.title: Keep the Passover at its appointed time in the wilderness of Sinai
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Second-year Passover, relayed (9:4) and kept (9:5); compare C0094, C0103. Rambam N119, marked at 9:3, belongs to 9:12 (P00338).

new.title: Do not neglect the Passover when clean and not travelling
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Penalty of being cut off; C0841 covers only those prevented.

new.title: God shares Moses' Spirit with seventy elders to bear the people
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: C0849 covers only gathering the elders (11:16); 11:24–25 narrate the fulfilment.

new.title: Joshua urges Moses to forbid Eldad and Medad's prophesying
new.speaker: Joshua son of Nun
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Moses declines (11:29); compare Mark 9:38–39.

new.title: Aaron begs Moses not to hold their sin against them
new.speaker: Aaron
new.note: A plea to Moses on Miriam's behalf; Moses' prayer (12:13) is out of scope.

new.title: Caleb urges Israel to go up and possess the land
new.speaker: Caleb
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Exhortation against the scouts' report; compare ot-numbers-v14-9.

new.title: The people propose appointing a leader to return to Egypt
new.speaker: the people of Israel
new.note: A rebellious proposal, recorded as the catalogue records other plots (e.g. ot-genesis-v37-20); compare Neh 9:17.

new.title: Do not sin defiantly, despising the Lord's word
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: No atonement provision for presumptuous sin, unlike 15:22–29; such a person is cut off. Compare C1057 (Deut 17:12).

new.title: God orders the Sabbath-breaker stoned outside the camp
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Specific ruling, carried out at 15:36; general penalty C0354 (Ex 31:14–15). Like the blasphemer records C0707–C0709.

new.title: Moses summons Dathan and Abiram, who refuse to come
new.speaker: Moses
new.recipient: Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab
new.note: Summons and refusal ('We will not come up', 16:12, 14) fall between records 16:5–11 and 16:16–30.

new.title: God orders the congregation to withdraw from around Korah's tents
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: C0863 (16:21) is addressed to Moses and Aaron; C0864 covers only touching. Moses relays this at 16:26.

new.title: Aaron's house: bear responsibility for offences against sanctuary and priesthood
new.speaker: the Lord
new.recipient: Aaron, his sons and his father's house
new.note: Opens the priestly charge of Numbers 18; not itemized.

new.title: Priests' clean household members may eat the presented gifts
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Includes daughters, unlike C0875 (most holy, males only); Lev 10:14 is also unitemized.

new.title: Everything devoted in Israel belongs to the priests
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: C0755–C0756 (27:28) forbid selling or redeeming devoted things but do not assign them.

new.title: Do not defile the Lord's tent by neglecting corpse purification
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses and Aaron
new.note: Cut-off sanction for skipping the sprinkling (C0896), restated at 19:20 (P00374); compare C0546, Leviticus 15:31.

new.title: Moses asks the king of Edom to let Israel pass through
new.speaker: Moses, through messengers, in Israel's name
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Only Edom's refusal is recorded (AUD-04-20-18, which spans the renewed plea of 20:19); the first request has no record.

new.title: Israel vows to devote the Canaanite towns if God gives victory
new.speaker: Israel
new.note: Vow kept in 21:3; vows are recorded like first-pass Judges 11:30–31 and 1 Samuel 1:11.

new.title: Moses asks Sihon to let Israel pass along the royal road
new.speaker: Moses, through envoys
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Retold at Deuteronomy 2:26–29, where only 2:28 has a Study Context record (ot-deuteronomy-v2-28); link that retelling.

new.title: Moses sends men to spy out Jazer
new.speaker: Moses
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported sending, like ot-numbers-v13-17 and ot-joshua-v2-1.

new.title: Balaam bids Balak's envoys lodge overnight while he consults the Lord
new.speaker: Balaam
new.recipient: the elders of Moab and Midian
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Ordinary request of the kind recorded at ot-numbers-v23-3; 22:7 is narrative only.

new.title: Balaam sends Balak's officials home, saying God forbids his going
new.speaker: Balaam
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Balaam's own order, acting on God's prohibition (F005).

new.title: Balaam bids the second delegation stay overnight for God's further word
new.speaker: Balaam
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list: 22:19 has no record at all; it repeats the 22:8 request to the second delegation.

new.title: Offer the prescribed Weeks burnt and sin offerings with their accompaniments
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam P45 missing. Differs from the loaves' offerings at C0687 (Leviticus 23:18–19): two bulls, one ram. Covers 28:31 (P00396).

new.title: The Lord orders Moses to avenge Israel on Midian before his death
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Renews C0918 (25:17) as a charge to Moses; M019 records his relay to the people (31:3–4).

new.title: Wash clothes on the seventh day before re-entering the camp
new.speaker: Eleazar the priest, stating the Lord's ordinance
new.note: Completes the seven-day purification (M023, 31:19) under Eleazar's ordinance (31:21); C0934 covers only the captured articles.

new.title: Put to death whoever kills with a deadly weapon or in enmity
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Murder criteria with mandatory death are unitemized: C0946 covers accidental killing, C0945 the avenger; Exodus 21:12 also lacks a record.

new.title: Keeping God's statutes is your wisdom before the nations
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: Distinct teaching: obedience displays Israel's wisdom; no nation has a god so near or laws so righteous.

new.title: Turn neither right nor left; walk in all God's commanded way
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: Named in the torah-deuteronomy-5-1 title but not itemized; the same charge is recorded for Joshua (X002, Joshua 1:7).

new.title: Man does not live by bread alone but by God's every word
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: Quoted by Jesus (Matthew 4:4; Luke 4:4); Luke 4:4 now sits only on passage group torah-deuteronomy-8-1.

new.title: You may slaughter and eat meat locally, clean and unclean alike
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: Permits profane slaughter away from the sanctuary (modifies Leviticus 17:3–5). Rambam P86 (12:15) and P146 (12:21) missing.

new.title: Let no one again entice another to serve other gods
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: Rambam N16 (do not entice an Israelite to idolatry) missing; existing records cover only responses to the enticer (C1019–C1025).

new.title: Eat nothing abominable
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: General heading prohibition over 14:4–20 (S127 topical). Rambam N140 (rabbinic: disqualified offerings) missing.

new.title: You may eat every clean bird
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam P150. Only inside S127 (Deut 14:3–20, prohibited food) and the chapter group; the permission clause has no record.

new.title: Eat a blemished firstborn at home like gazelle or deer
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: Clean and unclean may eat it alike; distinct from the 15:20 sacred meal.

new.title: Stone the man or woman proven to have served other gods
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: C1053 covers only the inquiry (17:2–4); C0202 (Exodus 22:19) and C1025 are related penalties.

new.title: Give the priest the foreleg, cheeks and stomach of sacrifices
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.recipient: Israelites who slaughter cattle or sheep
new.note: Rambam P143 missing; distinct from the breast-and-thigh portions (C0324, Exodus 29:27–28).

new.title: Give the priest the first of your sheep's fleece
new.speaker: Moses, relaying the Lord
new.note: Rambam P144 missing.

new.title: Do not practise divination
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Context verse: C1071–C1072 cover only spoken omens and sorcery; Rambam's divination ban here is unitemized (C0629 is omen-reading).

new.title: Add three more refuge cities when God enlarges your borders
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Conditional addition beyond the six cities of Numbers 35; itemized nowhere. 19:10 gives the purpose.

new.title: Apply the devotion judgment to the seven named nations
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.recipient: Israel at war in the land
new.note: Rambam P187 missing: C0997 is negative only; C0245 (Exodus 23:33) concerns removal. 20:18 gives the reason.

new.title: Do not sow your vineyard with a different crop
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
new.note: Rambam N216 missing; C0622 (Leviticus 19:19) covers the field (N215), not the vineyard.

new.title: You may lend at interest to a foreigner, not your brother
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam P198 missing; the brother clause repeats 23:20 (C0206).

new.title: Perform what your lips have vowed; declining to vow is no sin
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Rambam P94 missing as a general positive: C0930 (Numbers 30:3) is negative; C0826 covers Nazirite vows only.

new.title: Do not pervert the judgment of the sojourner, orphan or widow
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Context verse: C1177 covers only the widow's pledge; Rambam N280 missing. Deuteronomy 27:19 belongs with it.

new.title: Remember your slavery in Egypt as the reason for these laws
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: Motive command repeated at 24:22 (and 24:20 in Saints); C0116 (Exodus 13:3) is a Passover remembrance.

new.title: Bring firstfruits in a basket to the place God chooses
new.speaker: the Lord through Moses
new.note: First step of the itemized rite (C1198–C1201); the general law is C0237 (Exodus 23:19, Rambam P125).

new.title: Moses and the elders charge Israel to keep all the commandments
new.speaker: Moses and the elders of Israel
new.note: The only joint charge by Moses and the elders; compare the 27:9 records for Moses and the priests.

new.title: Guard against any heart turning from God to the nations' gods
new.speaker: Moses
new.recipient: every man, woman, family and tribe of Israel
new.note: Broad record names 'reject hidden idolatry'; the 'root of bitterness' is quoted at Hebrews 12:15 (A093). 29:21–24 are predictions.

new.title: Hidden things belong to God; revealed things are ours to do
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: Context verse, not flagged as a candidate; a well-known maxim with no itemized record. 29:27 itself is narrative.

new.title: The commandment is not beyond reach; the word is near you
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: Broad record names 'the word is near'; Romans 10:6–8 quotes it. 30:1–10 are restoration promises (compare C0983).

new.title: Moses tells Israel to be strong and unafraid in taking the land
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: The broad record's 'Be strong' is unitemized; C1213 is the separate charge to Joshua. Hebrews 13:5 cites 31:6.

new.title: Joshua is charged at the tent to lead Israel into the land
new.speaker: Moses at the tent commission (the Lord, in the Hebrew)
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: The charge for which Joshua was summoned in 31:14 (C1216–C1217) has no record itself; 31:20–21 are prediction.

new.title: Take these words to heart and command your children to keep them
new.speaker: Moses
new.note: Broad record names 'teach the words to children'; compare C0978 (Deuteronomy 4:9–10). 32:47 gives the motive: 'this is your life'.

new.title: Joshua tells the people to purify themselves for tomorrow's wonders
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside ot-joshua-v3-3 (3:3–6), whose title covers only the officers' order.

new.title: Joshua tells the priests to lift the ark and go ahead
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); inside ot-joshua-v3-3, whose title covers only the officers' order.

new.title: Joshua consecrates Jericho's metals to the Lord's treasury
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Distinct from 6:17 (the ban) and 6:18 (the warning): the metals go into the treasury.

new.title: Joshua forbids rebuilding Jericho under an oath-curse
new.speaker: Joshua, by an oath before the Lord
new.note: A binding oath-prohibition, its fulfilment narrated in the verse; compare C1030 (Deuteronomy 13:17).

new.title: Joshua sends men to spy out Ai
new.speaker: Joshua
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Direct charge ('Spy out Ai'), like ot-joshua-v2-1; their report is ot-joshua-v7-3.

new.title: The Lord decrees burning for the one taken with banned goods
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Sentence for the ban violation; ot-joshua-v7-14 covers only the identification by lot.

new.title: Joshua sends messengers to Achar's tent for the hidden goods
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Verifies the confession (7:19–21) before the judgment decreed in 7:15 (first-pass finding).

new.title: Joshua orders the king of Ai's body taken down at sunset
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Applies Deuteronomy 21:23 (C1120); 10:27 repeats it for the five kings.

new.title: Joshua and the leaders covenant by oath to let Gibeon live
new.speaker: Joshua and the leaders of the congregation
new.note: The binding oath enforced in 9:18–20 and avenged in 2 Samuel 21; compare first-pass Joshua 24:25–27.

new.title: Joshua orders the cave sealed and guarded over the five kings
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Distinct from the pursuit order that follows (ot-joshua-v10-19).

new.title: Joshua orders the five kings' bodies taken down at sunset
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Applies Deuteronomy 21:23 (C1120), as at Ai (8:29).

new.title: Jabin of Hazor summons the northern kings to fight Israel
new.speaker: Jabin king of Hazor
new.recipient: Jobab king of Marron and the northern kings
new.note: Reported summons, like ot-joshua-v10-4 (Jerusalem's king calls his allies).

new.title: Caleb asks Joshua for the promised hill country
new.speaker: Caleb son of Jephunneh
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Joshua 14 has no records; 14:6–11 is Caleb's case (14:9 a promise), 14:13 the grant.

new.title: Caleb promises his daughter to whoever takes the City of Letters
new.speaker: Caleb
new.note: Public offer, like first-pass 1 Chronicles 11:6; Judges 1:12 repeats it and is also unrecorded.

new.title: By God's command Israel gives Joshua the city he requested
new.speaker: the Lord (reported), at Joshua's request
new.note: 21:42b (Greek addition, passage Q04166) repeats the grant; Joshua 19 has no records.

new.title: Israel sends Phinehas and ten leaders to confront the eastern tribes
new.speaker: the sons of Israel (the congregation)
new.recipient: Phinehas son of Eleazar and ten tribal leaders
new.note: 22:13–15 outside candidate list. Envoys speak ‘thus says the whole congregation’ (22:16); only their warning (ot-joshua-v22-19) is recorded.

new.title: Joshua warns Israel not to intermarry with the remaining nations
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Warning distinct from 23:11 (love the Lord); compare C0998 (Deuteronomy 7:3). 23:14–16 echo 23:6–8.

new.title: Israel pledges at Shechem to serve the Lord alone
new.speaker: the people of Israel
new.note: Covenant pledge inside X004, whose title covers only Joshua’s charge; compare first-pass P00203 (Exodus 24:3, 7). Could merge with first-pass P00591.

new.title: Joshua makes a covenant, gives statutes, and sets a witness stone
new.speaker: Joshua
new.note: Covenant ratification with law and judgment (24:25) and a witness stone (24:27); no record covers 24:25–27.

new.title: Othniel urges Achsah to ask her father for a field
new.speaker: Othniel
new.note: Saints Judges reading; in Joshua 15:18 Achsah consults him instead. Caleb's question needs no record.

new.title: The Lord raises up Ehud as Israel’s deliverer from Moab
new.speaker: the Lord (narrated)
new.note: Narrated divine appointment; Israel then sends him with tribute. Othniel’s identical formula (3:9) is also unrecorded: report both or neither.

new.title: Barak asks Deborah to go with him into battle
new.speaker: Barak
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Conditional request; Deborah's reply (4:9) is consent and prophecy.

new.title: Barak summons Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh
new.speaker: Barak
new.recipient: the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali
new.note: Outside candidate list. Reported muster carrying out Deborah’s order (ot-judges-v4-6); first-pass P00601 noted it unrecorded but proposed only Sisera’s muster.

new.title: Sisera musters his chariots and army at the Kishon
new.speaker: Sisera
new.note: Reported muster order; Barak's muster (4:10) is likewise unrecorded.

new.title: Sisera asks Jael for a little water to drink
new.speaker: Sisera
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Ordinary request between 4:18 and 4:20, both recorded.

new.title: Deborah and Barak call Israel to bless the Lord
new.speaker: Deborah and Barak
new.note: Call to worship addressed to the people; repeated at 5:9 (outside this batch). 5:3 is Study Context.

new.title: Joash refuses to surrender Gideon and lets Baal defend himself
new.speaker: Joash
new.recipient: the men of the city demanding Gideon’s death
new.note: Counter-ruling to the recorded demand (6:30): whoever pleads for Baal shall die; ‘if he is a god, he himself shall avenge’.

new.title: Gideon summons Abiezer and sends messengers to rally four tribes
new.speaker: Gideon
new.recipient: Abiezer and the men of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali
new.note: Outside candidate list. Reported muster by trumpet and messengers. Candidate 6:39 is a petition to God and needs nothing.

new.title: Gideon tells the three hundred to copy him and blow trumpets
new.speaker: Gideon
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Battle orders: ‘as I do, so shall you do’; sound the trumpets around the camp and cry ‘For the Lord and for Gideon!’

new.title: Gideon asks Succoth for bread for his exhausted men
new.speaker: Gideon
new.note: Same request made to Penuel (8:8); both refuse and are punished (8:16–17).

new.title: Zebah and Zalmunna ask Gideon to strike them down himself
new.speaker: Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list. Request backed by the saying ‘as the man is, so is his strength’; compare ot-judges-v9-54 and ot-1-samuel-v31-4.

new.title: Israel asks Gideon to rule; he answers that the Lord will rule
new.speaker: the men of Israel; Gideon replies
new.note: Offer of hereditary rule and Gideon’s refusal; the earring request (8:24) is recorded separately.

new.title: Gaal incites Shechem against Abimelech and dares him to come out
new.speaker: Gaal son of Abed
new.note: Incitement to revolt (‘why should we serve him?’) with a taunt; Zebul’s answering challenge (9:38) is recorded.

new.title: Abimelech orders his men to cut branches as he did
new.speaker: Abimelech
new.note: ‘What you have seen me do, do quickly as I have done’; they burn the stronghold of Shechem’s Tower (9:49).

new.title: Gilead’s rulers promise headship to whoever leads against Ammon
new.speaker: the rulers of Gilead’s people
new.note: Public offer of leadership, fulfilled when the elders enlist Jephthah as head (AUD-07-11-8).

new.title: Jephthah sends envoys to rebut Ammon’s claim to Gilead
new.speaker: Jephthah
new.recipient: the king of the sons of Ammon, through messengers
new.note: Two embassies (11:12, 11:14–27); Ammon’s demand (11:13) is recorded but Jephthah’s reply, ending ‘May the Lord judge’, is not.

new.title: Jephthah vows to offer whoever first meets him on his return
new.speaker: Jephthah
new.note: Binding vow later carried out (11:35, 39: ‘I cannot turn back’); compare C0930. Addressed to God, hence medium.

new.title: Israel’s daughters lament Jephthah’s daughter four days every year
new.speaker: the narrator (an ordinance in Israel)
new.note: Outside candidate list. Narrated ‘ordinance in Israel’, comparable to the recorded statute at 1 Samuel 30:24–25 (ot-1-samuel-v30-24).

new.title: Gilead’s guards make Ephraimite fugitives say the password at the fords
new.speaker: the men of Gilead
new.recipient: Ephraimite fugitives at the Jordan crossings
new.note: The Shibboleth test (‘Please say Password’); only the fugitives’ request to cross (12:5) is recorded.

new.title: The messenger forbids a razor on the promised Nazirite child’s head
new.speaker: the Lord’s messenger
new.note: Not covered by the diet records (13:4, 13:7, 13:13–14). Samson restates it at 16:17: link as Additional Scripture.

new.title: Manoah urges the messenger to stay for a meal of goat
new.speaker: Manoah
new.note: Hospitality request, like Gideon’s recorded request to the messenger (ot-judges-v6-18).

new.title: The messenger declines food and directs the offering to the Lord
new.speaker: the Lord’s messenger
new.note: ‘If you prepare a whole burnt offering, offer it to the Lord’; compare ot-judges-v6-20. Manoah obeys (13:19).

new.title: The Timnites appoint thirty companions to attend Samson
new.speaker: the people of Timnah
new.note: Reported appointment of wedding companions, made out of fear; they become the riddle’s counterparties (14:12–15).

new.title: The Timnite men threaten Samson’s wife into coaxing out the riddle
new.speaker: the men of Timnah (Samson’s companions)
new.note: Outside candidate list. Coercive order (‘Deceive your husband… lest we burn you’); compare the Delilah commission (AUD-07-16-5).

new.title: Samson asks his guide to let him feel the pillars
new.speaker: Samson
new.recipient: the boy leading him by the hand
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request setting up the temple’s collapse; the boy complies. The prayer in 16:28 is addressed to God.

new.title: Micah’s mother consecrates the silver to make a carved and cast image
new.speaker: Micah’s mother
new.note: Dedication for an idol, carried out through the caster (17:4); recording it implies no approval. Her blessing (17:2) needs nothing.

new.title: Micah installs one of his sons as priest of his shrine
new.speaker: Micah
new.note: Outside candidate list. He ‘filled the hand’ (ordained) an unauthorized priest before hiring the Levite (ot-judges-v17-10); recording implies no approval.

new.title: The Danite scouts ask Micah’s priest to inquire of God
new.speaker: the five Danite scouts
new.note: Request answered by the priest’s recorded send-off (18:6, Study Context).

new.title: The scouts point out Micah’s idols and tell the Danites to decide
new.speaker: the five Danite scouts
new.note: ‘Now consider what you shall do’ prompts the seizure of the ephod and images (18:17–18).

new.title: The servant proposes lodging in Jebus, and the Levite refuses
new.speaker: the Levite’s servant; his master replies
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Proposal and refusal before the recorded plan for Gibeah or Ramah (19:13); compare the paired proposals at ot-1-samuel-v9-5.

new.title: Israel demands that Benjamin hand over Gibeah’s guilty men
new.speaker: Israel’s tribes, through messengers
new.note: ‘Hand over the impious men… and remove wickedness from Israel’ echoes the Deuteronomic purge formula; Benjamin refuses.

new.title: Israel arranges a smoke signal with the ambush at Gibeah
new.speaker: the men of Israel
new.note: 20:38 is outside the candidate list. A prearranged battle signal, like recorded signal instructions (ot-1-samuel-v20-21).

new.title: Israel swears that none will give a daughter to Benjamin
new.speaker: the men of Israel at Mizpah
new.note: Communal oath restated at 21:7 and with a curse at 21:18 (link both); it drives the Jabesh and Shiloh measures.

new.title: Israel’s congregation sends to Benjamin at Rimmon offering peace
new.speaker: the whole congregation of Israel
new.recipient: the Benjaminite survivors at the rock of Rimmon
new.note: Outside candidate list. Reported call to peace. Candidates 21:16–18 are deliberation; their oath is noted under P00653.

new.title: Naomi advises Ruth to keep with Boaz’s maidens for safety
new.speaker: Naomi
new.note: Counsel lest Ruth be molested in another field; Ruth follows it (2:23). The blessings in 2:19–20 need nothing.

new.title: Ruth asks Boaz to spread his garment over her as redeemer
new.speaker: Ruth
new.note: Ruth’s request for marriage and redemption, the hinge of the book; Boaz’s reply is recorded at 3:13.

new.title: Boaz calls the nearer kinsman to redeem Naomi’s field or decline
new.speaker: Boaz
new.note: ‘Acquire it before… the elders… if not, tell me’; the marriage condition (4:5) and his refusal (4:6) are recorded.

new.title: Boaz calls the elders and people to witness his redemption
new.speaker: Boaz
new.recipient: the elders and all the people at the gate
new.note: 4:9 is outside the candidate list. The people answer ‘We are witnesses’ (4:11); the elders’ blessing needs nothing.

new.title: Hannah vows her son to the Lord as a lifelong Nazirite
new.speaker: Hannah
new.note: Vow with Nazirite terms (no wine, no razor), fulfilled at 1:24–28; addressed to God, hence medium.

new.title: Hannah presents Samuel at Shiloh, lending him to the Lord for life
new.speaker: Hannah
new.note: 1:27–28 are outside the candidate list: the dedication fulfilling her vow (1:11) places Samuel in the Lord’s service at Shiloh.

new.title: No one can intercede for a person who sins against the Lord
new.speaker: Eli
new.note: Maxim closing Eli’s rebuke (ot-1-samuel-v2-24; the uncovered 2:23 opens it). Compare the separately recorded maxim at 15:22 (AUD-09-15-22).

new.title: God honours those who honour him; those who despise him are dishonoured
new.speaker: the Lord through a man of God
new.note: Outside candidate list. A declarative principle within the oracle against Eli’s house; the surrounding judgments need nothing.

new.title: The Lord calls the boy Samuel and entrusts him with his word
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Samuel’s prophetic call; 3:19–21 confirm him as prophet to all Israel. Only Eli’s directions (3:5–6, 3:9, 3:17) are recorded.

new.title: Samuel appoints his sons as judges over Israel
new.speaker: Samuel
new.note: Reported appointment, like other recorded appointments (AUD-11-4-7); the sons’ corruption prompts the demand for a king (8:3–5).

new.title: Samuel anoints Saul as ruler over the Lord’s people
new.speaker: Samuel, acting for the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Only the Lord’s order to anoint (9:16) is recorded, not the anointing and charge to save Israel; 11:15 reports a second anointing.

new.title: Samuel tells Saul to act as occasion serves once the signs come
new.speaker: Samuel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: ‘Do everything your hand finds, for God is with you’; lies between the recorded directions at 10:3–4 and 10:8.

new.title: Samuel declares the kingship’s rights and lays the scroll before the Lord
new.speaker: Samuel
new.note: Outside candidate list. Written ordinance of the kingship, contents unstated; compare the king’s law (C1065). The acclamation in 10:24 needs nothing.

new.title: Nahash demands every right eye as the price of a treaty
new.speaker: Nahash the Ammonite
new.note: Cruel surrender terms between the recorded requests of Jabesh (11:1, 11:3).

new.title: Saul summons Israel to war with pieces of oxen and a threat
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: Call to arms under threat (‘Whoever does not come out after Saul and Samuel—they will do this to his oxen!’); the muster follows (11:8).

new.title: The people demand death for those who scorned Saul
new.speaker: the people
new.note: Demand refused by Saul (11:13); compare the recorded demand for Gideon’s death (ot-judges-v6-30).

new.title: Saul forbids any execution on the day of the Lord’s deliverance
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: Royal clemency comparable to David’s (AUD-10-19-22, 2 Samuel 19:22–24).

new.title: Samuel makes obeying the Lord the condition for people and king
new.speaker: Samuel
new.note: Covenant terms: fear, serve and obey the Lord and do not rebel, or his hand will be against you and your king.

new.title: Israel asks Samuel to pray for them after the thunder
new.speaker: all the people
new.note: Distinct from the earlier request (ot-1-samuel-v7-8); they confess the sin of asking for a king.

new.title: Ceasing to pray for God’s people would be sin against the Lord
new.speaker: Samuel
new.note: Samuel’s commitment to intercede and teach the good way, stated as a principle; personal statement, hence low.

new.title: Saul chooses three thousand men and sends the rest home
new.speaker: Saul
new.recipient: three thousand chosen men; the rest of the people
new.note: Reported selection of a standing army, a thousand placed under Jonathan at Geba; like the appointment in first-pass P00716.

new.title: Saul sounds the trumpet throughout the land to rally Israel
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: Trumpet call after Jonathan’s strike; the people are called out after Saul to Gilgal (13:4). Compare first-pass musters P00609 and P00601.

new.title: Saul orders a muster to find who has left the camp
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: The muster shows that Jonathan and his armour-bearer are missing.

new.title: Saul puts the army under oath not to eat before evening
new.speaker: King Saul
new.note: Royal oath-decree (‘Cursed is the man who eats bread’), restated at 14:28 (link); it leads to Jonathan’s condemnation.

new.title: The people refuse Jonathan’s execution and rescue him by oath
new.speaker: the people
new.note: Collective oath overriding Saul’s sentence (ot-1-samuel-v14-44): ‘not one hair of his head shall fall’.

new.title: Saul asks Samuel to pardon his sin and return with him
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: First plea, refused (15:26); the second plea is recorded at 15:30.

new.title: Saul orders his servants to find him a skilled musician
new.speaker: Saul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Saul acts on his servants’ recorded proposal (16:16); it leads to David’s summons (16:19).

new.title: Saul asks Jesse to let David remain in his service
new.speaker: Saul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: A second request to Jesse, after the recorded summons (16:19).

new.title: The Lord saves not by sword and spear; the battle is his
new.speaker: David
new.note: 17:45 and 17:47 are outside the candidate list; candidate 17:46 is defiance and prediction. Compare ot-2-chronicles-v20-15.

new.title: Saul removes David and appoints him commander of a thousand
new.speaker: Saul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported appointment, made out of fear (18:12); the catalogue records other narrated appointments (AUD-11-4-7).

new.title: Saul demands a hundred Philistine foreskins as David’s bride-price
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: Order to his servants carrying a deadly bride-price; David fulfils it (18:27).

new.title: Michal warns David to escape that night or be killed
new.speaker: Michal
new.note: Urgent warning like Jonathan’s (ot-1-samuel-v19-2); she lowers him through the window (19:12).

new.title: Saul sends three bands of messengers to seize David at Naioth
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: Reported order given three times; each band prophesies instead, then Saul goes himself (19:22–24). Distinct from 19:11–15.

new.title: David asks Abimelech for bread and receives the holy loaves
new.speaker: David; Abimelech the priest replies
new.note: The priest’s purity condition (21:5) bears on C0706; Jesus cites this episode at Mark 2:25–26 (K013).

new.title: David asks the priest Abimelech for a spear or sword
new.speaker: David
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request answered with Goliath’s sword (‘Give it to me’, 21:10); the priest’s offer is only a Study Context record (ot-1-samuel-v21-10).

new.title: Achish rebukes his servants and bars the feigning David from his house
new.speaker: Achish king of Gath
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Royal refusal (‘This one shall not enter a house’) that secures David’s escape.

new.title: David asks Moab’s king to shelter his father and mother
new.speaker: David
new.topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
new.note: Care for his parents while he is a fugitive; the king grants it (22:4).

new.title: Saul summons Abimelech and all the priests of Nob
new.speaker: Saul
new.recipient: Abimelech son of Ahitub and his father’s house
new.note: Reported summons leading to the massacre ordered at 22:17–18; 22:12 is only a Study Context record.

new.title: Saul summons all the people to besiege David at Keilah
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: Reported order. David’s inquiries of the Lord (23:10–11) are prayers, and the oracle answers give no direction.

new.title: Saul sends the Ziphites to pinpoint David’s hiding places
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: Follows their recorded invitation (23:20); Saul’s blessing (23:21) needs nothing.

new.title: A messenger urges Saul to come quickly against a Philistine raid
new.speaker: a messenger
new.note: The summons that turns Saul back from David at the Divided Rock (23:28).

new.title: David shows Saul the cloak flap and pleads his innocence
new.speaker: David
new.note: 24:10–11 are outside the candidate list. ‘Know and see…’; David leaves judgment to the Lord. Compare the 26:19–20 records.

new.title: From the lawless comes wrongdoing, as the ancient proverb says
new.speaker: David, quoting an ancient proverb
new.note: Quoted proverb from which David concludes, ‘my hand shall not be against you’.

new.title: Saul affirms that the Lord rewards one who spares his enemy
new.speaker: Saul
new.note: Casuistic maxim (‘If someone finds his enemy in distress…’) generalizing David’s mercy; compare Proverbs 25:21–22. Not covered by ot-1-samuel-v24-22.

new.title: David orders his men to strap on their swords against Nabal
new.speaker: David
new.note: ‘Each of you strap on his sword’: four hundred go up while two hundred stay with the baggage; Abigail’s intervention halts them.

new.title: Nabal’s servant urges Abigail to act before disaster strikes
new.speaker: one of Nabal’s young men
new.note: ‘Now know and see what you will do’ prompts Abigail’s intervention; a servant’s urging like the chapter’s other recorded requests.

new.title: David swears to leave no male of Nabal’s house alive
new.speaker: David
new.note: Rash oath of vengeance, abandoned after Abigail’s plea (25:32–34; AUD-09-25-30); vows are recorded as in first-pass P00623.

new.title: Abigail asks David to hear her and disregard foolish Nabal
new.speaker: Abigail
new.note: Opening requests of Abigail’s plea; only 25:27 and 25:30–31 of her speech are recorded.

new.title: Abigail asks David to forgive her trespass
new.speaker: Abigail
new.note: ‘Please take away your handmaid’s lawless deed’ is a request to David, not a prayer; 25:29 is assurance and needs nothing.

new.title: David sends servants to ask Abigail to become his wife
new.speaker: David, through his servants
new.note: Marriage proposal by messengers (‘David has sent us to you to take you as his wife’); Abigail consents and follows them.

new.title: David sends spies to confirm that Saul has come
new.speaker: David
new.note: Reported sending, like ot-joshua-v2-1 (Joshua sends two spies).

new.title: David asks who will go down with him into Saul’s camp
new.speaker: David
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Call for a volunteer; Abishai answers, ‘I will enter with you.’

new.title: The Lord repays each one’s righteousness and faithfulness
new.speaker: David
new.note: General maxim grounding David’s restraint toward the Lord’s anointed; compare first-pass P01485 (Greek Psalm 61:13) and P00736 (1 Samuel 24:20).

new.title: David asks Achish for a place in a country town
new.speaker: David
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Direct request (‘please let them give me a place’); Achish grants Ziklag in 27:6. Chapter has only the 27:11 context record.

new.title: Achish enlists David for war and appoints him his bodyguard
new.speaker: Achish
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Achish requires David to march with him (‘you will go out with me to war’) and names him chief bodyguard for life.

new.title: Saul expels the mediums and spiritists from the land
new.speaker: King Saul
new.note: Outside candidate list. Narrated royal measure enforcing C0637 and C1074, recalled by the medium (28:9) and broken by Saul himself.

new.title: Saul asks the summoned Samuel to tell him what to do
new.speaker: Saul
new.recipient: Samuel, brought up by the medium
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request for counsel after God stopped answering; follows the recorded requests to the medium (28:8–13). Samuel answers with judgment.

new.title: The Egyptian asks David to swear to spare him before guiding him
new.speaker: David; the Egyptian servant
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: David asks to be led to the raiders; the Egyptian demands an oath not to be killed or handed back to his master.

new.title: David sends shares of the spoil to the elders of Judah
new.speaker: David
new.recipient: the elders of Judah and his allies’ towns
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Gifts sent with a message (‘from the spoils of the Lord’s enemies’), like first-pass envoy commissions P00770 and P00771.

new.title: The men of Judah anoint David king over Judah
new.speaker: the men of Judah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Royal anointing at Hebron, which David reports to Jabesh (2:7); compare first-pass P00689 (Samuel anoints Saul).

new.title: Abner makes Saul’s son Ish-bosheth king over Israel
new.speaker: Abner son of Ner
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list. Rival installation at Mahanaim; this translation calls him Mephibosheth at 3:7 and 4:8.

new.title: Abner appeals to Joab to call off the pursuit of their brothers
new.speaker: Abner
new.note: Appeal in question form (‘How long will you fail to tell the people to turn back…?’); Joab’s trumpet then recalls the army.

new.title: David orders Joab and the people to mourn Abner in sackcloth
new.speaker: David
new.recipient: Joab and all the people with him
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Explicit royal order: ‘Tear your garments, put on sackcloth, and beat yourselves in mourning before Abner.’

new.title: The people urge David to eat; he vows to fast until evening
new.speaker: all the people; David
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported urging to take the funeral meal, refused with an oath; compare ot-1-samuel-v28-22 (the medium urging Saul to eat).

new.title: David orders the execution of the murderers of Saul’s son
new.speaker: David
new.note: No record in this chapter. Saul’s son is called Mephibosheth in this translation (Ishbosheth in Hebrew); compare ot-2-samuel-v1-15.

new.title: Israel’s elders covenant with David and anoint him king over Israel
new.speaker: all Israel’s tribes and elders
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: AUD-10-5-2 records only the quoted divine word (5:2). Same event as first-pass P00963 (1 Chronicles 11:3): one record citing both.

new.title: David orders his men to strike Zion’s Jebusites with the dagger
new.speaker: David
new.note: Includes the resulting saying ‘The blind and the lame shall not enter the Lord’s house.’ Parallel 1 Chronicles 11:6 is unrecorded.

new.title: Hiram of Tyre sends envoys, cedar and craftsmen to build David’s house
new.speaker: Hiram king of Tyre
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Envoys sent with builders, like first-pass P00996 (Hiram sends Huram-abi to Solomon); parallel 1 Chronicles 14:1 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Toi sends his son to greet David with gifts
new.speaker: Toi king of Hamath
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Envoy sent with a charge to ask peace and bless David, like ot-1-samuel-v25-5. Parallel 1 Chronicles 18:10 is unrecorded.

new.title: David seeks Saul’s survivors to show kindness and summons Mephibosheth
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Keeping his covenant with Jonathan (ot-1-samuel-v20-15); he summons Ziba, then fetches Mephibosheth from Lo-debar. 9:7 is only Study Context.

new.title: David sends envoys to comfort Hanun after his father’s death
new.speaker: David
new.note: Context verse, not a flagged candidate (10:3–4 need nothing). Compare ot-1-samuel-v25-5; parallel 1 Chronicles 19:2 is unrecorded.

new.title: David sends Joab and the whole army against Ammon
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Reported dispatch answering Ammon’s hire of Syrian troops; parallel 1 Chronicles 19:8 is unrecorded (an S03 candidate): one record citing both.

new.title: Hadadezer summons the Syrians from beyond the River
new.speaker: Hadadezer
new.recipient: the Syrians beyond the River, under Shobach
new.note: Reported muster like first-pass P00601 (Sisera); parallel 1 Chronicles 19:16 is an S03 candidate. David’s answering muster (10:17) is narrative.

new.title: David sends Joab and all Israel to besiege Rabbah
new.speaker: King David
new.recipient: Joab, his servants and all Israel
new.note: Reported dispatch while David stays in Jerusalem, the setting for the orders concerning Bathsheba and Uriah.

new.title: David sends messengers to inquire about and take Bathsheba
new.speaker: King David
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported orders behind the adultery, before the recorded orders about Uriah (11:6–15); Nathan’s oracle condemns the taking (12:9).

new.title: Joab instructs the messenger how to report Uriah’s death to David
new.speaker: Joab
new.note: Detailed reported instruction (‘Then say, Your servant Uriah the Hittite also died’); no record between 11:15 and 11:25.

new.title: David sends for the widowed Bathsheba and takes her as wife
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Reported summons into marriage after the mourning, judged evil in the Lord’s eyes; compare David’s proposal to Abigail (1 Samuel 25:39–40).

new.title: The Lord sends Nathan to confront David with a parable
new.speaker: the Lord
new.recipient: Nathan the prophet, sent to David
new.note: First pass noted this commission unrecorded (P00775 covers David’s verdict, 12:5–6). Compare ot-1-kings-v12-23 and ot-isaiah-v22-15.

new.title: David rules that the rich man in Nathan’s parable must repay sevenfold
new.speaker: David
new.note: Royal verdict applying the restitution law (C0188, Exodus 21:37). Nathan’s commission in 12:1 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Fast and plead while there is hope; the dead do not return
new.speaker: David
new.note: David’s rationale for ending his fast (‘I will go to him, but he will not return to me’); include only if such reflections are itemized.

new.title: The Lord, through Nathan, names Solomon Jedidiah
new.speaker: the Lord through Nathan the prophet
new.note: Divine naming like C0038 (Name Sarah’s son Isaac); this translation renders the name Idedi. The sender could be read as David.

new.title: Amnon asks David to send Tamar to bake for him
new.speaker: Amnon
new.note: Amnon voices the request Jonadab scripted (ot-2-samuel-v13-5).

new.title: David sends Tamar to prepare food for Amnon
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Royal order sent to Tamar’s house: ‘Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare food for him.’

new.title: Tamar begs Amnon not to send her away
new.speaker: Tamar
new.note: Second plea, distinct from ot-2-samuel-v13-12; it echoes the violator’s duty not to send her away (C1141, Deuteronomy 22:29).

new.title: Absalom invites the king and asks that Amnon attend his shearing
new.speaker: Absalom
new.note: Repeated requests (13:24, 26) and the king’s ‘Please do not let us all go’ (13:25); leads to ot-2-samuel-v13-28.

new.title: The Tekoite woman asks David to swear to protect her son
new.speaker: the woman of Tekoa
new.note: Her request between ot-2-samuel-v14-10 and v14-12; David answers with an oath that not a hair of her son will fall.

new.title: The woman of Tekoa presses David to bring back his banished son
new.speaker: the woman of Tekoa
new.note: The point of Joab’s scripted appeal (ot-2-samuel-v14-2), grounded in the saying that we all die like water spilled on the ground.

new.title: David asks the woman of Tekoa to hide nothing from him
new.speaker: King David
new.note: She then admits ‘Joab commanded me’, recalling the order already recorded at ot-2-samuel-v14-2. 14:16 needs nothing.

new.title: David summons Absalom and receives him with a kiss
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Reported summons ending Absalom’s exclusion (ot-2-samuel-v14-24); summonses are recorded elsewhere, e.g. ot-1-kings-v1-32.

new.title: Absalom asks David’s leave to go to Hebron to pay his vow
new.speaker: Absalom
new.note: The request that ot-2-samuel-v15-9 grants; a pretext for the revolt. 15:5 is narrative.

new.title: Absalom sends agents to proclaim him king at the trumpet signal
new.speaker: Absalom
new.recipient: his secret agents in all Israel’s tribes
new.note: ‘When you hear the horn’s sound, say, King Absalom has begun to reign in Hebron!’ The order that launches the revolt.

new.title: Absalom summons Ahithophel, David’s counselor, from his city
new.speaker: Absalom
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported summons during the Hebron sacrifices; Ahithophel’s defection prompts David’s prayer (15:31) and Hushai’s mission (15:34).

new.title: David leaves ten concubines to keep the palace
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Outside candidate list. Reported assignment that sets up Absalom’s act (16:21–22) and their later seclusion (20:3).

new.title: Ittai swears to stay with David in life or death
new.speaker: Ittai the Gittite
new.note: Oath refusing David’s order to turn back (ot-2-samuel-v15-19, v15-20); compare Ruth’s pledge (ot-ruth-v1-16). David lets him cross (15:22).

new.title: David sends Zadok back with the priests’ sons to bring him word
new.speaker: King David
new.recipient: Zadok the priest, with Ahimaaz and Jonathan
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Sets up the courier line that ot-2-samuel-v15-36 relies on; distinct from returning the ark (ot-2-samuel-v15-25).

new.title: David awards Ziba everything that belonged to Mephibosheth
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Royal ruling on Ziba’s report (16:3), overturning AUD-10-9-9; later revised by first-pass P00802 (2 Samuel 19:30).

new.title: Absalom asks Ahithophel and his advisers for counsel
new.speaker: Absalom
new.note: Request answered by ot-2-samuel-v16-21; compare ot-2-samuel-v17-5, where Absalom consults Hushai.

new.title: Ahithophel advises Absalom to let him pursue David by night
new.speaker: Ahithophel
new.note: Ahithophel’s second counsel (his first is ot-2-samuel-v16-21); approved in 17:4 before Hushai is consulted.

new.title: Hushai counsels Absalom to muster all Israel before attacking David
new.speaker: Hushai the Archite
new.recipient: Absalom and the elders of Israel
new.note: Candidate 17:14 records the adoption of this counsel; 17:7–13 were not flagged as candidates and have no record.

new.title: Ahithophel sets his house in order before taking his life
new.speaker: Ahithophel
new.note: Reported charge (‘He gave instructions to his household’); its content is not stated.

new.title: Absalom appoints Amasa over the army in Joab’s place
new.speaker: Absalom
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported appointment; David later promises Amasa the same command (ot-2-samuel-v19-14).

new.title: David appoints commanders and sends out the army in three divisions
new.speaker: King David
new.recipient: his people; Joab, Abishai and Ittai
new.note: Officers of thousands and hundreds appointed, thirds under three commanders; the troops’ reply is ot-2-samuel-v18-3, his order on Absalom AUD-10-18-5.

new.title: Israel’s tribes urge one another to bring King David back
new.speaker: the people throughout Israel’s tribes
new.note: Appeal in question form (‘Why are you silent now about bringing the king back?’, 19:11 context); it prompts ot-2-samuel-v19-12.

new.title: Mephibosheth recalls ordering his servant to saddle his donkey
new.speaker: Mephibosheth
new.note: Reported order within his defence, comparable to ot-2-samuel-v1-9 (a reported request).

new.title: David orders Mephibosheth and Ziba to divide the land
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Royal ruling dividing Saul’s estate (compare AUD-10-9-9); Mephibosheth’s reply is ot-2-samuel-v19-31.

new.title: David invites Barzillai to cross over and live with him in Jerusalem
new.speaker: King David
new.note: The invitation that Barzillai declines in ot-2-samuel-v19-38.

new.title: Sheba son of Bichri calls Israel to desert David for their tents
new.speaker: Sheba son of Bichri
new.note: Rebel summons obeyed in 20:2; same cry as first-pass P00853 (1 Kings 12:16) but a different speaker and occasion.

new.title: David orders Amasa to summon Judah’s men within three days
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Explicit royal order; 20:5 notes Amasa’s delay, which prompts ot-2-samuel-v20-6.

new.title: Joab’s young man calls all loyal to David to follow Joab
new.speaker: one of Joab’s young men
new.note: Rallying call after Amasa’s murder; the men follow Joab once the body is moved (20:12–13).

new.title: Abel’s wise woman pleads with Joab to spare the city
new.speaker: the wise woman of Abel
new.note: Plea in question form (‘Why drown the Lord’s inheritance?’) citing Abel’s proverbial wisdom; Joab’s terms follow in ot-2-samuel-v20-21.

new.title: David has Saul’s and Jonathan’s bones buried in Kish’s tomb
new.speaker: King David
new.recipient: those who carried out the burial
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Reported order: ‘They did everything the king commanded’ (21:14), including the bones of the seven executed; then God heeded the land.

new.title: David longs for Bethlehem’s water, and three warriors fetch it
new.speaker: David
new.note: Indirect request (‘Who will give me water to drink?’); David pours the water out to the Lord. Parallel 1 Chronicles 11:17–19 unrecorded.

new.title: David appoints Benaiah to attend him and receive his orders
new.speaker: King David
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported appointment within the heroes list; parallel 1 Chronicles 11:25 is unrecorded.

new.title: Bathsheba urges David to declare Solomon his successor
new.speaker: Bathsheba
new.note: Carries out ot-1-kings-v1-12; 1:20 asks the king to tell Israel who will sit on his throne.

new.title: Nathan asks David whether he decreed Adonijah’s succession
new.speaker: Nathan the prophet
new.note: Appeal in question form completing the plan in ot-1-kings-v1-12; compare ot-1-chronicles-v21-3. 1:21 belongs with Bathsheba’s plea.

new.title: Zadok anoints Solomon king at Gihon
new.speaker: Zadok the priest
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Carries out David’s appointment (AUD-11-1-34); anointings are first-pass Commissions elsewhere (P00689, P00925). Jonathan reports it in 1:43–45.

new.title: Solomon spares Adonijah on condition of his good conduct
new.speaker: King Solomon
new.note: Conditional royal ruling answering ot-1-kings-v1-51, before ot-1-kings-v1-53 sends Adonijah home.

new.title: Adonijah asks Bathsheba to request Abishag from Solomon as his wife
new.speaker: Adonijah
new.note: The request itself; ot-1-kings-v2-16 (Study Context) covers only his asking to be heard.

new.title: Solomon condemns Adonijah and sends Benaiah to execute him
new.speaker: King Solomon
new.note: Sworn sentence (2:24) and reported order (context verse 2:25); no record between ot-1-kings-v2-22 and v2-26.

new.title: Solomon puts Benaiah over the army and Zadok in Abiathar’s place
new.speaker: King Solomon
new.recipient: Benaiah son of Jehoiada; Zadok the priest
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Verse 35 only, not 35a–o. Reported appointments after Joab’s death and Abiathar’s banishment; compare first-pass P00993 (1 Chronicles 29:22).

new.title: Solomon orders Benaiah to execute Shimei
new.speaker: King Solomon
new.note: Context verse beside candidate 2:45 (a blessing, needs nothing); the reported order ‘King Solomon commanded Benaiah’ has no record.

new.title: Hiram sends his attendants to anoint Solomon in David’s place
new.speaker: Hiram king of Tyre
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Greek-based reading ‘to anoint Solomon’: an embassy with a stated charge; compare first-pass P00771 (David’s envoys to Hanun).

new.title: Solomon levies Israelite workers for Lebanon and sets overseers over the works
new.speaker: King Solomon
new.recipient: the levy from all Israel, under Adoniram
new.note: Thirty thousand in monthly shifts (5:27 context). Parallel 2 Chronicles 2:16–17 is first-pass P00996; add 1 Kings 2:35h (3,600 overseers).

new.title: Solomon commands great costly stones brought for the temple’s foundation
new.speaker: King Solomon
new.note: Reported order (‘the king commanded’); Solomon’s and Hiram’s men hew and lay the stones (6:1b). 1 Kings 6 has no records.

new.title: Solomon appoints Jeroboam over the forced labour of Joseph’s house
new.speaker: King Solomon
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported appointment to office; precedes Ahijah’s oracle (ot-1-kings-v11-31).

new.title: The Lord through Ahijah appoints Jeroboam king on condition of obedience
new.speaker: the Lord through Ahijah
new.note: ‘You shall be king over Israel… If you keep all I command you’; compare AUD-10-5-2. 11:32 and 11:35 are prediction.

new.title: Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon’s heavy yoke
new.speaker: the people of Israel
new.note: Parallels 2 Chronicles 10:4 and 1 Kings 12:24p, both unrecorded; Rehoboam’s reply is ot-1-kings-v12-5.

new.title: The elders advise Rehoboam to serve the people and speak kindly
new.speaker: the elders who had served Solomon
new.note: Counsel to a ruler, like torah-exodus-18-13 (Jethro). Parallel 2 Chronicles 10:7 unrecorded; ot-1-kings-v12-24q records only the summons.

new.title: Rehoboam answers Israel harshly, promising a heavier yoke and scorpions
new.speaker: King Rehoboam
new.note: Royal answer enacting the young men’s counsel (first-pass P00852); parallel 2 Chronicles 10:13–14 is also unrecorded (outside candidate list).

new.title: Israel rejects David’s house and calls its men to their tents
new.speaker: the people of Israel
new.note: Same cry at 2 Samuel 20:1, 2 Chronicles 10:16 and 1 Kings 12:24t, none of them recorded.

new.title: Rehoboam sends Adoniram, overseer of the levy, to Israel
new.speaker: King Rehoboam
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported sending; Israel stones him. Parallel 2 Chronicles 10:18 is unrecorded.

new.title: Israel’s assembly summons Jeroboam and makes him king
new.speaker: all Israel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Context verse beside candidate 12:21; the people’s appointment of a king has no record.

new.title: Rehoboam musters Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel’s house
new.speaker: King Rehoboam
new.recipient: the assembly of Judah and Benjamin
new.note: Parallels 2 Chronicles 11:1 and 1 Kings 12:24x, both unrecorded; countermanded by ot-1-kings-v12-23.

new.title: Jeroboam asks the man of God to pray for his withered hand
new.speaker: King Jeroboam
new.recipient: the man of God from Judah
new.note: A request to a man to intercede, like ot-1-samuel-v7-8. 13:8 (his refusal) needs nothing beyond ot-1-kings-v13-9.

new.title: The old prophet tells his sons to saddle his donkey
new.speaker: the old prophet of Bethel
new.note: Household order before he overtakes the man of God; comparable orders are recorded at ot-2-kings-v4-24.

new.title: The old prophet asks to be buried beside the man of God
new.speaker: the old prophet of Bethel
new.note: Burial instruction to his sons, comparable to ot-genesis-v47-29 (Jacob’s burial request).

new.title: Asa orders all Judah to carry off Ramah’s stones and timber
new.speaker: King Asa
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported royal proclamation; parallel 2 Chronicles 16:6 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Israel’s army makes its commander Omri king in the camp
new.speaker: the people in Israel’s camp
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The people’s appointment of a king, like first-pass P00854 (1 Kings 12:20). 1 Kings 16 has no records.

new.title: Israel’s king proposes sending his men with Jehoshaphat’s on the ship
new.speaker: the king of Israel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Proposal Jehoshaphat refuses; the only form of this exchange here, since this text lacks the parallel at English 1 Kings 22:49.

new.title: Elijah calls Israel to stop wavering and follow the true God
new.speaker: Elijah
new.note: ‘How long will you limp on both your knees? If the Lord is God, follow Him’; no record between 18:19 and 18:23.

new.title: Elijah tells Baal’s prophets to withdraw so he can offer
new.speaker: Elijah
new.note: Direction found in the Greek text (‘Move away now’); no record between ot-1-kings-v18-27 and v18-30.

new.title: The Lord tells Elijah to go out and stand on the mountain
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Direct order at Horeb before the wind, earthquake, fire and gentle breeze; no record in 19:9-14.

new.title: The Syrian king demands Ahab’s silver, gold, wives and children
new.speaker: the son of Ader (Ben-hadad), king of Syria, through messengers
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Demand and threat to search the houses (21:5-6) are unrecorded; only Ahab's refusal (21:9) has a record.

new.title: Ben-hadad’s envoys in sackcloth beg Ahab to spare his life
