new.speaker: the son of Ader (Ben-hadad), through his attendants
new.note: Request distinct from the proposal at 21:31 and Ahab's reply at 21:33.

new.title: Ben-hadad offers terms and Ahab releases him under a treaty
new.speaker: the son of Ader (Ben-hadad) and Ahab
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Treaty terms: cities restored and markets in Damascus; condemned by the prophet at 21:42.

new.title: A prophet, by the Lord’s word, asks his companions to strike him
new.speaker: one of the sons of the prophets, by the Lord's word
new.note: The man who refuses is killed by a lion for not listening to the Lord's voice (21:36).

new.title: Jehoshaphat asks Ahab to inquire of the Lord first
new.speaker: Jehoshaphat king of Judah
new.note: Parallel 2 Chronicles 18:4 is also unrecorded.

new.title: The messenger urges Micaiah to speak favourably like the other prophets
new.speaker: the messenger sent to call Micaiah
new.note: Parallel 2 Chronicles 18:12 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Ahab adjures Micaiah to speak only the truth in the Lord’s name
new.speaker: Ahab king of Israel
new.note: An adjuration framed as a question; parallel 2 Chronicles 18:15 is also unrecorded.

new.title: The army herald sends every man home after Ahab’s death
new.speaker: the army herald
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list.

new.title: The third captain begs Elijah to spare his life and his men
new.speaker: the third captain of fifty
new.note: Contrasts with the captains' demands recorded at 1:9 and 1:11.

new.title: Elijah asks Elisha to stay behind at each stage of the journey
new.speaker: Elijah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Three requests (Bethel, Jericho, Jordan), each refused with Elisha's oath.

new.title: Elisha tells the sons of the prophets to keep silent
new.speaker: Elisha
new.recipient: the sons of the prophets at Bethel and Jericho
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

new.title: Jehoram asks Jehoshaphat to join his campaign against Moab
new.speaker: Jehoram king of Israel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Alliance request in question form, with the route agreed; similar requests at 1 Kings 22:4 and 2 Chronicles 18:3 are unrecorded.

new.title: Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet of the Lord to inquire through
new.speaker: Jehoshaphat king of Judah
new.recipient: the king of Israel and his attendants
new.note: Request in question form; an attendant names Elisha and the kings go to him (ot-2-kings-v3-13). Compare first-pass P00884 (1 Kings 22:5).

new.title: Moab’s troops rally one another to plunder the allied camp
new.speaker: the Moabite troops
new.note: Battle cry ‘Now, Moab, to the spoils!’ after mistaking the red water for blood; they are routed (3:24).

new.title: The Shunammite proposes building and furnishing a room for Elisha
new.speaker: the Shunammite woman
new.note: Hospitality to the man of God: room with bed, table, stool and lampstand.

new.title: Elisha sends Gehazi to ask the Shunammite what favour she wants
new.speaker: Elisha

new.title: The Shunammite asks her husband for a servant and donkey
new.speaker: the Shunammite woman
new.note: Request to reach the man of God after her son's death; distinct from her order to the attendant (4:24).

new.title: Elisha sends Gehazi running to ask after the Shunammite’s family
new.speaker: Elisha

new.title: The captive girl says Naaman should go to Samaria’s prophet
new.speaker: the young Israelite captive
new.note: Counsel in wish form, relayed to Naaman (5:4); it leads to ot-2-kings-v5-5.

new.title: Elisha asks Israel’s king to send Naaman to him
new.speaker: Elisha
new.note: 'Let him know that there is a prophet in Israel.'

new.title: Naaman’s servants urge him to bathe as the prophet said
new.speaker: Naaman's attendants
new.note: Counsel that turns Naaman back to obey Elisha's word (5:14).

new.title: Naaman asks for Israelite earth and pardon to worship the Lord
new.speaker: Naaman
new.note: Two mule-loads of earth to sacrifice to the Lord alone; pardon for bowing in Remman's house.

new.title: Gehazi falsely asks Naaman for silver and robes in Elisha’s name
new.speaker: Gehazi
new.note: Lying request punished with leprosy (5:26-27); the gift itself is only a Study Context record (5:23).

new.title: An attendant proposes sending horsemen to scout the abandoned camp
new.speaker: one of the king's attendants
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Proposal acted on by the king's commission at 7:14.

new.title: The king asks Gehazi to recount Elisha’s great deeds
new.speaker: the king of Israel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request for an account; leads to the restoration ordered at 8:6.

new.title: Jehu’s fellow officers press him to tell what the prophet said
new.speaker: the commanders with Jehu
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request that leads to Jehu's acclamation as king (9:13).

new.title: Jehu orders that no one slip out to warn Jezreel
new.speaker: Jehu
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

new.title: Joram orders his chariot yoked to go and meet Jehu
new.speaker: Joram king of Israel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list.

new.title: Jehu orders Jezebel buried because she is a king’s daughter
new.speaker: Jehu
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

new.title: Jehu’s letter dares Samaria’s leaders to crown Ahab’s son and fight
new.speaker: Jehu, by letter
new.recipient: the rulers, elders and guardians in Samaria
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

new.title: Jehu’s second letter orders the heads of Ahab’s seventy sons
new.speaker: Jehu, by letter
new.recipient: the rulers, elders and guardians in Samaria
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Order carried out in 10:7; the piling of the heads (10:8) is recorded separately.

new.title: Jehoiada crowns and anoints the boy Joash as king
new.speaker: Jehoiada the priest
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list. AUD-14-23-3 records only Jehoiada's call; parallel 2 Chronicles 23:11 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Jehoiada covenants king and people to be the Lord’s people
new.speaker: Jehoiada the priest
new.note: Covenant between the Lord, king and people; parallel 2 Chronicles 23:16 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Judah’s people make the sixteen-year-old Azariah king
new.speaker: all the people of Judah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list: the people’s appointment after Amaziah’s murder (14:19); parallel 2 Chronicles 26:1. Compare first-pass P00854.

new.title: Ahaz sends Uriah the Damascus altar’s design to copy
new.speaker: King Ahaz
new.note: Outside candidate list. Reported building instruction carried out exactly (16:11); precedes the order recorded at 16:15.

new.title: Hezekiah asks Sennacherib to withdraw and accepts a heavy tribute
new.speaker: Hezekiah king of Judah, through messengers
new.recipient: Sennacherib king of Assyria at Lachish
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Withdraw from me; whatever you impose I will bear'; Assyria imposes 300 talents of silver and 30 of gold.

new.title: Hezekiah commands Judah to worship only before the Jerusalem altar
new.speaker: Hezekiah, as quoted by the Assyrian envoy
new.note: Recalled royal decree centralising worship; parallels Isaiah 36:7 and 2 Chronicles 32:12 are also unrecorded.

new.title: The Assyrian envoy dares Judah to wager horses with Assyria
new.speaker: Rabshakeh (Rhapsakes), the Assyrian envoy
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Taunting proposal; parallel Isaiah 36:8 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Hezekiah asks for a sign and chooses the shadow’s return
new.speaker: Hezekiah king of Judah
new.note: Request addressed to Isaiah, not a prayer; parallel Isaiah 38:22 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Manasseh appoints a charmer and mediums
new.speaker: King Manasseh
new.note: Wicked appointment among his sins, comparable to AUD-11-13-33 (Jeroboam’s priests); contrary to C1074. Parallel 2 Chronicles 33:6 unrecorded.

new.title: The people of the land make Josiah king after Amon’s murder
new.speaker: the people of the land
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; parallel 2 Chronicles 33:25. Compare first-pass P00854 (Israel makes Jeroboam king).

new.title: Josiah gathers Judah’s elders and reads the covenant book to all
new.speaker: King Josiah
new.recipient: the elders of Judah and Jerusalem; all the people
new.note: Reported summons and public reading (23:2 context) before the covenant, first-pass P00953 (23:3); parallel 2 Chronicles 34:29–30 unrecorded.

new.title: Josiah and the people covenant to keep the Lord’s commandments
new.speaker: King Josiah
new.recipient: the people of Judah and Jerusalem
new.note: Covenant to follow the Lord and keep the book's words; parallel 2 Chronicles 34:31-32 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Josiah orders the priests to remove Baal’s vessels from the temple
new.speaker: King Josiah
new.recipient: Hilkiah the high priest, the second priests and the doorkeepers
new.note: Outside candidate list: explicit reported order opening Josiah's reform.

new.title: The people of the land anoint Jehoahaz and make him king
new.speaker: the people of the land
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list: anointing by the people, like first-pass P00925 and P00963; parallel 2 Chronicles 36:1.

new.title: Pharaoh Neco makes Eliakim king and renames him Jehoiakim
new.speaker: Pharaoh Neco
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse): vassal king installed and renamed; compare first-pass P00956. Parallel 2 Chronicles 36:4.

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah over the people left in Judah
new.speaker: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; Gedaliah's own counsel (25:24) is already recorded.

new.title: David appoints Levites over the singing before the tent
new.speaker: King David
new.recipient: the Levitical singers (Heman, Asaph, Ethan and their kin)
new.note: Outside candidate list (6:16 was context). Reported appointment of singers; chapter has no records.

new.title: David and Samuel appoint the gatekeepers to their trusted office
new.speaker: David and Samuel the seer
new.note: Reported appointment of Levites to guard the gates of the Lord's house.

new.title: David rules that only the Levites may carry God’s ark
new.speaker: David
new.note: Outside candidate list. Royal ruling restating Deuteronomy 10:8 (AUD-05-10-8).

new.title: David has the Levite chiefs appoint singers and musicians for the ark
new.speaker: David
new.note: Order (15:16) and the appointments made under it (15:17-24); not covered by 15:12-15.

new.title: The people are to answer Amen and praise the Lord
new.speaker: David's psalm of thanksgiving
new.note: Liturgical response after the doxology; Greek Psalm 105:48 parallel is also unrecorded.

new.title: David leaves Asaph at the ark and Zadok’s priests at Gibeon
new.speaker: David
new.recipient: Asaph, Obed-edom and the gatekeepers; Zadok and the priests; Heman and Jeduthun
new.note: Continual ministry at both sites, burnt offerings 'as written in the Lord's law'; AUD-13-16-4 covers only 16:4-7.

new.title: David conscripts resident foreigners as stonecutters for the temple
new.speaker: David
new.note: Reported order and appointment of quarrymen.

new.title: David numbers the Levites, assigns their offices and divides them
new.speaker: David
new.note: Outside candidate list: supervisors, scribes and judges, gatekeepers, musicians; courses by Levi's sons.

new.title: David, Zadok and Ahimelech divide the priests by lot into courses
new.speaker: David, with Zadok and Ahimelech
new.note: Outside candidate list: twenty-four courses, 'according to their ordinance through Aaron, as the Lord commanded' (24:19).

new.title: David appoints the families of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun as temple singers
new.speaker: King David and the army commanders
new.recipient: the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun
new.note: Outside candidate list: singers set apart to prophesy with instruments; duties assigned by lot (25:8).

new.title: The gatekeepers’ divisions receive their gates by lot
new.speaker: David's arrangement for the Levites
new.note: Outside candidate list: duty stations assigned by lot, as for priests (24:5) and singers (25:8).

new.title: David assigns Levites as officers and judges for outside duties
new.speaker: King David
new.note: Covers P00988 (26:32): appointed 'for every ordinance of the Lord and word of the king.'

new.title: Israel’s twelve army divisions serve the king in monthly turns
new.speaker: King David’s administration
new.recipient: the divisions of Israel and their officers
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list: rotation of 24,000 a month (27:2–15 name the commanders), like AUD-11-4-7; 1 Chronicles 27 has no records.

new.title: David declares the Lord chose Solomon to sit on Israel’s throne
new.speaker: the Lord, as declared by David
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Throne designation; 28:6 (temple builder) is already linked to ot-1-chronicles-v28-10.

new.title: David gives Solomon the Lord-given written pattern for the temple
new.speaker: David, from the Lord's hand
new.note: Outside candidate list: plan of courts, chambers, courses, vessels by weight, cherubim chariot (28:19).

new.title: David appeals to the assembly to give willingly for the temple
new.speaker: King David
new.note: 'Who is eager to fill his hands today for the Lord?' (29:5); answered by freewill gifts (29:6-9).

new.title: Israel anoints Solomon king again and Zadok as priest
new.speaker: the assembly of Israel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list: anointing 'for the Lord' as king and for the priesthood.

new.title: Hiram sends the skilled craftsman Huram-abi to work for Solomon
new.speaker: Hiram (Chiram) king of Tyre
new.note: Answer to Solomon's request (2:6-7); the craftsman is to work with Solomon's and David's skilled men.

new.title: Humble yourselves, pray and turn, and the Lord will heal the land
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Conditional promise that directs repentance; compare Wisdom record AUD-14-15-1. No record in 2 Chronicles 7.

new.title: Solomon conscripts the Canaanite remnant but makes no Israelite a slave
new.speaker: King Solomon
new.recipient: the remaining Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites; Israel
new.note: Outside candidate list: royal labour policy echoing C1096 and C0732; Greek parallel 1 Kings 10:22a–c, also unrecorded, belongs as Additional Scripture.

new.title: Solomon rules his Egyptian wife may not live in David’s city
new.speaker: Solomon
new.note: Ruling grounded in the holiness of places the ark entered.

new.title: Solomon stations the priestly and Levitical divisions as David commanded
new.speaker: Solomon, following David's ordinance
new.note: Outside candidate list: courses, watches and gates assigned; 'they did not transgress the king's commands' (8:15).

new.title: Happy are those who stand near wisdom and keep hearing it
new.speaker: the queen of Sheba
new.note: Beatitude in praise of Solomon's servants; parallel 1 Kings 10:8 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Rehoboam appoints Abijah chief among his brothers, intending him as king
new.speaker: King Rehoboam
new.note: Reported appointment of an heir; 2 Chronicles 11 has records only at 11:3–4.

new.title: Abijah warns Israel that fighting the Lord will not prosper
new.speaker: King Abijah
new.note: Climax of the speech opened at ot-2-chronicles-v13-4 (Study Context): a warning not to fight ‘the Lord, our fathers’ God’.

new.title: Asa commands Judah to seek the Lord and keep the law
new.speaker: King Asa
new.note: Reported royal command; 14:2 is narrative of the reform.

new.title: Asa’s assembly covenants to seek the Lord on pain of death
new.speaker: King Asa and the assembly
new.recipient: Judah, Benjamin and the Israelites living among them
new.note: Covenant stipulation with death penalty (15:13), sworn with trumpets (15:14); AUD-14-15-1 covers only 15:1–7.

new.title: Hanani rebukes Asa for relying on Syria’s king instead of the Lord
new.speaker: Anani (Hanani) the prophet
new.note: 16:8–9 outside candidate list; 16:9 gives the maxim: the Lord’s eyes range the earth to strengthen every heart whole toward Him.

new.title: Jehoshaphat garrisons Judah’s fortified cities and appoints leaders
new.speaker: King Jehoshaphat
new.note: Reported appointments in Judah and the Ephraimite cities Asa took; his teaching commission is first-pass P01012 (17:7–9).

new.title: Jehoshaphat sends officials, Levites and priests to teach the law
new.speaker: King Jehoshaphat
new.recipient: his officials, the Levites and the priests
new.note: Adjacent gap, not a flagged candidate (17:5 itself is narrative); chapter 17 has no records.

new.title: Jehu rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping the wicked and loving the Lord’s enemies
new.speaker: Jehu son of Anani the prophet
new.note: Prophetic rebuke implying a prohibition on alliance with the wicked; rhetorical-question form, hence low.

new.title: Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast throughout Judah
new.speaker: King Jehoshaphat
new.note: Outside candidate list (20:3). Royal fast proclamation, like ot-jonah-v3-7 and first-pass P01193 (Ezra 8:21).

new.title: Jehu orders a search for Ahaziah, who is caught and killed
new.speaker: Jehu
new.note: Reported order. Kings parallel 2 Kings 9:27 ('strike him too') is also unrecorded.

new.title: The Lord’s prophets and Azarias son of Jehoiada call Judah back
new.speaker: the Lord through his prophets and Azarias son of Jehoiada
new.note: Prophets sent 'to turn them back' (24:19) and Azarias’s rebuke for transgressing the commandments; cf. ot-2-kings-v17-13.

new.title: Joash orders Azarias son of Jehoiada stoned in the temple court
new.speaker: King Joash
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Reported royal order in the context verse; 24:22 dying words are an appeal to God, out of scope.

new.title: Hezekiah orders the priests to offer sin offerings for all Israel
new.speaker: King Hezekiah
new.note: 29:21 order to go up to the altar; 29:24 royal ruling that the offerings are for all Israel.

new.title: Hezekiah orders the burnt offering begun with song and trumpets
new.speaker: King Hezekiah
new.note: Reported order; follows the instrument arrangements of AUD-14-29-25 (29:25–26), which could instead be extended.

new.title: Hezekiah tells the Levites to sing praise in David’s and Asaph’s words
new.speaker: King Hezekiah and the rulers
new.note: Reported call to worship using the words of David and Asaph the prophet.

new.title: Hezekiah’s assembly decrees a second-month Passover for all Israel
new.speaker: King Hezekiah, his rulers and the assembly in Jerusalem
new.recipient: all Israel, from Beersabee to Dan
new.note: Royal decree behind the Passover letters (30:6–9 records); compare the second-month Passover law C0841 (Numbers 9:10–11).

new.title: The assembly resolves to keep the feast seven more days
new.speaker: the whole assembly in Jerusalem
new.note: Communal festival decision, like first-pass P01033 (30:2–5).

new.title: Hezekiah organizes the priestly and Levitical divisions and funds the offerings
new.speaker: King Hezekiah
new.note: 31:2 assigns divisions and duties; 31:3 sets the king’s portion for daily, Sabbath and festival burnt offerings.

new.title: Hezekiah orders storerooms prepared in the temple for the offerings
new.speaker: King Hezekiah

new.title: Hezekiah and Azarias appoint Levites to oversee and distribute the offerings
new.speaker: King Hezekiah and Azarias, leader of the Lord’s house
new.recipient: Chonenias, Semei, Kore and the Levite overseers
new.note: 31:13 'as King Hezekiah and Azarias commanded'; 31:12 and 31:14–15 outside candidate list.

new.title: Hezekiah appoints commanders of war over the people
new.speaker: King Hezekiah
new.note: He then gathers them for the 32:7–8 speech (ot-2-chronicles-v32-7).

new.title: Manasseh commands Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel
new.speaker: King Manasseh, after his repentance
new.note: Adjacent gap, not a flagged candidate; chapter 33 has no records. Same kind as Asa’s command (14:3).

new.title: Josiah stations the priests at their duties and strengthens them
new.speaker: King Josiah
new.note: Outside candidate list (35:2, never batched); precedes his charge to the Levites (ot-2-chronicles-v35-3).

new.title: Laments for Josiah are made an ordinance in Israel
new.speaker: the male and female rulers of Judah
new.note: Customary ordinance of mourning, like first-pass P00624 (Judges 11:39–40).

new.title: Pharaoh imposes tribute, which Jehoiakim exacts from the land by assessment
new.speaker: Pharaoh Neco
new.note: 36:3 outside candidate list (never batched); 36:4a 'at Pharaoh’s command'. 2 Kings 23:33–35 also unrecorded.

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar makes Zedekiah king and binds him by oath
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Also deports Jechonias (36:10). 2 Kings 24:17 unrecorded; the broken oath is treated in AUD-30-17-11 (Ezekiel 17).

new.title: Alexander divides his kingdom among his officers before his death
new.speaker: Alexander the Macedonian
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Authority handed on in narrative; include only if the catalogue keeps such historical transfers.

new.title: Antiochus appoints overseers and orders every Judean town to sacrifice
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.recipient: his kingdom and the towns of Judah
new.note: Enforcement clause after the decree records for 1:41–50: overseers appointed and sacrifice ordered city by city.

new.title: The king’s decree executes keepers of the covenant book and circumcisers
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes, through his officers
new.note: Law books burned; owning one or keeping the law is capital (1:57), applying ot-1-maccabees-v1-48 and v1-49.

new.title: Mattathias refuses the king’s decree and vows to keep the covenant
new.speaker: Mattathias
new.note: Declared refusal to obey the king against the law; compare A051 (Acts 5:29) and AUD-16-6-21 (Eleazar).

new.title: Victory comes from Heaven, not from the size of an army
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Declarative saying in Judas’s speech; the following command not to fear is recorded separately (3:22).

new.title: Antiochus pays his army a year’s wages and orders it ready
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.note: Reported royal order.

new.title: Antiochus leaves Lysias regent and orders him to destroy Judea
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.note: Regency and guardianship of the heir (3:32–33) with orders to crush Judea and resettle its land (3:34–36).

new.title: Lysias sends Ptolemy, Nicanor and Gorgias to destroy Judah
new.speaker: Lysias
new.recipient: Ptolemy son of Dorymenes, Nicanor and Gorgias
new.note: Carries out the king’s command; parallel account 2 Maccabees 8:8–9 (also proposed under P01151).

new.title: Better to die in battle than to watch the nation’s ruin
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: 'Better… than' saying with submission to Heaven’s will after the 3:58 command; could instead extend ot-1-maccabees-v3-58.

new.title: Judas orders men to fight the citadel garrison during the cleansing
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus

new.title: Judas chooses blameless priests to cleanse the holy places
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.recipient: blameless priests devoted to the law
new.note: Carries out the cleansing proposed in ot-1-maccabees-v4-36.

new.title: The priests store the defiled altar’s stones until a prophet decides
new.speaker: the chosen priests, with Judas
new.note: Ruling on the profaned altar (4:44–45 outside candidate list); new altar of whole stones 'according to the law' (4:47).

new.title: Judas urges his army to fight today for their brothers
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Battle exhortation at the relief of the besieged city (5:31–33).

new.title: Judas sends men to spy out Timothy’s camp
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Like ot-joshua-v2-1 (spies sent).

new.title: Judas asks Ephron for peaceful passage through its land
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request for passage in the context verse; Moses’s similar offer is only Study Context (ot-deuteronomy-v2-28), hence low.

new.title: Judas orders his company to encamp where they stand
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Reported order by proclamation before the assault on Ephron.

new.title: Dying Antiochus appoints Philip regent and guardian of his heir
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Appointment with diadem, robe and ring to bring up the heir to reign (recalled at 6:55).

new.title: Lysias makes the young Antiochus king and names him Eupator
new.speaker: Lysias
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Royal appointment that sets aside Antiochus’s choice of Philip as guardian.

new.title: Judas assembles the people to besiege the citadel in Jerusalem
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Reported summons without speech; record only if such musters are kept.

new.title: Renegade Israelites urge the king to act quickly against Judas
new.speaker: ungodly men from Israel who escaped the blockade
new.note: Petition for vengeance; also covers P01081 (6:27). Compare Alcimus’s similar petition (ot-1-maccabees-v7-7).

new.title: Antiochus Eupator breaks his oath and orders Zion’s wall torn down
new.speaker: King Antiochus Eupator
new.note: Reported order breaking the sworn peace of 6:60–61.

new.title: Demetrius sends Bacchides to take vengeance and confirms Alcimus as priest
new.speaker: King Demetrius
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Demetrius sends them again at 9:1 (Q04539); link that verse here.

new.title: Bacchides places the country under Alcimus with a supporting force
new.speaker: Bacchides
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (7:20).

new.title: Nicanor threatens to burn the temple unless Judas is handed over
new.speaker: Nicanor
new.recipient: the priests and elders on Mount Zion
new.note: Demand in the adjacent verse 7:35 (7:33 is narrative); compare 2 Maccabees 14:33.

new.title: Judas sends envoys to Rome to seek alliance and friendship
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 8:17–19 outside candidate list; 8:20 is their request to the senate. The treaty is AUD-15-8-24.

new.title: Rome warns Demetrius to stop oppressing its Jewish allies
new.speaker: the Roman Senate
new.note: Warning letter reported after the treaty (AUD-15-8-24, 8:24–30); could instead extend that record.

new.title: Bacchides appoints ungodly men as masters of the country
new.speaker: Bacchides
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Appointment by a hostile governor; 9:26 records its outworking.

new.title: Judas’s friends choose Jonathan to lead them in Judas’s place
new.speaker: all Judas’s friends
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The people commission a leader (9:30), accepted in 9:31; compare AUD-07-11-8 (Jephthah).

new.title: Jonathan sends John to ask the Nabateans to store their goods
new.speaker: Jonathan
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Sending with a request; the brother is named John in 9:36.

new.title: Alcimus orders the wall of the inner temple court demolished
new.speaker: Alcimus
new.note: Reported order 'tearing down the works of the prophets'; 9:55 records his being struck.

new.title: Bacchides secretly writes to his Judean allies to seize Jonathan
new.speaker: Bacchides
new.note: Acts on the plot recorded at ot-1-maccabees-v9-58.

new.title: Jonathan sends envoys to seek peace and the captives’ return
new.speaker: Jonathan
new.note: Reported request granted under oath (9:71–72); 9:70 sits in P01096’s context.

new.title: Demetrius authorizes Jonathan to raise an army and frees the hostages
new.speaker: King Demetrius, by letter
new.note: Grant of authority and order to hand over the hostages, read publicly in 10:7–9.

new.title: Jonathan orders Mount Zion’s walls rebuilt with four-foot stones
new.speaker: Jonathan
new.note: Reported order, with its execution.

new.title: Alexander appoints Jonathan high priest and the King’s Friend
new.speaker: King Alexander, by letter
new.note: Seleucid appointment to the high priesthood, taken up at the Festival of Booths (10:21).

new.title: Alexander summons Jonathan to meet him at Ptolemais
new.speaker: King Alexander, by letter
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported written summons.

new.title: Alexander orders Jonathan stripped of his garments and clothed in purple
new.speaker: King Alexander
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Distinct honour preceding the protection order (ot-1-maccabees-v10-63); could instead extend that record.

new.title: Alexander appoints Jonathan general and district governor
new.speaker: King Alexander
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Enrolled among the First Friends and given military and civil office.

new.title: Demetrius appoints Apollonius, governor of Coele-Syria, to lead his forces
new.speaker: King Demetrius
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: His challenge to Jonathan follows (first-pass P01105, 10:70–73).

new.title: Jonathan’s troops stand firm under the ambush as he commanded
new.speaker: Jonathan
new.note: Reported order; its wording is not given.

new.title: Alexander grants Jonathan a golden clasp and Ekron as an inheritance
new.speaker: King Alexander
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Royal grant, like the catalogue’s itemized Seleucid grants (e.g. ot-1-maccabees-v11-34).

new.title: Alexander orders his cities to welcome Ptolemy as his father-in-law
new.speaker: King Alexander
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported order mentioned in passing; 11:1 is narrative.

new.title: Demetrius orders Jonathan to stop the siege and come to Ptolemais
new.speaker: King Demetrius II, by letter
new.note: Reported written order in the context verse, defied in 11:23.

new.title: Jonathan orders the siege of the citadel to continue
new.speaker: Jonathan
new.note: Reported order; he then takes elders and priests to the king at personal risk.

new.title: Demetrius confirms Jonathan as high priest and ranks him among First Friends
new.speaker: King Demetrius
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (11:27, never batched).

new.title: Jonathan asks Demetrius to free Judea and the three districts from tribute
new.speaker: Jonathan
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (11:28, never batched); the king consents (11:29) and grants it in ot-1-maccabees-v11-34.

new.title: Jonathan asks Demetrius to remove the citadel garrison from Jerusalem
new.speaker: Jonathan
new.note: Reported request in the context verse, answered in 11:42–43.

new.title: Demetrius promises honours and asks Jonathan to send him troops
new.speaker: King Demetrius II
new.note: Royal request, met with three thousand men (11:44).

new.title: Antiochus VI confirms Jonathan as high priest and grants royal honours
new.speaker: the young King Antiochus, by letter
new.note: Confirms the high priesthood, appoints him over four districts, and grants purple and gold vessels.

new.title: Antiochus VI appoints Simon general from Tyre’s Ladder to Egypt
new.speaker: the young King Antiochus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Separate appointment in the context verse; could be combined with the 11:57–58 record.

new.title: Jonathan sends envoys to renew friendship with Rome and Sparta
new.speaker: Jonathan
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Embassy and letters; the envoys’ charge is restated in the Spartan letter (12:16–17).

new.title: Rome gives Jonathan’s envoys letters ordering safe escort home
new.speaker: the Roman council
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 12:4 outside candidate list. The embassy itself is first-pass P01111 (12:1–2), which could widen to 12:3.

new.title: Remember your brothers continually in prayers and sacrifices
new.speaker: Jonathan, the elders and the Jewish people
new.note: Maxim in the letter: 'as it is right and fitting to remember brothers'. The letter’s request is first-pass P01112.

new.title: Jonathan’s letter asks Sparta to receive his envoys and reply
new.speaker: Jonathan the high priest, with the elders and priests, by letter
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The letter of 12:6–18 has no record; its directives are the envoys’ charge (12:17) and the request for a reply (12:18).

new.title: Areus asks Onias to write and orders their shared property reported
new.speaker: Areus king of the Spartans
new.recipient: Onias the high priest; Areus’s envoys
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request (12:22) and 'We therefore command that they report to you' (12:23), declaring property shared.

new.title: Jonathan and the elders resolve to fortify Judea and isolate the citadel
new.speaker: Jonathan and the elders of the people
new.note: Council decision, like Asa’s fortification proposal (ot-2-chronicles-v14-6) and 1 Maccabees 4:36.

new.title: Tryphon orders his Friends and forces to obey Jonathan
new.speaker: Tryphon
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Deceptive honour leading to ot-1-maccabees-v12-45; could instead extend that record to 12:43–45.

new.title: Tryphon sends forces to destroy all Jonathan’s men in Galilee
new.speaker: Tryphon
new.note: Like AUD-15-16-17 (Ptolemy sends agents against John).

new.title: The people acclaim Simon their leader and pledge to obey him
new.speaker: the people gathered in Jerusalem
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Acclamation with a pledge of obedience; compare ot-joshua-v1-18 and AUD-07-11-8.

new.title: Simon sends Jonathan son of Absalom with a force to take Joppa
new.speaker: Simon

new.title: The citadel garrison urges Tryphon to come through the wilderness with food
new.speaker: those in the citadel
new.note: Reported request carried by envoys; 13:20 is narrative.

new.title: Simon sends envoys to Demetrius to seek remission for the country
new.speaker: Simon
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Demetrius’s reply is first-pass P01120 (13:36–39).

new.title: Demetrius II confirms Judea’s strongholds and remits its offences and levies
new.speaker: King Demetrius II, by letter
new.recipient: Simon, the elders and the nation of the Jews
new.note: Royal decree answering Simon’s embassy (13:34); the letter is otherwise unrecorded.

new.title: Demetrius II opens royal enrollment to Jews and declares peace
new.speaker: King Demetrius II, by letter
new.note: Separate grant in the same letter; followed by the removal of the nations’ yoke (13:41).

new.title: Simon decrees a yearly celebration of the citadel’s capture
new.speaker: Simon
new.note: Annual festival for the 23rd of the second month (13:51); compare ot-1-maccabees-v4-59.

new.title: Simon appoints his son John commander of all the forces
new.speaker: Simon
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Appointment of John as commander, residing at Gazara.

new.title: Arsaces sends a commander to capture Demetrius alive
new.speaker: Arsaces king of Persia and Media

new.title: Sparta resolves to honor the Jewish envoys and record their words
new.speaker: the rulers and people of Sparta, by letter
new.recipient: Simon the high priest and the Jews
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Foreign civic resolution quoted in a letter. 14:25 is a question leading to the recorded decree (14:41–49).

new.title: The decree forbids annulling Simon’s terms or rivaling his authority
new.speaker: the great assembly of priests, people, rulers and elders
new.note: Obedience; no contradicting him, convening without him, or wearing purple; penalty (14:45). Inside ot-1-maccabees-v14-41, whose title omits these.

new.title: Antiochus VII confirms past remissions and lets Judea mint its own coins
new.speaker: King Antiochus VII, by letter
new.recipient: Simon and the nation of the Jews
new.note: Chapter 15 has no records; 15:5 was not flagged. The coinage grant is a distinct royal privilege.

new.title: Antiochus VII declares Jerusalem free and remits all royal debts forever
new.speaker: King Antiochus VII, by letter
new.recipient: Simon and the nation of the Jews
new.note: Freedom of Jerusalem, retention of weapons and strongholds, perpetual remission; later annulled (15:27).

new.title: Rome directs kings and countries not to make war on the Jews
new.speaker: Lucius, consul of the Romans
new.recipient: King Ptolemy and the kings and countries of 15:22–23
new.note: Roman circular decree protecting Judea and forbidding alliance with its enemies.

new.title: Rome orders fugitives from Judea handed over to Simon for judgment
new.speaker: Lucius, consul of the Romans
new.note: Extradition clause: offenders to be punished 'according to their law'.

new.title: Antiochus VII demands Simon surrender the cities or pay a thousand talents
new.speaker: King Antiochus VII, through Athenobius
new.note: Ultimatum after annulling earlier grants (15:27); Simon’s reply follows in 15:33–35.

new.title: Antiochus VII appoints Cendebaeus to rebuild Kedron and make war on Judea
new.speaker: King Antiochus VII
new.note: 15:41 records the order carried out 'as the king had ordered him'; 15:40 is narrative.

new.title: Nehemiah orders the remaining water poured over the larger stones
new.speaker: Nehemiah
new.note: Further ritual order in the fire episode; the prayer (1:24–29) is out of scope; AUD-16-1-20 covers only 1:20–21.

new.title: Jeremiah orders the deportees to take some of the altar fire
new.speaker: Jeremiah the prophet, as found in the records
new.note: Reported order distinct from AUD-16-2-2 (remember the law, 2:2–3); could instead extend that record to 2:1–3.

new.title: The Jerusalem letter invites Egypt’s Jews to send for the gathered books
new.speaker: the Jews of Jerusalem and Judea, by letter
new.note: Offer of Judas’s collected writings (cf. Nehemiah’s library, 2:13); the 2:16 request to observe the days is recorded.

new.title: Heliodorus’s companions beg Onias to pray for his life
new.speaker: some of Heliodorus’s companions
new.note: Outside candidate list (3:31). Onias’s sacrifice and the angels’ charge follow (ot-2-maccabees-v3-33).

new.title: Heliodorus advises the king to send only an enemy to Jerusalem
new.speaker: Heliodorus
new.note: Ironic counsel bearing witness that God guards the temple (3:39); advisers’ counsel is usually Instruction.

new.title: Jason’s envoys ask that his gift for Heracles not fund sacrifice
new.speaker: the envoys Jason sent to Tyre
new.note: Jason sent the money for the sacrifice; the bearers’ scruple redirected it (4:20). 2 Maccabees 4 has no records.

new.title: Antiochus gives Menelaus, Jason’s envoy, the high priesthood by royal orders
new.speaker: Jason; King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.note: Jason sends Menelaus with the money (4:23); 4:24–25 outside candidate list (4:25 never batched).

new.title: Menelaus urges Andronicus to murder Onias
new.speaker: Menelaus
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Reported incitement to murder; chapter 4 has no records.

new.title: The elders’ council sends three men to accuse Menelaus
new.speaker: the council of elders

new.title: God chose the place for the nation, not the reverse
new.speaker: the narrator (the epitomist)
new.note: Outside candidate list (5:19–20). Teaches that the sanctuary shares the people’s sins and fortunes; cf. AUD-16-6-12.

new.title: Antiochus leaves Philip and Andronicus as overseers to afflict the people
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.recipient: Philip in Jerusalem and Andronicus at Gerizim
new.note: Appointment of oppressive governors after the temple’s plunder (5:21).

new.title: Antiochus sends Apollonius to slaughter Jerusalem’s men and sell the rest
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Reported order of massacre and enslavement; parallel 1 Maccabees 1:29–32 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Apollonius orders his troops to parade under arms on the Sabbath
new.speaker: Apollonius
new.note: Reported order exploiting the Sabbath rest, followed by the massacre (5:26).

new.title: Antiochus orders the first brother mutilated and fried before his family
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Reported orders of torture after the refusal in 7:2; compare the massacre order AUD-16-5-11.

new.title: The brothers and their mother urge one another to die nobly
new.speaker: the brothers and their mother
new.note: Mutual exhortation citing Moses’ song (Deuteronomy 32:36); 7:2 states their shared resolve.

new.title: The torturers demand the second brother eat pork or be dismembered
new.speaker: the king’s torturers
new.note: The compulsion of 7:1 is also unrecorded; first-pass P01144 covers the king’s orders in 7:3–5.

new.title: Better to die hoping in God’s promise of resurrection
new.speaker: the fourth brother
new.note: 'It is preferable…' saying; the judgment on the king is out of scope. 7:9 (P01145) is declaration only.

new.title: The mother urges her sons to hope in the Creator of life
new.speaker: the mother of the seven brothers
new.note: Her exhortation to each son; the later appeal to the youngest is ot-2-maccabees-v7-29.

new.title: Antiochus presses the youngest son and his mother to abandon the law
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.recipient: the youngest brother and his mother
new.note: Inducement with oaths, wealth and office to abandon ancestral ways; then he urges the mother to persuade him.

new.title: Obey the law given through Moses, not the king’s ordinance
new.speaker: the youngest brother
new.note: Principle of obeying God’s law over a ruler; compare A051 (Acts 5:29). 7:31 is judgment.

new.title: The youngest son warns Antiochus not to exalt himself against Heaven’s children
new.speaker: the youngest brother
new.note: Warning like the sixth brother’s (ot-2-maccabees-v7-18); 7:35–36 announce judgment.

new.title: Nicanor invites the coastal cities to buy Jewish captives
new.speaker: Nicanor
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Reported offer of ninety bodies for a talent to pay Rome’s tribute; compare 1 Maccabees 3:41.

new.title: Judas urges his men to fight nobly and trust the Almighty
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Reported exhortation with the saying 'they trust in weapons… we trust in the Almighty God' (8:18).

new.title: Judas appoints his brothers over divisions and reads the sacred book
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Division commands, a public reading and the watchword 'God’s help' before battle.

new.title: Antiochus orders his charioteer to drive on to destroy Jerusalem
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
new.note: Reported order with an arrogant vow, answered by God’s plague (9:5); 9:2 is narrative.

new.title: Submit to God; no mortal should think himself equal to God
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes, stricken
new.note: Maxim spoken in context verse 9:12; 9:11 narrates his coming to understanding.

new.title: Antiochus appoints his son Antiochus king as his successor
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes, by letter
new.recipient: the Jews and his son Antiochus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Designation of a successor, explained from his father’s practice; chapter 9 has no records.

new.title: Antiochus asks the Jews to stay loyal to him and his son
new.speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes, by letter
new.note: Request in the dying king’s letter; its greetings (9:19–22, P01157) need no record.

new.title: Antiochus Eupator appoints Lysias chief minister and governor of Coele-Syria
new.speaker: King Antiochus Eupator
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Distinct from first-pass P01060 (Antiochus IV leaves Lysias regent, 1 Maccabees 3:32–36).

new.title: Maccabeus leaves Simon, Joseph and Zacchaeus to besiege the towers
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Outside candidate list (10:19); their men’s bribery follows (10:20–22).

new.title: Judas urges his men to share the danger and help their brothers
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Reported battle exhortation; the prayer in 11:6 is out of scope.

new.title: Lysias proposes peace with the Jews on just terms
new.speaker: Lysias
new.note: Peace overture and Judas’s written requests granted by the king; compare ot-1-maccabees-v6-58.

new.title: Lysias’s letter urges the Jews’ goodwill and sends negotiators
new.speaker: Lysias
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 11:18–21 outside candidate list (never batched); Lysias’s proposal is first-pass P01161 (11:13–15).

new.title: Antiochus V tells Lysias to send the Jews pledges of peace
new.speaker: King Antiochus Eupator, by letter
new.note: Executive instruction following the decree of 11:25 (ot-2-maccabees-v11-25); 11:23 is its preamble.

new.title: Roman envoys tell the Jews to send word quickly on referred matters
new.speaker: Quintus Memmius and Titus Manius, Roman envoys
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Letter approving Lysias’s grants and asking for envoys; 11:38 is a farewell.

new.title: Joppa’s decree lures its Jews aboard boats and drowns them
new.speaker: the people of Joppa, by common decree
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Treacherous civic decree in the context verses; Judas’s orders in 12:5 lack content and 12:7 is narrative.

new.title: The defeated Arabs ask Judas for pledges of peace
new.speaker: the defeated Arab nomads
new.note: Reported request, granted with pledges (12:12).

new.title: The Jews urge Scythopolis to remain favorable to their people
new.speaker: Judas and his men
new.note: Reported thanks and request after the Scythopolitans’ humane treatment of local Jews.

new.title: Judas sends a sin offering to Jerusalem for the fallen
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus, commended by the narrator
new.recipient: his men and the priests in Jerusalem
new.note: Adjacent gap, not flagged: collection, sin offering and the narrator’s teaching on prayer for the dead. 12:39 is narrative.

new.title: Antiochus V orders Menelaus executed at Beroea
new.speaker: King Antiochus Eupator
new.note: Reported execution order at Lysias’s prompting; 13:5–8 describe it as just retribution.

new.title: Judas and the elders resolve to march out before the king invades
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus with the elders
new.note: Council decision after the three days of prayer recorded in AUD-16-13-10.

new.title: Judas urges his men to die fighting for law and temple
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Reported exhortation to fight for laws, temple, city, homeland and civic life.

new.title: Demetrius appoints Nicanor governor of Judea with orders to kill Judas
new.speaker: King Demetrius
new.recipient: Nicanor, former commander of the elephants
new.note: Also ordered to scatter Judas’s men and install Alcimus as high priest. The parallel 1 Maccabees 7:26 is not itemized either.

new.title: Nicanor sends envoys to give and receive pledges with Judas
new.speaker: Nicanor
new.note: Envoys sent with a charge, like the catalogue’s messenger commissions (e.g. Esther 4:10).

new.title: Judas posts armed men at key points against treachery
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.note: Outside candidate list (14:22); cf. AUD-15-12-26 (Jonathan’s armed watch).

new.title: Nicanor urges Judas to marry and have children
new.speaker: Nicanor
new.note: Reported urging; Judas complies, marries and settles down.

new.title: Demetrius orders Nicanor to send Judas in chains to Antioch
new.speaker: King Demetrius, by letter
new.note: Outside candidate list: royal written order prompted by Alcimus’s slander (14:26); Nicanor receives ‘these instructions’ (14:28).

new.title: Nicanor sends five hundred soldiers to arrest Razis
new.speaker: Nicanor
new.note: Outside candidate list (candidate 14:42 is narrative). Reported sending with orders to arrest, like AUD-16-5-11.

new.title: Nicanor commands arms taken up on the Sabbath for the king’s business
new.speaker: Nicanor
new.recipient: his army, including the Jews compelled to accompany him
new.note: His counter-claim to command as ‘sovereign on earth’, answering 15:4; the narrator says he did not succeed.

new.title: Judas orders Nicanor’s head and hand displayed and his tongue cut up
new.speaker: Judas Maccabeus
new.recipient: his men and the people gathered at Jerusalem
new.note: 15:30 (outside candidate list) begins the orders; 15:33 has the tongue given to birds. Cf. 1 Maccabees 7:47, not itemized.

new.title: Wine mixed with water delights, as a well-ordered account does
new.speaker: the epitomist (author of 2 Maccabees)
new.note: Epilogue maxim that unmixed wine or water harms; a borderline literary analogy, so low.

new.title: The governor bars unproven priests from eating the most holy things
new.speaker: Athersatha (the governor)
new.recipient: priestly families unable to prove their descent
new.note: Until a priest arises with the illuminating and perfect things (Urim and Thummim). Same ruling at Nehemiah 7:65 (P01208).

new.title: Zorobabel and Iesous set the Levites over the temple work
new.speaker: Zorobabel, Iesous and the returned priests and Levites
new.recipient: the Levites from twenty years old and upward
new.note: Outside candidate list (3:8 never batched, 3:9 context); Ezra 3 has no records.

new.title: Officials urge Artaxerxes to search the records and halt Jerusalem’s rebuilding
new.speaker: Raoum the baaltam, Samsai the scribe and their colleagues
new.note: Petition by letter; compare the catalogue’s record of an opponent’s appeal to a king (ot-1-maccabees-v7-7).

new.title: Arthasastha orders the records searched and finds Jerusalem rebellious
new.speaker: King Arthasastha
new.recipient: his officials; Raoum, Samsai and their colleagues
new.note: 4:19 'I issued a decision, and we searched'; cf. Darius’s search (first-pass P01191). Stop order is P01188 (4:21–22).

new.title: Thanthanai asks Darius to search the archives for Cyrus’s decree
new.speaker: Thanthanai the governor, Satharbouzana and their colleagues
new.note: Petition by letter; also asks the king to send word of his decision.

new.title: Darius orders a search of the royal archives in Babylon
new.speaker: Darius the king
new.note: Outside candidate list: the king’s decision answering 5:17; it leads to Cyrus’s archived decree (6:3).

new.title: The exiles station priests and Levites in their divisions per Moses’ book
new.speaker: the returned exiles
new.note: Outside candidate list (never batched).

new.title: Arthasastha sends Ezra to inspect Judea and Jerusalem by God’s law
new.speaker: King Arthasastha and his seven advisers
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

new.title: Ezra sends leaders to bring Levites and temple servants for God’s house
new.speaker: Ezra
new.recipient: Eleazar, Ariel, Samaia and other leading men
new.note: Outside candidate list: finding no Levites (8:15), Ezra sends men with words to speak, to bring ministers.

new.title: Ezra proclaims a fast at the river to seek a safe journey
new.speaker: Ezra

new.title: Ezra makes the leaders and all Israel swear to the proposal
new.speaker: Ezra
new.recipient: the leaders, priests, Levites and all Israel
new.note: Outside candidate list: the oath executing Shecaniah’s covenant proposal (10:3); compare Nehemiah 5:12 (Instruction).

new.title: Ezra and family heads are set apart to examine the foreign marriages
new.speaker: the returned community
new.recipient: Ezra the priest and the heads of ancestral houses
new.note: Carries out the hearing plan of 10:14 (ot-ezra-v10-14) by appointing the examiners.

new.title: The guilty priests pledge to dismiss their wives and offer a ram
new.speaker: the priests of Iesous’s family
new.note: Pledge with a guilt-offering ram, carrying out the oath of 10:5 (first-pass P01196).

new.title: Artaxerxes sends Nehemiah to Judah to rebuild Jerusalem
new.speaker: Arthasastha (Artaxerxes) the king, at Nehemiah’s request
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (2:6 is a context verse): Nehemiah’s request (2:5) and the king’s sending with a time limit (2:6).

new.title: Nehemiah asks the king for letters of passage and timber
new.speaker: Nehemiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Letters to the governors beyond the river and to Asaph, keeper of the king’s park; the king grants them.

new.title: Nehemiah’s enemies plot a surprise attack to stop the work
new.speaker: Sanaballat, Tobia and the other adversaries
new.note: A plot, recorded as the catalogue records plots at Genesis 37:20 and Exodus 1:10 (Instruction).

new.title: Nehemiah orders the builders to rally wherever the horn sounds
new.speaker: Nehemiah
new.recipient: the nobles, leaders and people building the wall
new.note: Outside candidate list; the chapter’s records cover only 4:8 and 4:16.

new.title: Nehemiah has gatekeepers, singers and Levites appointed
new.speaker: Nehemiah
new.note: Precedes his orders for the gates (ot-nehemiah-v7-3).

new.title: The people ask Ezra to bring the book of Moses’ law
new.speaker: all the people gathered at the Water Gate
new.note: Ezra brings the law and reads it to the assembly (8:2–3).

new.title: The people cast lots to settle one in ten in Jerusalem
new.speaker: the people and their rulers
new.recipient: the families of Judah outside Jerusalem
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (no passage in chapter 11): a communal resettlement decision by lot.

new.title: A royal command governs the temple singers
new.speaker: the Persian king
new.note: Reported royal order; the Saints text gives no content.

new.title: The Levites are summoned to Jerusalem for the wall’s dedication
new.speaker: the leaders at Jerusalem
new.note: Brought to celebrate with thanksgivings, songs, cymbals, psalteries and lyres.

new.title: Nehemiah stations two great thanksgiving choirs on the wall
new.speaker: Nehemiah
new.recipient: the rulers of Judah and two companies of singers
new.note: Outside candidate list; the dedication rite of 12:27–43 has no record.

new.title: Nehemiah charges the Levites to guard the gates and hallow the Sabbath
new.speaker: Nehemiah
new.note: The prayer in the rest of the verse is out of scope.

new.title: Nehemiah sets duty divisions for priests and Levites and the wood offering
new.speaker: Nehemiah
new.recipient: the priests, Levites and wood carriers
new.note: Includes the firstfruits (bakchouria); the prayers in 13:29 and 13:31 are out of scope.

new.title: The king orders Mordecai to serve at court and rewards him
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Addition A; the record-keeping in 1:1p parallels first-pass P01227 (2:23).

new.title: The king orders the stewards to follow his and the guests’ wishes
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes
new.recipient: the stewards of the royal household
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported order governing the drinking at the feast.

new.title: The king orders the eunuchs to bring Queen Astin before him
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes
new.note: Outside candidate list: the order Astin refuses (1:12), which 1:15 calls ‘what the king commanded through the eunuchs’.

new.title: Mordecai commands Esther not to reveal her ancestry or homeland
new.speaker: Mordecai
new.note: Repeated at 2:20; link that verse here too.

new.title: Mordecai instructs Esther to fear God and keep his commandments
new.speaker: Mordecai
new.note: Greek text; the verse also restates the non-disclosure order of 2:10.

new.title: The king orders Mordecai’s loyalty recorded in the royal library
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list: the commendation later read to the king (6:1–2).

new.title: The king commands everyone at court to bow down before Haman
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes
new.note: 3:3–4: the courtiers press Mordecai daily to obey the king’s word; he refuses.

new.title: Haman asks the king to decree the destruction of the Jews
new.speaker: Haman
new.note: Accuses the Jews of disobeying the king’s laws and offers ten thousand talents; leads to 3:10–11 (ot-esther-v3-11).

new.title: Esther sends Achrathaeus to learn from Mordecai what has happened
new.speaker: Queen Esther
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Like the catalogue’s 4:10 messenger record (ot-esther-v4-10); 4:4 reports her earlier sending of clothes.

new.title: Persian law: uninvited entry to the king’s inner court means death
new.speaker: Persian royal law, cited by Esther
new.note: Only one to whom the king extends the golden sceptre lives; Esther goes 'contrary to the law' (4:16).

new.title: Esther invites the king and Haman to her reception
new.speaker: Queen Esther
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: A request to the king, answering his offer in 5:3.

new.title: The king orders Haman brought quickly to Esther’s reception
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Compare the catalogue’s summons record at 6:5 (ot-esther-v6-5).

new.title: Esther asks the king and Haman to come again tomorrow
new.speaker: Queen Esther
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Her second invitation, made at the first drinking feast.

new.title: The sleepless king orders the chronicles brought and read to him
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The reading uncovers Mordecai’s unrewarded loyalty (6:2–3).

new.title: Esther pleads with the king for her life and her people
new.speaker: Queen Esther
new.note: Her decisive petition at the second feast; the king’s offer (7:2) is not itself a directive.

new.title: Esther asks the king to revoke Haman’s letters against the Jews
new.speaker: Queen Esther
new.note: 8:3 and 8:5 (context verses) carry the request; 8:6 is its plea. Leads to the counter-decree (ot-esther-v8-8).

new.title: Artaxerxes warns that trusted advisers can lead rulers into innocent bloodshed
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes (royal letter)
new.recipient: the satraps, rulers and loyal subjects
new.note: Gnomic warning in the letter's preamble; the long record ot-esther-v8-11 captures only the decree's provisions.

new.title: The king grants a second day and orders Haman’s sons hanged
new.speaker: King Artaxerxes
new.note: Outside candidate list: the royal order granting Esther’s request (ot-esther-v9-13).

new.title: Job summons and purifies his children, offering sacrifices for them
new.speaker: Job
new.note: Job’s habitual practice: he sends for his children to be purified, lest they had cursed God in their hearts.

new.title: The Lord gave and the Lord took away; bless his name
new.speaker: Job
new.recipient: spoken in worship before the Lord
new.note: 1:21 is a context verse (outside candidate list): a maxim of acceptance; cf. Ecclesiastes 5:14 and 1 Timothy 6:7.

new.title: Job rebukes his wife: bear evil from God as well as good
new.speaker: Job
new.note: Answers his wife’s urging (ot-job-v2-9e); counsel to a person, not an appeal to God.

new.title: Eliphaz: those who plow wrong and sow it reap pains
new.speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
new.note: Outside candidate list (follows the 4:7 Study Context record); the friends’ counsel, which God later faults (42:7); cf. Galatians 6:7.

new.title: Eliphaz: anger kills the fool, and his prosperity is soon devoured
new.speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
new.note: Covers candidate 5:5 (P01251) as well; the friends’ counsel, recorded with its speaker.

new.title: Eliphaz urges Job to examine for himself whether he has sinned
new.speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
new.note: Closing charge of Eliphaz’s first speech, after the promises of 5:18–26.

new.title: Those who trust in cities and possessions will be put to shame
new.speaker: Job
new.note: 6:20 (context verse) states the maxim within Job’s complaint about faithless friends.

new.title: Bildad: the hope of those who forget the Lord will perish
new.speaker: Bildad the Shuhite
new.note: Outside candidate list (8:11 is a context verse): the papyrus saying; 8:14–19 elaborate it.

new.title: Bildad: the ungodly are uprooted, but God will not reject the innocent
new.speaker: Bildad the Shuhite
new.note: Conclusion of the papyrus illustration (8:14–19) with the maxim of 8:20.

new.title: Zophar: the one who says much will hear an answer
new.speaker: Zophar the Minaean
new.note: Also contains the Greek beatitude ‘Blessed is the one born of woman who lives a short life’.

new.title: Zophar urges Job to purify his heart and put away lawlessness
new.speaker: Zophar the Minaean
new.note: The promises that follow (11:15–19) are not directives.

new.title: Job tells his friends that keeping silent would be their wisdom
new.speaker: Job
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse) between 13:4 and recorded 13:6; cf. Proverbs 17:28 (first-pass B12 P01694).

new.title: Eliphaz: a wise person does not argue with useless words
new.speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
new.note: A rhetorical question carrying a maxim on speech; borderline.

new.title: Eliphaz calls Job to hear what the wise have handed down
new.speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
new.note: Compare the catalogue’s ‘listen’ Commands at Job 13:17 and 34:16.

new.title: Let the faithful hold their way and the clean-handed take courage
new.speaker: Job
new.note: 17:9 is a context verse; jussive exhortation that the righteous persevere and resist the lawless, otherwise unrecorded.

new.title: Bildad: such is the dwelling of those who do not know God
new.speaker: Bildad the Shuhite
new.note: Sums up Bildad’s description of the ungodly’s end (18:5–20).

new.title: Job pleads with his friends to have mercy on him
new.speaker: Job
new.note: Addressed to the friends, not to God.

new.title: Job warns his friends to beware, for wrath comes on the lawless
new.speaker: Job

new.title: Zophar: the joy of the ungodly is brief and ends in ruin
new.speaker: Zophar the Minaean
new.note: Outside candidate list: thesis of Zophar’s second speech (after candidate 20:2); 20:6–29 elaborate it.

new.title: God humbles the arrogant and saves the one with downcast eyes
new.speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
new.note: Maxim within Eliphaz's promise (22:21–30); cf. Proverbs 3:34, James 4:6. Borderline: 22:30 is only Study Context.

new.title: The silver the ungodly hoard will pass to the righteous
new.speaker: Job
new.note: Part of Job’s description of the ungodly’s portion (27:13–23).

new.title: Job rescued the poor and orphan and was eyes to the blind
new.speaker: Job
new.note: Includes 29:12, 14–17 beyond the candidates; portrait of righteous conduct like first-pass Job 31 findings (B10 P01315).

new.title: Job covenants with his eyes not to gaze at a virgin
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.note: The oath (31:1–40) is itemized only at 31:13–15; 31:2–4 give the motive: God sees every step. Cf. K007 (Matthew 5:28).

new.title: Job disowns deceit, a straying heart and the taking of gifts
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.note: Outside candidate list; oath clause (gifts as bribes) with the self-imprecation of 31:8.

new.title: Job renounces adultery as a fire that destroys to the roots
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.note: The self-curse of candidate 31:10 frames the maxim of 31:11–12: defiling a neighbor’s wife is a consuming fire.

new.title: Job did not withhold help from the poor, widow, orphan or naked
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.note: Outside candidate list; oath clause on care for the needy, motivated by fear of the Lord (31:23).

new.title: Job renounces trust in gold and the worship of sun and moon
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.note: Oath clause; 31:28 calls such worship lying before the Lord Most High. Cf. C0981 (Deuteronomy 4:19).

new.title: Job kept his door open and lodged every stranger
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.note: Outside candidate list; oath clause on hospitality.

new.title: Job did not hide his sin but confessed it before all
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.note: Outside candidate list; oath clause (31:34 is a context verse).

new.title: Job tore up debtors’ bonds, taking nothing from the debtor
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.note: Greek text of the oath: for fear of the Lord he returned written bonds and exacted nothing.

new.title: Job did not exploit the land or wrong its owners
new.speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
new.topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
new.note: Outside candidate list; final oath clause, with nettles and brambles as self-imprecation.

new.title: Elihu refuses to show partiality or be overawed by anyone
new.speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
new.note: A personal resolve of impartiality; borderline.

new.title: Elihu calls Job to hear his words and listen to his speech
new.speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
new.note: Elihu's opening call to listen; the catalogue records like calls (13:17, 34:16) as Commands.

new.title: Elihu: God inspects everyone and repays each as he acts
new.speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
new.note: 34:9 forbids saying there is no inspection; 34:11 states repayment by deeds (cf. Romans 2:6 in AUD-49-2-1).

new.title: Elihu: the Lord does not reject the innocent but upholds the righteous
new.speaker: Elihu son of Barachel

new.title: Elihu: those who listen and serve prosper; the disobedient perish
new.speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
new.note: 36:10 reports God telling them to turn from injustice; candidate 36:12 completes the two ways.

new.title: Wrath comes on the ungodly for gifts taken to do injustice
new.speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
new.note: Immediately precedes ot-job-v36-19 (36:19–21); bribery maxim, cf. Exodus 23:8 (C0225).

new.title: Elihu: the Almighty judges justly, so the wise in heart fear him
new.speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
new.note: 37:24 is a context verse; compare AUD-20-28-28.

new.title: God directs Job to look at the beast made beside him
new.speaker: the Lord, from the cloud
new.note: Behemoth: the ironic challenges of 40:10–13 are Study Context, but this is a plain call to consider God’s work.

new.title: The rebel kings resolve to throw off the Lord’s bonds
new.speaker: the kings and rulers of the earth
new.note: A plot quoted in the psalm, recorded as the catalogue records plots at Genesis 11:4 and 37:20 (Instruction).

new.title: Turn back, or God will sharpen his sword against you
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.recipient: the wicked who refuse to turn back
new.note: Conditional warning addressed to hearers ('if you do not return'): an implicit call to repent, like recorded warnings at 49:22 and 74:5.

new.title: Advisers urge the psalmist to flee to the mountains like a bird
new.speaker: unnamed advisers
new.note: Quoted counsel the psalmist rejects as faithless; the catalogue records such advice (cf. Job's wife, ot-job-v2-9e).

new.title: Whoever loves injustice hates his own soul
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Outside candidate list: maxim that the Lord tests righteous and ungodly and loves righteous deeds; uncovered.

new.title: The fool says in his heart that there is no God
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Repeated as Greek Psalm 52:2–4: link that as Additional Scripture. 13:3 is quoted in Romans 3:10–18 (A121 is Study Context only).

new.title: Jacob and Israel are called to rejoice when God restores them
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Jussive call to rejoice, like recorded Greek Psalm 149:2. Same verse at Greek Psalm 52:7 (there indicative): link as Additional Scripture.

new.title: Whoever dwells with the Lord walks blamelessly and keeps his word
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Entrance liturgy: blameless walk, truthful speech, no harm or reproach to neighbours, honouring God-fearers, keeping oaths.

new.title: Do not lend at interest or take bribes against the innocent
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Echoes Torah laws C0206 (interest) and C0225 (bribes); closes 'whoever does these things will never be shaken'.

new.title: The Lord's law gives wisdom; in keeping it is great reward
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Praise of the law that teaches its worth, like recorded law-wisdom AUD-21-118-9; 18:12 'in keeping them there is great recompense'.

new.title: Only the clean-handed and pure in heart may ascend God's mountain
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Entrance liturgy like Greek Psalm 14: innocent hands, pure heart, no vain or deceitful oath.

new.title: The Lord teaches his way to the humble and God-fearing
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Context verse 24:8 and unflagged 24:9–10,12–14: declarative wisdom inside the prayer, uncovered.

new.title: Blessed is the forgiven one in whose mouth is no deceit
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Beatitude quoted in Romans 4:7–8 (no record there either); 31:5 testimony of confession supports it.

new.title: Confess sin to the Lord; let every holy one pray in time
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Between first-pass 31:1–2 and 31:8–9: confession brings forgiveness, so the godly should pray in time (31:6, context verse).

new.title: The sinner has many scourges; mercy surrounds those who trust the Lord
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Outside candidate list: wisdom saying between recorded 31:9 and 31:11, uncovered.

new.title: Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord
new.speaker: the psalmist
new.note: Beatitude; declarative rather than directive.

new.title: Armies do not save kings; the Lord guards those who fear him
new.speaker: the psalmist
new.note: Candidate 32:19 completes unflagged 32:16–18: strength and horses do not save; the Lord rescues those who hope in him.

new.title: Approach the Lord and be enlightened; you will not be ashamed
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.recipient: the meek who hear the psalm
new.note: Plural imperative to hearers between recorded 33:4 and 33:9–10.

new.title: The Lord's eyes are on the righteous; he is near the brokenhearted
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Outside candidate list: motive of recorded 33:14–15; 33:16–17 quoted in 1 Peter 3:12 (A118), psalm verses unlinked.

new.title: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the Lord rescues them
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Closing wisdom of the acrostic psalm, incl. candidate 33:22 ('the death of sinners is evil'); its counsels 33:9–15 are recorded.

new.title: The wicked plots evil and has no fear of God before him
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Wisdom portrait of the wicked (35:2 quoted in Romans 3:18); descriptive, so low.

new.title: Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will grant your heart's requests
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.recipient: the faithful tempted to envy the wicked
new.note: Imperative between recorded 36:3 and 36:5; only this verse of the run is missing.

new.title: The wicked will soon vanish, but the meek will inherit the land
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.recipient: the faithful tempted to envy the wicked
new.note: Wisdom sayings motivating 36:7–8; 36:11 is echoed in Matthew 5:5 (AUD-44-5-3).

new.title: The sword the wicked draw against the upright pierces their own heart
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.recipient: the faithful tempted to envy the wicked
new.note: Fills the gap between first-pass 36:9–13 and 36:16–17 in this saying-by-saying psalm; 36:15 is worded as a wish, hence low.

new.title: Better a little for the righteous than the great wealth of sinners
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Classic 'better than' wisdom saying; no record (nor for similar Proverbs 15:16, 16:8).

new.title: The sinner borrows and does not repay; the righteous gives freely
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Outside candidate list: a clear uncovered wisdom saying in the same psalm (no signal detected).

new.title: The righteous is never forsaken; he shows mercy and lends all day
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Outside candidate list: elder's testimony teaching mercy and lending, as in recorded AUD-21-111-1; uncovered.

new.title: The righteous speaks wisdom and keeps God's law in his heart
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Portrait of righteous speech and an inward law, distinct from neighbouring records.

new.title: The Lord will not abandon the righteous to those seeking his life
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Declarative assurance leading into recorded 36:34 ('Wait for the Lord').

new.title: The psalmist resolves to guard his tongue when sinners confront him
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Autobiographical resolve long read as counsel on restraint of speech; borderline, like first-pass Greek Psalm 100:2–3.

new.title: Every person is a passing shadow, hoarding wealth for unknown heirs
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.recipient: God, in the hearing of readers
new.note: Context verse 38:6 and unflagged 38:7: reflection on vanity inside a prayer, so low.

new.title: Blessed is the one who hopes in the Lord, not in vanities
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Beatitude directing trust and turning from vanities.

new.title: God desires a listening, obedient heart rather than sacrifice
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Same teaching as AUD-09-15-22 and ot-hosea-v6-6; quoted in Hebrews 10:5–7 (A103 is Study Context only).

new.title: Blessed is the one who considers the poor and needy
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Beatitude commending care for the poor, with the Lord's promised protection (40:3–4).

new.title: God anoints the righteous king with the oil of gladness
new.speaker: the sons of Korah (royal wedding song)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported anointing to kingship (quoted of the Son in Hebrews 1:8–9, no record there); poetic, so low.

new.title: Mount Zion and Judah's daughters are called to rejoice in God's judgments
new.speaker: the sons of Korah
new.recipient: Mount Zion / the daughters of Judea
new.note: Jussive call to rejoice spoken within an address to God; opens the processional commands recorded at 47:13–14.

new.title: Wealth cannot ransom a life; rich and foolish alike die
new.speaker: the sons of Korah (wisdom psalm)
new.note: Core teaching of the wisdom psalm whose call to listen (48:2) and counsel (48:17) are recorded.

new.title: Death shepherds the self-assured into Hades; God redeems the upright
new.speaker: the sons of Korah (wisdom psalm)
new.note: Fills the gap between first-pass 48:7–13 and 48:17–21 (extend) in this wisdom psalm.

new.title: God calls his people to hear his testimony against them
new.speaker: God (in Asaph's psalm)
new.note: God's own summons 'Hear, My people… I testify unto you', like recorded 80:9.

new.title: God needs no animal sacrifices; the world and its fullness are his
new.speaker: God, in Asaph's psalm
new.note: God's rationale before recorded 49:14–15 (offer praise instead); cf. Acts 17:25 and first-pass Greek Psalm 49:16–21.

new.title: God rebukes those who recite his covenant but hate his instruction
new.speaker: God (in Asaph's psalm)
new.note: Indictment naming hypocrisy, joining thieves and adulterers, deceit and slandering a brother; precedes recorded 49:22.

new.title: A broken and humbled heart is the sacrifice God will not despise
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Context verse 50:19 with 50:18, not flagged: declarative teaching like recorded AUD-09-15-22 and ot-hosea-v6-6.

new.title: See the one who trusted wealth instead of making God his helper
new.speaker: the righteous, quoted by David
new.note: Lesson drawn from the boaster's downfall; compare recorded 61:11 (do not hope in wealth).

new.title: A rebuke to rulers who neither speak nor judge righteously
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.recipient: the sons of men who judge (rulers and judges)
new.note: Rebuke addressed to people, like recorded AUD-21-4-3 ('Sons of men, how long…'); implicit charge to judge uprightly.

new.title: Surely there is reward for the righteous and a God who judges
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Outside candidate list: concluding wisdom of the psalm whose rebuke (57:2–3) is proposed above.

new.title: Submit to God, my soul, for my hope comes from him
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Self-exhortation (refrain of 61:2–3) like recorded AUD-21-41-6; leads into recorded 61:9.

new.title: Power belongs to God, who repays each according to his works
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Outside candidate list: closes the counsel of recorded 61:9–11; quoted in Romans 2:6 (only broad AUD-49-2-1).

new.title: God's mercy is better than life itself
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.recipient: God, in the hearing of readers
new.note: 'Better than' saying spoken to God in praise, so low (cf. 83:11).

new.title: The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and hope in him
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: Closing declarative assurance about the righteous; not a direct call, so low.

new.title: God will not hear one who cherishes injustice in his heart
new.speaker: the psalmist
new.note: Teaching within the testimony invited at recorded 65:16; compare Proverbs 28:9.

new.title: All peoples are called to thank God and to fear him
new.speaker: the psalmist (community song)
new.note: Jussives partly addressed to God (cf. Study Context 34:27), but 66:8 matches recorded 32:8 ('Let all the earth fear the Lord').

new.title: A call to bless God in the assemblies of Israel
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
