new.note: Outside candidate list: plural imperative 'In assemblies bless God' missed by the detector; uncovered call to worship.

new.title: Praise in song pleases God more than a sacrificial bull
new.speaker: David (the psalmist)
new.note: First-person vow carrying a teaching on praise over sacrifice; leads into recorded 68:33.

new.title: The psalmist's enemies urge one another to pursue and seize him
new.speaker: the psalmist's enemies
new.note: Quoted hostile exhortation; the catalogue records such plots elsewhere (ot-jeremiah-v11-19, ot-genesis-v37-20).

new.title: The wicked's prosperity ends in ruin; nearness to God is good
new.speaker: Asaph
new.recipient: God, in the hearing of readers
new.note: Candidate 72:18 sits in the wisdom psalm's resolution; 72:27–28 (unflagged) state its lesson.

new.title: Israel's enemies resolve to burn all God's feasts from the earth
new.speaker: Israel's enemies (quoted by Asaph)
new.note: 'Come, let us burn…' plot like recorded ot-jeremiah-v18-18 and ot-genesis-v37-20.

new.title: If only my people would listen and walk in my ways
new.speaker: God (in Asaph's psalm)
new.note: Outside candidate list: Greek Psalm 80 has no passage in this batch; continues God's recorded appeals at 80:9–11.

new.title: The nations allied against Israel plot to wipe out its name
new.speaker: the coalition of nations and their rulers (quoted by Asaph)
new.note: 'Come, let us destroy them' (82:5) and 'Let us inherit God's sanctuary' (82:13, P01534); plots are recorded elsewhere (ot-jeremiah-v18-18).

new.title: Blessed are those dwelling in God's house, strengthened by him
new.speaker: the sons of Korah
new.recipient: God, in the hearing of worshippers
new.note: Beatitudes spoken to God, so low; they commend dwelling in God's house and pilgrim devotion.

new.title: One day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere

new.title: It is good to walk after the Lord
new.speaker: Ben Sira
new.note: Moral drawn from Caleb's preserved strength; the only counsel line in 46:1–10.

new.title: Elijah is appointed to turn fathers' hearts and restore Jacob's tribes
new.speaker: the Lord (recalled by Ben Sira)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Recalls Malachi 3:22–23 (Elijah sent to restore hearts), which itself has no itemized record.

new.title: Blessed is the one who studies and practices these teachings
new.speaker: Ben Sira
new.note: Closing beatitude of the book (50:23 wish, 50:25–27 colophon are out of scope).

new.title: Woe to the sinful nation that has abandoned the Lord
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Prophetic woe, treated as Wisdom like first-pass woes (Isaiah 3:9–11, 5:8–10); 1:5 warns against adding lawlessness.

new.title: The Lord tells Judah to stop bringing futile offerings and festivals
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: the rulers and people of Judah and Jerusalem
new.note: 1:12–13 'you will no longer continue… it is futile' forbids empty worship; 1:15 refuses bloodstained prayers. Covers P01874.

new.title: Isaiah summons the house of Jacob to walk in the Lord's light
new.speaker: Isaiah

new.title: Woe to the lawless: the works of their hands return on them
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Woes of 3:9 and 3:11 frame the plot already recorded at 3:10.

new.title: The Lord summons Judah to judge between Him and His vineyard
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: the men of Judah and residents of Jerusalem
new.note: 5:3 (shown as context) has no record; its summons to judge introduces 5:4's question.

new.title: Woe to those who join house to house and field to field
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor

new.title: Woe to those who chase strong drink and ignore the Lord's works
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah

new.title: Woe to those who drag sin along and mock God's plan
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: 5:19 is a Study Context record; the woes of 5:20–24 are AUD-28-5-20.

new.title: Aram and Ephraim plan to invade Judah and install Tabeel's son
new.speaker: the kings of Aram and Ephraim
new.note: Plotted plan, like records ot-isaiah-v3-10 and ot-genesis-v11-4; the Lord annuls it (7:7).

new.title: Ahaz is warned that without faith he will not understand
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: Ahaz and the house of David
new.note: Closing call to faith of the 7:4–9 message; could instead extend ot-isaiah-v7-4.

new.title: The house of David is told to call the virgin's son Emmanuel
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: Ahaz and the house of David
new.note: Naming command, like 'you shall call his name Jesus'. Matthew 1:23 quotes it within AUD-44-1-20.

new.title: Ephraim proudly resolves to rebuild with hewn stone and cedar
new.speaker: the people of Ephraim and Samaria
new.note: Proud 'come, let us' resolve, recorded like the Babel builders' plan (ot-genesis-v11-4).

new.title: Woe to those who write unjust decrees that rob the poor
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah

new.title: The Lord sends His wrath against a lawless nation by Assyria's rod
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: Assyria, the rod of His anger
new.note: God commissions an instrument of judgment and orders the plunder (10:6); Assyria's own boast differs (10:7–14).

new.title: Zion’s inhabitants are called to exult in Israel’s Holy One
new.speaker: the redeemed people’s song in Isaiah’s oracle
new.note: Call to praise addressed to people; closes the song whose 12:4–5 calls are only a Study Context record (ot-isaiah-v12-4).

new.title: Babylon’s people are told to wail, for the Lord’s day is near
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle against Babylon)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Prophetic summons to wail, like recorded ot-isaiah-v23-6 and ot-jeremiah-v6-26.

new.title: Israel is to take up a taunt against Babylon’s fallen king
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Scripted taunt ('you will take up this lament… and say'); compare future songs treated as Study Context (ot-isaiah-v12-4).

new.title: Moab is called to wail and mourn in sackcloth over its ruin
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle against Moab)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 15:3 (context verse, outside candidate list) continues the summons: sackcloth, beating, wailing. Isaiah 15 has no records.

new.title: Moab’s devourers are told to trample its vineyards as far as Iazer
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: the devourers of nations (invaders of Moab)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Summons to attackers, comparable to recorded ot-jeremiah-v5-10; 'Wander in the wilderness!' follows.

new.title: The watchman tells the inquirer from Seir to seek and stay near
new.speaker: the watchman in Isaiah’s vision
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reply to the call recorded at ot-isaiah-v21-11; a different speaker, so not an extension.

new.title: The Lord called Jerusalem to weeping, shaving and sackcloth
new.speaker: the Lord Sabaoth (reported by Isaiah)
new.note: Outside candidate list. Reported summons to mourn; ot-isaiah-v22-13 records the people feasting instead.

new.title: The ships of Carthage are told to wail over Tyre’s fall
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle concerning Tyre)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 23:14 (P01934) repeats the summons. The ships stand for their crews; compare recorded ot-isaiah-v23-6.

new.title: The earth’s people are told to wail over the vanished wine
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Imperative summons to wail amid the world judgment; Isaiah 24 has no records.

new.title: Hope belongs to the devout; woe to those who reject the law
new.speaker: voices from the ends of the earth (Isaiah’s oracle)
new.note: Woe-saying with its contrast of the devout and those who reject the law.

new.title: The hearer is told to deliver all these things to the nations
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Greek-based text has an imperative ('hand all these things over to the nations'); the addressee is unclear.

new.title: Women returning from a spectacle are summoned to come
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Brief summons inside the judgment oracle; its purpose is left unstated.

new.title: Unnamed gatherers are told to gather Israel’s sons one by one
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Command within the 'on that day' promise; compare recorded ot-isaiah-v43-6 (release My sons and daughters).

new.title: Woe to the proud crown of Ephraim’s drunken hirelings
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Woe against pride and drunkenness (28:7–8 continue), though mainly a judgment on Ephraim.

new.title: Woe to those who plan in secret and apart from the Lord
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Ethical woe, like recorded AUD-28-5-20; 30:1 ('a plan not through Me', context-adjacent, unrecorded) makes the same charge.

new.title: Turning back to God brings salvation; trust in futile things fails
new.speaker: the Lord, Israel’s Holy One, through Isaiah
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse). Call to return that was refused, like recorded ot-jeremiah-v6-16.

new.title: Blessed are those who remain in the Lord
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.note: Beatitude ('Blessed are those remaining in Him') after the promise that God waits to show mercy.

new.title: Woe to those trusting horses and chariots rather than the Holy One
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: 30:1–2 (woe to those going down to Egypt without asking God; unrecorded) is the same charge; link as Additional Scripture.

new.title: Blessed is the one with offspring and household in Zion
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Greek-text beatitude closing the Assyria oracle; more a blessing than counsel.

new.title: The fool plots harm against the lowly; the devout plan wisely
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.note: Wisdom contrast following 32:5 (Study Context ot-isaiah-v32-5); 32:8 is a context verse.

new.title: Blessed are those who sow beside every water
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
new.note: Beatitude closing the promise of the Spirit’s renewal (32:15–20).

new.title: Woe to the destroyer: those who betray will be handed over
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Retribution woe, though mainly a judgment on Assyria. Isaiah 33 has no records.

new.title: Wisdom, knowledge and reverence for the Lord are true treasures
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.note: Outside candidate list; maxim inside a promise ('these are treasures of righteousness').

new.title: Whoever walks righteously and refuses bribes will dwell secure
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.note: Outside candidate list. Entrance saying like Greek Psalm 14: upright speech, no bribes, shunning bloodshed and injustice.

new.title: The Lord’s sign: eat the aftergrowth, then sow, reap and plant
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: Hezekiah and the remnant of Judah
new.topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
new.note: Parallel 2 Kings 19:29 is also unrecorded; link it as Additional Scripture.

new.title: Those who wait for God renew their strength
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.note: Maxim-like promise to a class ('those enduring for God'), answering the complaint of 40:27.

new.title: The Lord puts His spirit on His servant to judge the nations
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: the Lord’s servant (named Jacob/Israel in this text)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 42:1 and 42:4 are outside the candidate list. Matthew 12:18–21 quotes it (inside AUD-44-12-15); the 42:5–9 commission is AUD-28-42-5.

new.title: The deaf and blind are summoned to listen and look
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.recipient: Israel, the spiritually deaf and blind
new.note: Call to perceive addressed to the people (42:19 names God’s servants); bare 'hear' summonses are often Study Context.

new.title: God tells Israel to remember and confess its lawless acts first
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: 'You, state your lawless acts first, so that you may be justified': a call to confession in the trial speech.

new.title: Know that the idolater’s heart is ashes and cannot save him
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Imperatives 'Know… See' close the idol satire; ot-isaiah-v44-21 then calls Israel to remember.

new.title: The Lord commissions His anointed Cyrus to free His people
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 44:28–45:1 and 45:3–6 are outside the candidate list. Cyrus’s call is also recalled in 41:2, 46:11 and 48:14–15.

new.title: Do not quarrel with your Maker, as clay with its potter
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Saying against disputing the Maker’s purposes (MT: two woes); Paul applies it in Romans 9:20–21, which is not itemized.

new.title: The Lord gives His servant an instructed tongue and an open ear
new.speaker: the Lord (reported by the servant)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Third Servant Song: equipped for a speaking task, and obedient ('I do not disobey'); records at 50:8 and 50:10 follow.

new.title: The righteous are taken away from evil, yet no one considers it
new.speaker: Isaiah
new.note: 'See how the righteous man perished': a reflection rebuking indifference. Isaiah 57 has no records.

new.title: Those who hold fast to the Lord will inherit His holy mountain
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Contrasted with idols that cannot rescue (57:13a is sarcastic); a maxim-like promise to a class.

new.title: The unjust are tossed like waves; the ungodly have no joy
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Outside candidate list. 48:22 (context verse) repeats 'There is no rejoicing for the ungodly'; link as Additional Scripture.

new.title: God rejects fasting joined to quarrels, oppression and outward show
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: 58:3 and 58:5 are context verses. Negative half of the fast teaching recorded at 58:6–7 (ot-isaiah-v58-6, ot-isaiah-v58-7).

new.title: The Lord appoints unceasing watchmen on Jerusalem’s walls
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Appointed guards 'will never be silent as they remember the Lord'; compare ot-isaiah-v21-6.

new.title: God looks to the humble who tremble at His word
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.note: Outside candidate list. Quoted in Acts 7:49–50 (A099, Study Context only); see also ot-isaiah-v66-5.

new.title: The Lord sends survivors to the nations and takes priests from them
new.speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 66:20–21 are outside the candidate list. Foretold sending to announce God’s glory among the nations; priests and Levites taken from them.

new.title: The Lord puts His words in Jeremiah’s mouth, setting him over nations
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 1:9 is a context verse; the mandate is 'to uproot, demolish, destroy, build and plant'.

new.title: Your own evil disciplines you; abandoning the Lord is bitter
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: 'Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter': maxim with a call to recognize it; 2:17 and 4:18 make the same point.

new.title: Israel is told to examine its ways and know what it did
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Call to self-examination; the similar call in 3:2 is only a Study Context record (ot-jeremiah-v3-2).

new.title: God recalls calling faithless Israel to return to Him
new.speaker: the Lord (recalled to Jeremiah)
new.note: Reported earlier call ('I said, Return to Me. But she did not return'), like the recalled command ot-jeremiah-v7-23.

new.title: Israel is called to acknowledge its iniquity against the Lord
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Content of the message Jeremiah is sent to proclaim (ot-jeremiah-v3-12); addressed to Israel, so a separate record.

new.title: Israel is called to return, renounce idols and swear truthfully
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Outside candidate list. Conditional call to return, with the oath 'The Lord lives' sworn in truth, judgment and righteousness.

new.title: Judah is told to wear sackcloth and wail at the Lord’s fury
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Summons to mourn in the alarm oracle of 4:5–8 (ot-jeremiah-v4-5, ot-jeremiah-v4-6); compare ot-jeremiah-v6-26.

new.title: Heralds are told to warn the nations and Jerusalem of invaders
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Remind the nations… Announce in Jerusalem': a warning summons like ot-jeremiah-v4-5.

new.title: Jeremiah is given the answer to why the Lord brought disaster
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Scripted reply ('you will say to them'): they served foreign gods, so they will serve foreigners in a foreign land.

new.title: The message is to be announced to Jacob and proclaimed in Judah
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Introduces the address recorded as Study Context at 5:21 (ot-jeremiah-v5-21).

new.title: Offerings from those who reject God’s law are not acceptable
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Follows 6:19 ('rejected My law'); compare AUD-09-15-22 (1 Samuel 15:22) and ot-hosea-v6-6.

new.title: The Lord appoints Jeremiah to test His people’s ways
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Appointment as assayer ('I have made you a tester'); 6:30 is Study Context (ot-jeremiah-v6-30).

new.title: Judah is told to amend its ways so God will settle it
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.recipient: all Judea at the Lord’s house
new.note: Core call of the temple sermon; 7:5–6 (ot-jeremiah-v7-5) spells out the amendment.

new.title: Judah is told to go to Shiloh and see what God did
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Warning by example: what God did to Shiloh because of Israel’s evil.

new.title: Jerusalem is told to cut off her hair and raise a lament
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Prophetic summons to mourn the rejected generation, like the recorded calls at 6:26, 9:17 and 22:10.

new.title: Israel is told to say false gods will perish from the earth
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Scripted answer to idolaters ('This is what you will say to them'); distinct from records 10:1–2 and 10:5.

new.title: Acknowledge that a person cannot direct his own steps
new.speaker: Jeremiah (in prayer)
new.note: Declarative maxim opening a prayer (10:23–25); only 10:23 teaches. Drop if sayings addressed to God are excluded.

new.title: Jeremiah is told to deliver the saying of the filled wineskins
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Scripted saying and reply ('you will say to this people… then you will say'), like the recorded reply at 23:33.

new.title: Jeremiah is given the answer: to death, sword, famine and captivity
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Scripted reply to 'Where shall we go out?' Alternatively extend ot-jeremiah-v15-1 (15:1, 'Send this people away').

new.title: God calls Jeremiah to return and renews his commission as His mouth
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 15:19 (context verse) holds the directive: return, bring out the honored from the unworthy, do not turn to them; echoes 1:18.

new.title: Jeremiah is told how to answer when asked why disaster comes
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Scripted reply: their fathers abandoned God and did not keep His law, and this generation did worse.

new.title: God tells Jeremiah to smash the jar before the men with him
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The sign-act itself; 19:1 (get the jar) and 19:11 (Study Context, its meaning) are recorded, the smashing is not.

new.title: Do not build your house by injustice or withhold workers’ wages
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Ethical woe like Hab 2:6–12 (AUD-39-2-6); 22:15–16 ties judging the poor’s case to knowing God; echoes Lev 19:13 (C0607).

new.title: God orders Jeconiah recorded as an outcast with no heir enthroned
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Decree on Jeconiah’s line ('Record this man as an outcast'); compare the recorded naming order for Pharaoh Neco (26:17).

new.title: Egypt’s routed troops urge one another to flee home
new.speaker: Egypt’s soldiers (quoted in the oracle)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Quoted mutual exhortation inside the Egypt oracle; the catalogue records similar ones at 6:4–5 and 28:9–10.

new.title: Jeremiah tells Seraiah to sink the scroll in the Euphrates
new.speaker: Jeremiah, relaying the Lord’s word
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The sign-act itself (bind a stone to the scroll, throw it in); record 28:64 holds only the interpreting words.

new.title: Attackers are told to set young warriors over Edom
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Brief war summons ('Appoint the young men over her') in the Edom oracle; the parallel line at 27:44 is first-person, not imperative.

new.title: Moab’s shattering is to be announced in Zogora
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Announce it in Zogora': a summons like recorded 27:2 (announce Babylon’s capture) and 31:17–19.

new.title: The priests and false prophets demand a death sentence for Jeremiah
new.speaker: the priests and false prophets
new.recipient: Judah’s rulers and all the people
new.note: Formal charge at Jeremiah’s trial (MT 26:11), like the first-pass demand at 45:4–5. Recording it does not approve it.

new.title: Judah’s rulers rule that Jeremiah does not deserve death
new.speaker: Judah’s rulers and all the people
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); the court’s acquittal answering 33:11 (MT 26:16).

new.title: The elders cite Micah’s case to dissuade the people from killing Jeremiah
new.speaker: some of the land’s elders
new.recipient: the whole assembly of the people
new.note: Counsel from precedent, comparable to Gamaliel’s advice (AUD-48-5-34); MT 26:17–19.

new.title: Jehoiakim sends men to Egypt to bring back the prophet Uriah
new.speaker: King Jehoiakim
new.note: Reported order of a wicked king; Uriah is then executed (MT 26:22–23).

new.title: Jeremiah is told to answer Shemaiah and rebuke the priest Zephaniah
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Greek-order text: 'I did not send you' to Shemaiah; Zephaniah reminded of his appointment as overseer to confine raving prophets (36:26).

new.title: Restored Israel is told to plant vineyards in Samaria and praise
new.speaker: the Lord through Jeremiah
new.note: Imperatives in the restoration oracle ('plant and praise'), like the recorded calls at 38:7 and 38:21.

new.title: Zedekiah’s covenant requires every Hebrew slave to be set free
new.speaker: King Zedekiah, by covenant with the people
new.note: Royal covenant of release (MT 34:8–10; also 41:15), distinct from the Torah law God recalls in ot-jeremiah-v41-14.

new.title: The officials summon Baruch to read the scroll to them
new.speaker: the officials (rulers) of Judah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Take… the roll… and come'; 'Read it again to us' (43:15, context); then 'Let us certainly report all these words to the king.'

new.title: Jehoiakim sends Jehudi to fetch the scroll and read it to him
new.speaker: King Jehoiakim
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported royal order (MT 36:21); the officials’ earlier summons of Baruch (43:14–16) is a first-pass finding.

new.title: Elnathan, Gedaliah and Gemariah urge the king not to burn the scroll
new.speaker: Elnathan, Gedaliah and Gemariah
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); a reported request the king ignored (MT 36:25).

new.title: Jehoiakim orders Baruch and Jeremiah arrested
new.speaker: King Jehoiakim
new.recipient: Jerahmeel the king’s son and Seraiah son of Azriel
new.note: Explicit reported order (MT 36:26); the officials’ warning to hide is ot-jeremiah-v43-19.

new.title: Zedekiah sends envoys asking Jeremiah to pray for them
new.speaker: King Zedekiah, through Jehucal and Zephaniah
new.note: A separate occasion from 21:2 (ot-jeremiah-v21-2): different envoys and a request for intercession.

new.title: Jeremiah begs Zedekiah not to send him back to Jonathan’s house
new.speaker: Jeremiah

new.title: Zedekiah orders Jeremiah held in the prison court with daily bread
new.speaker: King Zedekiah
new.note: Reported royal order in a context verse (not a listed candidate); no record covers 44:21.

new.title: The officials demand Jeremiah’s death, and Zedekiah yields him to them
new.speaker: the officials of Judah
new.note: 'Let that man be killed!'; the king answers 'He is in your hands' (45:5). Recording the demand does not approve it.

new.title: Zedekiah orders Ebed-melech to take thirty men and rescue Jeremiah
new.speaker: King Zedekiah
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours

new.title: Ebed-melech tells Jeremiah to put the rags beneath the ropes
new.speaker: Ebed-melech
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Uncovered directive two verses after the candidate (not listed): 'Put these beneath the ropes. Jeremiah did so.'

new.title: Babylon’s commanders release Jeremiah from prison into Gedaliah’s care
new.speaker: the king of Babylon’s commanders
new.recipient: their men and Gedaliah son of Ahikam
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported order (‘they sent and took Jeremiah’); the Greek omits MT 39:4–13. The later release is ot-jeremiah-v47-5.

new.title: Baalis king of Ammon sends Ishmael to assassinate Gedaliah
new.speaker: Baalis (Belisa) king of the Ammonites
new.note: Reported in the commanders’ warning, which Gedaliah disbelieves (MT 40:14); Johanan’s follow-up request is ot-jeremiah-v47-15.

new.title: Ishmael lures the mourning pilgrims in to Gedaliah to kill them
new.speaker: Ishmael son of Nethaniah
new.recipient: eighty pilgrims from Shechem, Salem and Samaria
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Deceitful invitation (‘Come in to Gedaliah’) before the massacre (MT 41:6–7).

new.title: God sends Ezekiel to the rebellious house of Israel
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Ezekiel’s call proper ('stand on your feet… I am sending you… you will say to them'); only 2:6 and 2:8 are recorded.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to announce that the end has come on Israel
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Order to proclaim ('say, Thus says the Lord to the land of Israel'); such orders are Commission records at 6:3 and 11:4.

new.title: The land is told to sound the trumpet as judgment comes
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Greek-text imperative ('Sound the trumpet and judge everything') inside the judgment oracle; compare recorded alarm calls Jeremiah 4:5 and 6:1.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to look north and see the people’s lawlessness
new.speaker: the Lord (in the vision)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: First order of the temple vision tour, like ot-ezekiel-v8-9; 8:6 adds ‘you will yet see greater lawlessness’.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to eat and drink in anguish as a sign
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Sign-act; its meaning (12:19) has a Study Context record, the command itself has none.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Israel’s false prophets
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Commission with the opening woe on those who prophesy from their own heart; 13:8 and 13:11 are Study Context only.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against the women who prophesy falsely
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 'Set your face firmly against the daughters of your people'; the 13:18 woe is Study Context only.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to testify to Jerusalem about her lawlessness
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 16:3 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v16-3); compare the first-pass extension of ot-ezekiel-v22-3 to 22:2.

new.title: Jerusalem is told to bear her shame for outdoing her sisters
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Imperatives 'receive your torment… be ashamed'; cf. 36:32 call to shame (ot-ezekiel-v36-32). Borderline sentence of judgment.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to tell Israel the parable of the eagles
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Opening charge; only the explanation (17:11–15, AUD-30-17-11) is recorded; 17:3 has a Study Context record only.

new.title: God forbids Israel's sour-grapes proverb: the soul that sins will die
new.speaker: the Lord
new.recipient: Ezekiel, for the house of Israel
new.note: Outside candidate list; 18:1–4 has no record. Cf. the 12:23 proverb kept as Study Context (ot-ezekiel-v12-23).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to take up a lament over Israel's rulers
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 19:2 has only a Study Context record; the charge to lament is unrecorded.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to confront the elders with their fathers' lawlessness
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Distinct from the later charge at 20:27 (ot-ezekiel-v20-27).

new.title: God tells the house of Israel to remove their idolatrous practices
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Present call to put away practices; 20:7 (ot-ezekiel-v20-7) only recalls the Exodus generation's command.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against the forest of the Negev
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: 21:3 has only a Study Context record; the commission itself is unrecorded.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to mark out two roads for Babylon's sword
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Symbolic act: a signpost where the road forks toward Rabbah and Jerusalem.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy the sword against the Ammonites
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

new.title: Ezekiel is told to indict the land and its corrupt leaders
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Outside candidate list; the oracle 22:23–31 against leaders, priests and people has no record.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to record the day Babylon besieged Jerusalem
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; distinct from the cauldron-parable charge at 24:3 (ot-ezekiel-v24-3).

new.title: Ezekiel is told not to mourn publicly for his wife's death
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Sign-act wholly unrecorded; 24:16–17 outside candidate list; 24:18 records his obedience; 24:22–24 applies the sign to Israel.

new.title: The exiles ask Ezekiel to explain his refusal to mourn
new.speaker: the people in exile
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); the request is answered by the oracle recorded at 24:21 (ot-ezekiel-v24-21).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against the Ammonites
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; 25:3 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v25-3).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to confront the ruler of Tyre's claim to divinity
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; the oracle 28:1–10 has no record.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to lament over the ruler of Tyre
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: The lament 28:11–19 has no record.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Sidon
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 28:22 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v28-22).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Pharaoh and all Egypt
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 29:3 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v29-3).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to proclaim the Lord's day against Egypt
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; 30:1–19 has only a Study Context record at 30:15.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to address Pharaoh and his multitude
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; chapter 31 has no record.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to lament over Pharaoh, king of Egypt
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 32:4 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v32-4).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to lament Egypt's descent into the pit
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; the second lament (32:17–32) has only a Study Context record at 32:21.

new.title: Shepherds should feed the flock, not themselves
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Indictment states leaders' duties: feed, strengthen, heal, bind up, seek the lost. Only the commission (34:2) is recorded.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Mount Seir
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; 35:3 has only a Study Context record (ot-ezekiel-v35-3).

new.title: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against Gog a second time
new.speaker: the Lord
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); a separate oracle from 38:2–3 and 38:14, which are recorded separately.

new.title: Appointed men search out and bury the dead to cleanse the land
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Foretold procedure: seven months of burial, permanent searchers, markers set by bones. Prediction rather than command.

new.title: Ezekiel is told to observe the temple vision and declare it
new.speaker: the man with the measuring reed
new.note: Opening charge of the temple vision; cf. the later charges at 43:10–11 and 44:5, recorded separately.

new.title: Inner-court chambers are assigned to priests keeping house and altar
new.speaker: the man with the measuring reed
new.note: Outside candidate list; also names Zadok's sons as those who draw near. Cf. 42:13–14 (AUD-30-42-13).

new.title: Levites who served idols may not serve as priests
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Outside candidate list; only inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v44-13 (44:13–21). 44:14 restates the 44:11 duties.

new.title: Only Zadok's sons may approach to offer fat and blood
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.recipient: Israel; the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v44-13. Same restriction at 40:46, 43:19 and 48:11.

new.title: Priests wear linen, not wool, when ministering in the inner court
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v44-13. Echoes Exodus 28:42–43 (C0301) but adds the wool ban.

new.title: Priests must not shave their heads and must keep them covered
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v44-13. Echoes Leviticus 21:5 (C0655), which concerns mourning.

new.title: The ruler worships at the east gate's threshold; the people bow there
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.recipient: the ruler and the people of the land
new.note: Inside broad ot-ezekiel-v46-1 (title covers only the gate's opening); first pass itemized 46:4–15 (B18 P02314). 46:3 outside candidate list.

new.title: The ruler's Sabbath burnt offering: six lambs and a ram
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v46-1 (46:1–13). Differs from Numbers 28:9–10 (C0928); cf. 45:17.

new.title: The new-moon offering: a calf, six lambs and a ram
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v46-1. Differs from Numbers 28:11–15 (C0929).

new.title: Festival worshippers leave by the opposite gate; the ruler goes with them
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.recipient: the ruler and the people of the land
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v46-1, whose title covers only the east gate.

new.title: Festival grain offerings: a cake for each calf and ram
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v46-1.

new.title: The east gate is opened for the ruler's freewill offering
new.speaker: the Lord through Ezekiel
new.note: Outside candidate list; inside broad record ot-ezekiel-v46-1; the gate is shut again after he leaves.

new.title: Daniel asks to be tested on legumes and water, not royal food
new.speaker: Daniel
new.note: Request to avoid defilement (1:8, outside candidate list) and the ten-day test (1:12–13); nothing in 1:6–21 is recorded.

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar examines the four youths and appoints them rulers
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Includes the king's order to bring them in (1:18).

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men tell and interpret his dream
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.recipient: the incantation-singers, magi, sorcerers and Chaldeans
new.note: Summons and demand under threat of death; distinct from the execution decree (2:13, ot-daniel-v2-13).

new.title: The Chaldeans ask the king to tell them his dream
new.speaker: the Chaldeans
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Ordinary request, repeated in 2:7.

new.title: Daniel asks the king for time to disclose the dream
new.speaker: Daniel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; reported request.

new.title: Daniel calls his companions to fast and seek God's help
new.speaker: Daniel
new.note: Outside candidate list; 'He called for fasting and supplication': a reported call to prayer.

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar orders sacrifices and libations offered to Daniel
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.note: Outside candidate list; reported order.

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar summons all officials to the golden image's dedication
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.recipient: the satraps, governors and officials of every nation
new.note: Outside candidate list; reported summons preceding the herald's decree (3:4–6, ot-daniel-v3-4).

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar orders the three to bow to the image or burn
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.note: Personal ultimatum, distinct from the general decree (3:4–6) and the accusers' citation (3:10).

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar orders the furnace heated and the three thrown in
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.note: The order is recalled at 3:22 and 3:24.

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar calls the three to come out of the fire
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; direct command.

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar decrees death for blaspheming the God of the three
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.note: Royal decree in 3:96 (context verse, outside candidate list); no record covers 3:91–97.

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar gives the three authority over the whole country
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life

new.title: An angel tells Nebuchadnezzar to serve and glorify the Most High
new.speaker: an angel from heaven
new.note: Direct heavenly command at his restoration (Old Greek).

new.title: Nebuchadnezzar condemns to death anyone who speaks against God
new.speaker: King Nebuchadnezzar
new.note: Royal pronouncement with his vow of sacrifice for himself and his people; distinct from the circular letter (4:37b, ot-daniel-v4-37b).

new.title: King Baltasar orders God's temple vessels brought for his banquet
new.speaker: King Baltasar (Belshazzar)
new.note: Wicked ruler's order profaning God's holy vessels; chapter 5 has no record.

new.title: Baltasar decrees a reward for whoever interprets the writing
new.speaker: King Baltasar (Belshazzar)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; summons plus 'the king issued a decree': purple, gold necklace, a third of the kingdom.

new.title: Baltasar summons the queen about the writing
new.speaker: King Baltasar (Belshazzar)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported summons.

new.title: Baltasar asks Daniel to interpret the writing, promising high rank
new.speaker: King Baltasar (Belshazzar)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Request phrased as a question with a promised reward; fulfilled at 5:29.

new.title: Baltasar gives Daniel authority over a third of the kingdom
new.speaker: King Baltasar (Belshazzar)
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; appointment to office, like 2:48–49 (AUD-31-2-48).

new.title: Darius appoints satraps and three leaders, Daniel among them
new.speaker: King Darius
new.recipient: 127 satraps and three leaders including Daniel
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; includes the king's plan to set Daniel over the whole kingdom (6:4–5).

new.title: Darius orders Daniel thrown into the lions' pit
new.speaker: King Darius
new.note: Outside candidate list; enforcement of the decree recorded at 6:10 (ot-daniel-v6-10).

new.title: A voice charges Gabriel to explain the vision to Daniel
new.speaker: a human voice from the Ulai
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; heavenly commission of an angel.

new.title: Blessed is the one who perseveres to the end of the days
new.speaker: the angelic messenger
new.note: Beatitude commending endurance to the 1,335th day.

new.title: An angel, as commanded, gives young Daniel a spirit of understanding
new.speaker: the Lord (reported)
new.note: Outside candidate list; reported commission of an angel, like Bel 1:34 (ot-daniel-bel-v1-34).

new.title: Daniel asks the king for authority to kill the dragon
new.speaker: Daniel
new.note: Request granted in 1:26 ('It is granted to you').

new.title: The king hands Daniel over to destruction under the crowd's pressure
new.speaker: the king of Babylon
new.recipient: his companions, before the hostile crowd
new.note: Royal sentence like first-pass Daniel 6:15 (B18 P02341); the crowds then throw Daniel into the lions' pit (1:31–32).

new.title: The hearer is told to begin harvesting when captivity is reversed
new.speaker: the Lord through Hosea
new.note: Figurative imperative in the oracle (cf. Micah 4:13 Command, Joel 4:13 Study Context); include only if such harvest summonses are recorded.

new.title: Joel calls drunkards to sober up and weep over lost wine
new.speaker: the Lord through Joel
new.recipient: drunkards and all who drink wine to intoxication
new.note: First summons to lament in Joel 1; the later summonses (1:9, 1:11, 1:13–14) are already recorded.

new.title: Joel calls the people to lament like a bride in sackcloth
new.speaker: the Lord through Joel
new.note: Distinct summons to lament between 1:5 and the priests’ call at 1:9.

new.title: The Lord ironically bids that Israel’s love of these rites be announced
new.speaker: the Lord through Amos
new.recipient: the sons of Israel worshipping at Bethel and Gilgal
new.note: Ironic imperative exposing Bethel and Gilgal worship; low because it reads more as indictment than direction.

new.title: Israel is told to prepare to call upon its God
new.speaker: the Lord through Amos
new.note: Climactic summons after the refrain ‘you did not turn to Me’ (4:6–11); Amos 4 has no record beyond 4:1.

new.title: In an evil time the prudent keep silent
new.speaker: Amos, for the Lord
new.note: Outside candidate list (context verse): a maxim between the indictment (5:12) and the call to seek good (ot-amos-v5-14).

new.title: Woe to those who long for the Lord’s day: it is darkness
new.speaker: Amos, delivering the Lord’s word
new.recipient: Israelites who desire the Lord’s day
new.note: Woe warning against presumption, comparable to recorded woes (Amos 6:1–7, Isaiah 5:20–24); 5:19–20 complete the image.

new.title: The Lord teaches Jonah to share His compassion for Nineveh
new.speaker: the Lord
new.note: Closing lesson of the gourd, a teaching question like recorded Zechariah 7:5 and Malachi 1:9; Jonah 4 has no records.

new.title: The Lord calls His people to remember Balak’s plot and Balaam’s answer
new.speaker: the Lord through Micah
new.note: Command to the people within the Lord’s case; ot-micah-v6-1 (6:1–3) covers only the summons to the mountains.

new.title: The Lord’s voice summons the tribe to hear
new.speaker: the Lord’s voice through Micah
new.note: Summons opening the indictment of 6:10–16; similar summonses are sometimes Study Context (Amos 3:1, Micah 3:9).

new.title: The Lord bids the despisers look and marvel at His unbelievable work
new.speaker: the Lord, answering Habakkuk
new.note: Summons to scoffers; Paul quotes it as a warning in Acts 13:40–41, which also has no record.

new.title: Woe to one who makes his neighbour drunk to see his shame
new.speaker: the peoples’ taunt within the Lord’s answer
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Fourth woe of the series; AUD-39-2-6 covers only the first three (2:6–12). Extending that record is the alternative.

new.title: Zephaniah calls for reverence before the Lord, for His day is near
new.speaker: the Lord through Zephaniah
new.note: Same kind of call as Habakkuk 2:20 (ot-habakkuk-v2-20, Command); Zephaniah 1 has no records.

new.title: The inhabitants of the battered quarter are told to lament
new.speaker: the Lord through Zephaniah
new.recipient: inhabitants of the battered place, the traders’ quarter
new.note: Prophetic summons to wail over the destroyed traders; such summonses are in scope (Joel 1:11 is recorded).

new.title: The Lord sends horsemen to patrol the earth
new.speaker: the Lord (reported by the man among the mountains)
new.recipient: the horsemen in Zechariah's night vision
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported sending, like ot-zechariah-v6-7 (gray horses sent through the earth); 1:11 reports the patrol completed.

new.title: Daughter Zion is called to rejoice, for the Lord comes to dwell
new.speaker: the Lord through Zechariah
new.note: Context line not flagged as a candidate; compare Zechariah 9:9 (ot-zechariah-v9-9), recorded as a Command.

new.title: Joshua the high priest is charged to keep God's ways and court
new.speaker: the angel of the Lord, for the Lord Almighty
new.note: Conditional charge: walk in My ways, keep My commands, guard My court, and you will govern My house. Follows ot-zechariah-v3-4.

new.title: Not by might or strength but by My Spirit, says the Lord
new.speaker: the Lord, through the angel speaking to Zechariah
new.note: The Lord’s word to Zerubbabel (4:6 is a context line); Zechariah 4 has no records.

new.title: Do not despise the day of small beginnings
new.speaker: the Lord through Zechariah
new.recipient: the returned community rebuilding the temple
new.note: Teaching rhetorical question (‘who treated the small days with contempt?’), like recorded Zechariah 7:5.

new.title: Sarasar and Arbeseer send to entreat the Lord and ask the priests
new.speaker: Sarasar, King Arbeseer and his men
new.recipient: the priests and prophets of the Lord's house
new.note: Envoys sent to seek the Lord, like ot-2-kings-v22-13; the Greek blurs their fifth-month fasting question, which 7:5 answers.

new.title: The shepherd asks to be paid his wages, if they see fit
new.speaker: Zechariah, acting as the shepherd
new.recipient: those who traded in the flock
new.note: Request that yields the thirty silver pieces; the next direction (11:13) is recorded as ot-zechariah-v11-13.

new.title: The Lord will send Elijah to turn hearts before His day
new.speaker: the Lord Almighty through Malachi
new.note: Promised sending with a charge, like 3:1 (linked via AUD-46-7-24); Luke 1:17 and Matthew 17:10–13 also lack records.

new.title: John the Baptist calls Judea to repent as the kingdom nears
new.speaker: John the Baptist
new.recipient: the people coming to him in the wilderness of Judea
new.note: Same words as Jesus’ call (K029) but a distinct speaker; origin follows AUD-44-3-7. Luke 3:3 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Jesus tells John to allow His baptism to fulfil all righteousness
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Unique to Matthew; John’s attempt to prevent Him (3:14) is the occasion.

new.title: The Father anoints Jesus with the Spirit and names Him beloved Son
new.speaker: God the Father, a voice from the heavens
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: Declaration rather than order: the Spirit's anointing (cf. AUD-46-4-16) in Isaiah 42:1's words (first-pass B16 P01992). Mark, Luke parallel.

new.title: The devil demands Jesus make bread, leap down and worship him
new.speaker: the devil (the tempter)
new.note: Hostile directives, recorded as for wicked rulers; no origin value fits the devil. Luke 4:3–9 demands are also unrecorded.

new.title: Jesus commands Satan to go away
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Jesus’ own dismissal, distinct from the quoted law; Matthew 16:23 // Mark 8:33 (‘Get behind me, Satan’) are also unrecorded.

new.title: Jesus sends the centurion home: as you believed, let it be
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: The centurion episode (Matthew 8:5–13 // Luke 7:1–10) has no record at all.

new.title: Jesus tells the paralytic to take courage, for his sins are forgiven
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: ‘Take courage’ sayings are recorded elsewhere (K082); Mark 2:5 and Luke 5:20 lack the imperative and have no record.

new.title: Jesus sternly charges two healed blind men to tell no one
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Includes ‘According to your faith, let it happen for you’; secrecy orders are recorded elsewhere (AUD-44-12-15). Their cry is a petition.

new.title: Expect allegiance to Jesus to divide even households
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 12:49–53; 10:35–36 echo Micah 7:6.

new.title: Whoever is not with Jesus is against him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the Pharisees attributing his exorcisms to Beelzebul
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 11:17–26; Mark 3:22–27 (candidate 3:27) is the same teaching.

new.title: Repent at Jesus' preaching as Nineveh repented at Jonah's
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: scribes and Pharisees asking for a sign
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 11:29–32; Matthew adds the three days and nights in the sea creature (12:40).

new.title: Let wheat and darnel grow together until the harvest
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the crowds; explained to the disciples
new.note: Parable of the darnel and its explanation have no record; only the closing formula (13:43) is linked, on AUD-45-4-23.

new.title: The mustard seed and leaven show the kingdom's hidden growth
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 13:18–21; Mark 4:30–32 (candidate 4:30) is the mustard-seed parallel.

new.title: The dragnet shows the final separation of the evil from the righteous
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Dragnet parable has no record; it sits between AUD-44-13-44 (13:44–46) and AUD-44-13-51 (13:51–52).

new.title: Herodias' daughter, prompted by her mother, demands John's head
new.speaker: Herodias’ daughter, prompted by Herodias
new.note: Herod's rash oath (14:7) invites the request; C0586 covers only John's rebuke (14:3–4). Mark 6:21–25 is the parallel.

new.title: Herod orders John the Baptist beheaded in prison
new.speaker: Herod the tetrarch
new.note: Reported royal order, like AUD-44-2-16 (the boys of Bethlehem); Mark 6:26–28 names the executioner.

new.title: Jesus makes the disciples sail ahead while he dismisses the crowds
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported order after the feeding (AUD-46-9-13 ends at 14:21); Mark 6:45–46 is the parallel.

new.title: Jesus tells the disciples on the sea not to fear
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record John 6:16–21; Mark 6:50 (candidate) has the same word.

new.title: Jesus bids Peter come to him on the water
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Peter asks to be commanded and Jesus says 'Come'; 'Lord, save me' is a petition. Unique to Matthew; ends with the little-faith rebuke.

new.title: Leave the blind guides: if the blind lead the blind, both fall
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the disciples, about the offended Pharisees
new.note: Unique to Matthew in this setting; Luke 6:39 has the proverb in the Sermon on the Plain (see this batch's K050 finding).

new.title: Jesus grants the Canaanite woman's plea: let it be as you wish
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: a Canaanite woman from the region of Tyre and Sidon
new.note: Episode has no record; her cries are petitions, the disciples ask 'Dismiss her' (15:23). Mark 7:24–30 is the parallel.

new.title: Interpret the present time as you read the weather
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: Pharisees and Sadducees asking for a sign
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 12:54–56; outside candidate list. 16:4 repeats the sign-of-Jonah refusal of 12:39.

new.title: Jesus rebukes Peter: Get behind me, Satan
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Peter's protest against the passion prediction is rebuked; Mark 8:31–33 (candidates) is the parallel. B19 noted it unrecorded.

new.title: Peter proposes making three tents on the mountain
new.speaker: Peter
new.note: Parallel of first-pass B20 P02636 (Mark 9:5–6) and P02706 (Luke 9:32–33); the Father's voice (AUD-44-17-5) interrupts it.

new.title: Jesus has the convulsed boy brought and rebukes the unclean spirit
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the boy’s father and the crowd; the demon
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 9:41–42; the father's plea (17:15) is a petition.

new.title: Agree in prayer: Jesus is present where two or three gather
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Outside candidate list; no record covers 18:19–20. K105 (18:18) is Study Context, so it is not extended here.

new.title: Do not begrudge God's generosity: the last will be first
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Parable of the labourers in the vineyard has no record; covers candidates 20:6–8 and 20:14 (P02557).

new.title: Zebedee's sons ask for the places of honour in the kingdom
new.speaker: the mother of Zebedee’s sons, with James and John
new.note: Ordinary request answered with the cup saying; leads into K054. Mark 10:35–40 (candidates 10:37–38) is the parallel.

new.title: Jesus has the blind man brought and tells him to receive sight
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: two blind men near Jericho, and the crowd
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 18:40–42; the crowd silences the two men's cries (petitions) and Jesus calls them.

new.title: The chief priests object to the children's hosannas in the temple
new.speaker: the chief priests and scribes
new.note: Implied demand to silence the praise; Jesus answers with Greek Psalm 8:3. Compare proposed B21 record Luke 19:37–40, a different occasion.

new.title: Jesus answers the challenge to his authority with John's baptism
new.speaker: Jesus, challenged by the chief priests and elders
new.recipient: the chief priests and elders of the people
new.note: Their demand (21:23) and his counter-question; covers candidate 21:27 (P02564). Mark 11:27–33 is the parallel; AUD-44-21-28 follows.

new.title: The parable of the tenants warns those who reject the owner's son
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the chief priests and the Pharisees
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 20:9–19; covers candidates 21:37–38 and 21:41–42 (P02566, P02567).

new.title: Do not refuse God's great supper with excuses
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the chief priests and the Pharisees
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 14:15–24; Matthew adds the wedding garment (22:11–14). Covers candidates in P02569 and P02570.

new.title: Know the Scriptures and God's power: He is God of the living
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the Sadducees, who deny the resurrection
new.note: Jesus' answer has no record; only the Sadducees' question is linked (S156). Mark 12:24–27 and Luke 20:34–38 parallel it (this batch).

new.title: Woe to lawyers who take away the key of knowledge
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 11:52; in Matthew they shut the kingdom and block those entering.

new.title: Woe to those who make converts twice sons of Gehenna
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Unique to Matthew; the other woes are recorded (K025, AUD-44-23-16, AUD-44-23-25) or proposed by B21 from Luke 11.

new.title: Woe to those who build prophets' tombs yet share their killers' guilt
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 11:47–51; includes 'fill up the measure of your fathers' and the sending of prophets (23:34).

new.title: The council plots Jesus' arrest by stealth, avoiding the feast
new.speaker: the chief priests and elders, gathered at Caiaphas’ court
new.note: A recorded plot, like Genesis 37:20 (ot-genesis-v37-20); Mark 14:1–2 (candidate 14:1) is the parallel.

new.title: Judas offers to hand Jesus over to the chief priests for money
new.speaker: Judas Iscariot
new.note: A proposal like Judah's (Genesis 37:27, ot-genesis-v37-27); Mark 14:10–11 and Luke 22:3–6 are parallels.

new.title: Woe to the one who hands over the Son of Man
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: A woe, but a judgment on the betrayer rather than counsel; Mark 14:17–21 (candidate 14:21) is the parallel.

new.title: Judas signals the arrest with a kiss: 'Seize him'
new.speaker: Judas Iscariot
new.recipient: the armed crowd from the chief priests and elders
new.note: Includes Jesus' 'Friend, do what you have come for' (26:50); Mark 14:43–46 is the parallel.

new.title: The council condemns Jesus as liable to death for blasphemy
new.speaker: Caiaphas the high priest and the council
new.note: False witnesses, the high priest's adjuration (26:63) and verdict (26:66); compare AUD-47-19-6. Covers 26:65 (P02592); Mark 14:55–64 parallels.

new.title: Jesus' captors strike him and demand, 'Prophesy!'
new.speaker: those holding Jesus at the high priest’s house
new.note: Mocking demand, in scope only if taunts count as directions; Mark 14:65 is the parallel. Peter's denials (26:69–75) are out of scope.

new.title: Pilate's wife warns him to have nothing to do with Jesus
new.speaker: Pilate’s wife
new.note: A message sent to the judgment seat after her dream; unique to Matthew.

new.title: Pilate sentences Jesus to crucifixion at the crowd's demand
new.speaker: Pilate
new.note: parallel to proposed B21 record Luke 23:22–25; he washes his hands, 'See to it yourselves' (27:24), releases Barabbas and hands Jesus over.

new.title: Soldiers compel Simon of Cyrene to carry Jesus' cross
new.speaker: the governor’s soldiers
new.note: Outside candidate list; a reported requisition (compare Matthew 5:41). Mark 15:21 and Luke 23:26 are parallels; 27:29 is mockery.

new.title: Passers-by and leaders taunt Jesus to come down from the cross
new.speaker: passers-by, the chief priests, scribes and elders, and the robbers
new.note: Taunting demands echoing the tempter's 'If you are God's Son' (Matthew 4:3, 6); include only if hostile taunts are recorded. Mark 15:29–32 parallels.

new.title: Bystanders say, 'Leave it; let us see whether Elijah comes'
new.speaker: bystanders at the cross
new.note: A 'let us' resolution like those recorded at Genesis 11:3; Jesus' cry (27:46) is prayer. Mark 15:34–36 is the parallel.

new.title: Joseph of Arimathea asks Pilate for Jesus' body
new.speaker: Joseph of Arimathea
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Parallel of first-pass B20 P02668 (Mark 15:42–46), whose note names it; here Pilate orders the body given.

new.title: Jesus has his disciples keep a boat ready against the crowd
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported order, unique to Mark; compare B19's proposed Matthew 8:18 crossing order.

new.title: The kingdom grows unseen, like seed, until the harvest
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Outside candidate list; the seed growing by itself, a parable unique to Mark, has no record.

new.title: Jesus orders His disciples to cross to the other side
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: parallel to proposed B19 record Matthew 8:18; 'Let us cross to the other side.' Luke 8:22 (candidate) is the same.

new.title: Jesus rebukes His disciples’ fear and little faith in the storm
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: parallel to proposed B19 record Matthew 8:25–26; 'Be silent; be still' (4:39) addresses the wind and sea.

new.title: Jesus sends the pleading demons out into the herd of pigs
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the unclean spirits (Legion) in the Gerasene man
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: parallel to proposed B19 record Matthew 8:31–32; 'Come out of the man, unclean spirit!' (5:8). Covers candidate 5:12 (P02620).

new.title: The townspeople beg Jesus to leave their territory
new.speaker: the people of the region
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: parallel to proposed B19 record Matthew 8:34; the eyewitnesses' report (5:16) prompts the request (5:17).

new.title: The Twelve go out proclaiming that people should repent
new.speaker: the Twelve
new.recipient: the people of the towns they visit
new.note: Reported call to repent, like first-pass Matthew 3:1–2 and Acts 26:19–20; carries out K096/K097. Luke 9:6 is similar.

new.title: Jesus tells the apostles to come away and rest a while
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the apostles returning from their mission
new.note: Unique to Mark; given on the apostles' return, before the feeding (AUD-46-9-13 links Mark 6:34–44).

new.title: Jesus says 'Ephphatha' to a deaf man and orders silence
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: a deaf man with a speech impediment, and the onlookers
new.note: Unique to Mark; the healing word and the secrecy order (7:36), like AUD-44-12-15, have no record.

new.title: Jesus sends the healed blind man home: do not enter the village
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Unique to Mark; a two-stage healing with 'Do you see anything?' (8:23) and the order of 8:26.

new.title: This kind can come out only by prayer
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Outside candidate list; Jesus' private answer about the failed exorcism has no record. Matthew 17:19–20 answers with mustard-seed faith (K071).

new.title: God sends the angel Gabriel to Mary in Nazareth
new.speaker: God
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: Sending of an angel, like first-pass Daniel 8:16 (B18 P02345); first pass widens AUD-46-1-30 back only to 1:28. Luke 1:19 likewise unrecorded.

new.title: The angel tells the shepherds not to fear, giving a sign
new.speaker: an angel of the Lord
new.recipient: shepherds in the fields near Bethlehem
new.note: Includes the shepherds' 'Let us go over to Bethlehem and see' (2:15), carried out in 2:16–17. Covers P02683.

new.title: A prophet is not without honour except in his homeland
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Includes 'Physician, heal yourself' and the Elijah and Elisha examples; Mark 6:1–6 and Matthew 13:54–58 are parallels.

new.title: Jesus tells Simon to put out deep and lower the nets
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: K035 links only 5:8–11; the fishing order precedes the call. Compare proposed B21 record John 21:4–13. Covers 5:7 (P02692).

new.title: Wisdom is vindicated though this generation rejects John and Jesus
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: parallel to proposed B20 record Matthew 11:16–19; 7:29–30 contrast the baptized tax collectors with the Pharisees.

new.title: Jesus tells the healed woman to take courage: her faith saved her
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the woman with the flow of blood
new.note: parallel to proposed B19 record Matthew 9:20–22; Luke: 'Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace.'

new.title: Jesus tells the disciples to let his betrayal prediction sink in
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: 'Place these words in your ears'; parallels Matthew 17:22–23 and Mark 9:30–32 are unrecorded.

new.title: Jesus rebukes James and John for wanting fire on a Samaritan village
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Rebuke is narrated, not quoted; it forbids retaliation against a village that refused Jesus.

new.title: Count the cost: the Son of Man has nowhere to rest
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Parallel of first-pass B19 P02511 (Matthew 8:19–20), whose note flags this verse; K038 begins at 9:59.

new.title: Woe to the towns that saw Jesus' mighty works without repenting
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum (spoken to the seventy-two)
new.note: Woes are in scope as Wisdom; parallel Matthew 11:20–24 is also unrecorded.

new.title: Jesus gives the seventy-two authority over snakes, scorpions and the enemy
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: 10:19 (outside candidate list) hands on authority; K101 (10:20) follows and AUD-46-10-1 holds the sending.

new.title: Blessed are the eyes that see what the disciples see
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Beatitude; parallel Matthew 13:16–17 is also unrecorded. 10:21–22 is prayer to the Father, out of scope.

new.title: God knows hearts; what people exalt is abomination before Him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Rebuke of self-justification before people; no record covers Luke 16:14–17 (K077 and K075 end at 16:13).

new.title: The kingdom is preached since John, yet no stroke of Law falls
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Counterparts: Matthew 11:12–13 (first pass links it to AUD-46-7-24) and 5:18 (only Study Context K001). Link there if preferred.

new.title: Heed Moses and the Prophets before it is too late
new.speaker: Jesus (Abraham speaking in the parable)
new.note: Rich man and Lazarus parable has no record; 16:29 'let them hear them' is its directive.

new.title: Do not seek God's kingdom in visible signs; it is within you
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the Pharisees asking when the kingdom comes
new.note: No record; the warning to the disciples that follows (17:22–25) is AUD-44-24-23.

new.title: Jesus tells Zacchaeus to hurry down because he must stay with him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Zacchaeus episode has no record; his pledge of fourfold restitution (19:8) belongs in it.

new.title: Pharisees demand that Jesus rebuke his disciples' praise
new.speaker: some Pharisees in the crowd
new.note: 19:37–38 is praise, out of scope; the Pharisees' demand (19:39) and Jesus' refusal could be recorded.

new.title: Pilate sends Jesus to Herod on learning He is a Galilean
new.speaker: Pilate
new.note: Jurisdictional referral found only in Luke; Herod sends Him back (23:11). Custody orders are itemized elsewhere, e.g. first-pass Acts 23:34–35.

new.title: Believe all that the prophets spoke about the Christ's suffering
new.speaker: the risen Jesus
new.recipient: two disciples on the road to Emmaus
new.topic: Minor Teachings: The Scriptures Read in Christ
new.note: Emmaus rebuke and Scripture interpretation have no record; compare AUD-46-24-5 (remember his words).

new.title: The Emmaus disciples urge the stranger to stay with them
new.speaker: Cleopas and his companion
new.note: Ordinary hospitality request, comparable to recorded Old Testament hospitality requests.

new.title: The risen Jesus tells the disciples to see and touch him
new.speaker: the risen Jesus
new.recipient: the Eleven and those with them
new.note: Includes his request for food (24:41); same evening as John 20:19–20. Compare AUD-47-20-24 (Thomas).

new.title: Jerusalem's leaders send priests and Levites to question John
new.speaker: the Jews of Jerusalem, from the Pharisees
new.recipient: priests and Levites sent to John
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 1:19–22 outside candidate list (linked only to ot-isaiah-v40-3 for the voice saying); 1:22 'those who sent us'; 1:24 sent from the Pharisees.

new.title: Jesus invites John's two disciples to come and see
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: Andrew and another disciple of John
new.note: Call of Andrew and another disciple; the recorded call of Philip (AUD-47-1-43) follows.

new.title: Jesus gives Simon the name Cephas, that is, Peter
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: Divine renamings are itemized (C0034 Abraham, C0058 Israel); Mark 3:16 and Matthew 16:18 records do not itemize it.

new.title: Philip invites Nathanael to come and see Jesus
new.speaker: Philip
new.note: A disciple's invitation, echoing Jesus' 'come and see' (1:39).

new.title: Mary tells the servants to do whatever Jesus tells them
new.speaker: Mary, the mother of Jesus
new.recipient: the servants at the wedding in Cana
new.note: Distinct speaker from Jesus' own instructions in AUD-47-2-7 (2:7–8).

new.title: Whoever does the truth comes to the light
new.speaker: Jesus (or the evangelist)
new.note: Declarative teaching on conduct; compare AUD-47-12-34 (walk in the light).

new.title: He must increase, but I must decrease
new.speaker: John the Baptist
new.note: John's maxim of self-effacement before Christ, closing his answer to his disciples.

new.title: Jesus asks the Samaritan woman for a drink
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well
new.note: An ordinary request of the kind the catalogue records; it crosses the Jewish–Samaritan divide.

new.title: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman to call her husband
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Direct order that exposes her situation and leads to the worship teaching (K026).

new.title: The Samaritan woman invites her townspeople to come and see Jesus
new.speaker: the Samaritan woman
new.note: Her testimony leads many Samaritans to believe (4:39–42).

new.title: Jesus tells the royal official to go, for his son lives
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: a royal official whose son lay ill in Capernaum
new.note: Healing word like AUD-46-7-11; 4:47 and 4:49 are petitions to Jesus, out of scope.

new.title: Jesus answers Sabbath critics: my Father is working, and I work
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the Jews persecuting him over a Sabbath healing
new.note: John 5's Sabbath dispute lacks the Sabbath-teaching record other controversies have (K013, K014, AUD-46-13-10, K015).

new.title: Jesus tells the crowd to stop grumbling among themselves
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Includes the Prophets quotation 'they shall all be taught by God' (6:45).

new.title: Jesus' brothers urge him to go to Judea and show himself
new.speaker: Jesus' brothers
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Unbelieving advice; Jesus declines, saying his time has not yet come, and sends them up to the feast.

new.title: The chief priests and Pharisees rebuke officers for not seizing Jesus
new.speaker: the chief priests and Pharisees
new.note: The arrest order itself (7:32) is also unrecorded; compare AUD-47-11-55.

new.title: Abraham's true children do Abraham's works
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the Jews who claimed Abraham as their father
new.note: 8:42 adds 'If God were your Father, you would love Me.' Compare AUD-44-3-7 on presuming descent from Abraham.

new.title: Admit blindness; those who claim to see remain in sin
new.speaker: Jesus
new.recipient: the healed man and the Pharisees with him
new.note: Includes the call to believe in the Son of Man (9:35–38); a judgment saying on spiritual blindness.

new.title: Enter through Jesus, the door, and follow the shepherd's voice
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Shepherd-and-door figure has no record; AUD-47-10-14 begins at 10:14. Covers candidate 10:9–10 (P02795).

new.title: Jesus tells the disciples they will return to Judea for Lazarus
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Direction to go back despite the threat of stoning; 11:9–10 is reported separately.

new.title: Thomas urges the disciples to go and die with Jesus
new.speaker: Thomas called Didymus
new.note: A disciple's exhortation to follow Jesus into danger.

new.title: Martha tells Mary that the Teacher is here and calls her
new.speaker: Jesus, his summons relayed by Martha
new.note: Relayed summons; Mary rises quickly and goes to him (11:29). Compare the summons in B20 P02645 (Mark 10:49).

new.title: Caiaphas counsels that one man should die for the nation
new.speaker: Caiaphas the high priest
new.recipient: the council of chief priests and Pharisees
new.note: Council counsel recorded like Gamaliel's (AUD-48-5-34); it leads to the plot (11:53) and AUD-47-11-55.

new.title: Greeks at the feast ask Philip to let them see Jesus
new.speaker: some Greeks who came up to worship at the feast
new.note: Ordinary request, passed through Andrew to Jesus; it occasions AUD-47-12-23 (12:23–26).

new.title: Jesus tells Judas to do quickly what he is about to do
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 13:29: the disciples assumed an errand, buying for the feast or giving to the poor.

new.title: Jesus tells the disciples to rise and leave with him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Spoken as he goes to do 'just as the Father commanded Me'.

new.title: Remember that the world hated Jesus before it hated you
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Compare AUD-47-16-1 (remember the warning) and Matthew 10:24–25; the slave-and-master saying recalls 13:16.

new.title: Jesus tells the high priest to question those who heard him
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: Appeal to proper testimony, comparable to AUD-47-7-50; 18:23 asks for testimony about any wrong spoken.

new.title: Annas sends Jesus bound to Caiaphas the high priest
new.speaker: Annas
new.note: Reported transfer between hearings; similar transfers (Luke 23:7, Pilate sends Jesus to Herod) are also unrecorded.

new.title: Everyone who is from the truth hears Jesus' voice
new.speaker: Jesus
new.note: With Jesus' stated purpose, to bear witness to the truth; compare John 8:47 and 10:27 in first-pass findings.

new.title: Pilate offers the Passover custom of releasing one prisoner
new.speaker: Pilate
new.note: Custom with legal force, like AUD-48-25-13; parallels Matthew 27:15 and Mark 15:6 are unrecorded.

new.title: The chief priests ask Pilate to reword the inscription on the cross
new.speaker: the chief priests
new.note: Pilate refuses: 'What I have written, I have written.'

new.title: The soldiers agree to cast lots for Jesus' seamless tunic
new.speaker: the soldiers at the cross
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: A 'let us' resolution, as the catalogue records Genesis 11:3; fulfils Greek Psalm 21:19.

new.title: The Jews ask Pilate to break the legs and remove the bodies
new.speaker: the Jewish authorities
new.note: Outside candidate list; grounded in Deuteronomy 21:23 (C1120) and the coming Sabbath; the soldiers carry it out (19:32–33).

new.title: Mary asks the supposed gardener where he has laid Jesus
new.speaker: Mary Magdalene
new.recipient: the risen Jesus, taken for the gardener
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Ordinary request; the commission that follows is AUD-47-20-16.

new.title: The risen Jesus directs the catch and invites the disciples to breakfast
new.speaker: the risen Jesus
new.recipient: seven disciples fishing on the Sea of Tiberias
new.note: Cast the net (21:6), bring fish (21:10), come and eat (21:12); compare Luke 5:4, also unrecorded.

new.title: Angels ask the disciples why they stand gazing into heaven
new.speaker: two men in white (angels)
new.note: Rhetorical rebuke with a promise of return; in scope only if read as a direction to stop gazing.

new.title: Do not lie to the Holy Spirit about what you give
new.speaker: Peter
new.note: Peter's rebukes (5:3–4,9): the property was theirs to keep; the sin was lying to God.

new.title: Stephen's opponents set up false witnesses against him
new.speaker: Stephen's opponents
new.note: Suborned false testimony, contrary to the false-witness law (C0157); recorded only as a hostile direction.

new.title: Moses urges two quarrelling Israelites to stop wronging each other
new.speaker: Moses, recalled by Stephen
new.topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
new.note: Its source, Exodus 2:13–14, is also unrecorded; the wrongdoer rejects Moses as ruler and judge.

new.title: The Ethiopian official stops the chariot and asks to be baptized
new.speaker: the Ethiopian eunuch
new.note: Reported order and request; the commission to Philip (AUD-48-8-26) ends at 8:35.

new.title: God shows no partiality but accepts all who fear Him
new.speaker: Peter
new.note: Outside candidate list; Peter's opening maxim: in every nation whoever fears God and practices righteousness is acceptable to Him.

new.title: Peter tells the believers to inform James of his release
new.speaker: Peter
new.recipient: the believers gathered at Mary's house
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Report these things to James and the brothers', given after the angel's rescue (AUD-48-12-6).

new.title: Herod orders the guards led away for execution
new.speaker: Herod (Agrippa)
new.note: Reported hostile order, like AUD-44-2-16 (Herod and the boys of Bethlehem).

new.title: Tyre and Sidon win over Blastus and ask Herod for peace
new.speaker: the people of Tyre and Sidon
new.note: Outside candidate list; a diplomatic request, since their food came from the king's territory; it leads to Herod's address (12:21–23).

new.title: Paul rebukes Elymas for opposing the faith and pronounces blindness
new.speaker: Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit
new.note: 'Will you not stop making crooked the Lord's straight ways?' is the implied directive; the blindness is judgment.

new.title: Synagogue rulers invite Paul and Barnabas to speak a word of encouragement
new.speaker: the synagogue rulers at Pisidian Antioch
new.note: Shows synagogue order: reading of the law and prophets, then exhortation; Paul answers 'listen' (13:16).
