new.title: Believe the proclaimed forgiveness and beware of scoffing at God's work
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul's sermon (13:16–41) has no record before 13:43; quotes Habakkuk 1:5, itself unrecorded. 13:42 is the hearers' request.

new.title: Paul tells the man lame from birth to stand upright
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: a man lame from birth at Lystra
new.note: Healing order like AUD-48-3-4 and AUD-48-9-32; it prompts the Lystra episode (AUD-48-14-11).

new.title: Paul and Barnabas appoint elders in every church with fasting
new.speaker: Paul and Barnabas
new.recipient: elders of the churches of Lystra, Iconium and Antioch
new.note: AUD-48-14-21's note mentions this appointment, but no record itemizes it; compare Titus 1:5 (AUD-60-1-5).

new.title: Do not test God by putting the yoke on Gentile disciples
new.speaker: Peter
new.recipient: the apostles and elders in council
new.topic: Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On
new.note: Peter's council speech: all are saved through grace; it precedes James' decree (A111).

new.title: Paul proposes to Barnabas revisiting the churches they planted
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Leads to the dispute over John Mark and the separation of Paul and Barnabas.

new.title: Lydia urges Paul's company to stay at her house
new.speaker: Lydia of Thyatira
new.note: Hospitality request after her household's baptism.

new.title: The Philippian magistrates order Paul and Silas beaten and jailed
new.speaker: the magistrates of Philippi
new.note: Reported orders (16:22–23) after the charge of unlawful customs (16:20–21); the jailer obeys (16:24).

new.title: Thessalonian officials take security from Jason before releasing the accused
new.speaker: the city officials of Thessalonica
new.note: Outside candidate list; the charge of acting against Caesar's decrees (17:7) is answered with a surety bond.

new.title: Thessalonian brothers send Paul and Silas away by night to Berea
new.speaker: the brothers at Thessalonica
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Protective dispatch like 17:14 (within B22 P02876) and Acts 9:30 (also unrecorded).

new.title: Receive the word eagerly and examine the Scriptures daily, like the Bereans
new.speaker: Luke, the narrator
new.recipient: readers; the Berean Jews as example
new.note: Outside candidate list; the narrator commends the Bereans as noble-minded. Example-based Wisdom like AUD-48-4-32.

new.title: Paul sends word for Silas and Timothy to join him quickly
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: Silas and Timothy, via the escorts returning from Athens
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list (Acts 17:4–26 falls between batches). 17:14: the Berean brothers send Paul off toward the sea.

new.title: Athenian philosophers ask Paul to explain his new teaching
new.speaker: Epicurean and Stoic philosophers at Athens
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 17:20–21 outside candidate list; occasions the Areopagus speech (AUD-48-17-29); compare B21 P02865 (13:15) and B22 P02908 (28:22).

new.title: Ephesian Jews ask Paul to stay; he promises to return, God willing
new.speaker: the Jews of the synagogue at Ephesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 18:20 outside candidate list; hospitality request like B21 P02873 (Lydia); Paul's 'God willing' practices James 4:15 (AUD-63-4-13).

new.title: Ephesian believers write asking the Achaian disciples to welcome Apollos
new.speaker: the brothers at Ephesus
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Outside candidate list; a letter of recommendation, compare AUD-49-16-1 (Phoebe) and AUD-50-16-10 (Timothy).

new.title: Renounce magic openly, as the Ephesian believers burned their books
new.speaker: Luke, the narrator
new.recipient: readers; the Ephesian believers as example
new.note: Outside candidate list; confession and burning of magic books as a model of repentance.

new.title: Paul sends Timothy and Erastus ahead to Macedonia
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: 19:22 is outside candidate list; 19:21 gives Paul's Spirit-led resolve to go to Jerusalem and then Rome.

new.title: Disciples and friendly Asiarchs urge Paul not to enter the theater
new.speaker: the disciples and some Asiarchs
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported restraint and urging, like AUD-48-21-4 (disciples urge Paul not to enter Jerusalem).

new.title: Paul tells the Troas believers not to be alarmed over Eutychus
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Spoken as Paul embraces the fallen young man, who is restored; compare AUD-48-9-36 (Tabitha, rise).

new.title: Paul summons the Ephesian elders to meet him at Miletus
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the elders of the church at Ephesus
new.note: Reported summons that occasions the Miletus charge (AUD-48-20-24, A062).

new.title: Jews from Asia rouse the crowd to seize Paul in the temple
new.speaker: Jews from Asia
new.recipient: the men of Israel at the temple
new.note: Outside candidate list; 'Men of Israel, help!' with the charge of bringing Greeks into the temple.

new.title: Tribune orders Paul bound with two chains and taken to the barracks
new.speaker: Claudius Lysias, the tribune
new.note: 21:34 (outside candidate list) adds the order to bring Paul into the barracks.

new.title: Paul asks the tribune for permission to address the people
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Request granted at 21:40; Paul then asks the crowd to hear his defense (22:1).

new.title: Paul asks the Jerusalem crowd to hear his defense
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the crowd at the temple in Jerusalem
new.note: B22 P02888 (21:37–40) mentions this request; widen it to 21:37–22:2 or keep separate like B22 P02903 (26:1–3).

new.title: The crowd demands that Paul be removed from the earth
new.speaker: the Jerusalem crowd
new.note: Repeats the cry 'Away with him!' (21:36, outside candidate list).

new.title: The tribune orders the chief priests and council to assemble
new.speaker: the tribune
new.recipient: the chief priests and the whole council
new.note: Convened to learn the accusation; Paul is set before them (23:1–10).

new.title: The high priest Ananias orders Paul struck on the mouth
new.speaker: Ananias the high priest
new.note: Paul protests that the order violates the law (23:3); 23:4–5 is already linked to C0209.

new.title: The tribune orders troops to snatch Paul from the divided council
new.speaker: the tribune

new.title: Conspirators vow to kill Paul and ask the council to summon him
new.speaker: more than forty Jewish conspirators
new.note: Includes their oath under a curse to neither eat nor drink (23:12–14); AUD-48-23-16 begins when the plot is disclosed.

new.title: Felix orders Paul held in Herod's praetorium until his accusers arrive
new.speaker: Felix the governor

new.title: Tertullus asks Felix to hear the accusation briefly and examine Paul
new.speaker: Tertullus the advocate
new.note: Courtroom requests (24:4, 24:8); the surrounding verses are outside candidate list.

new.title: Strive always for a blameless conscience toward God and people
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Outside candidate list; Paul's stated rule of life (compare 23:1).

new.title: Felix sends Paul away, then summons him often hoping for a bribe
new.speaker: Felix the governor
new.note: Paul's subjects (righteousness, self-control, coming judgment) are reported without quoted directives.

new.title: The chief priests ask Festus to bring Paul to Jerusalem
new.speaker: the chief priests and leading Jews
new.note: A favor requested to set an ambush on the road; Festus declines (25:4).

new.title: Festus tells the Jewish leaders to accuse Paul at Caesarea
new.speaker: Festus
new.recipient: the influential men among the Jews
new.note: Includes his order to bring Paul before the tribunal (25:6), retold by Festus at 25:17.

new.title: Festus brings Paul before Agrippa to find charges to write
new.speaker: Festus, at King Agrippa's request
new.recipient: King Agrippa and the assembled hearers
new.note: Agrippa asks to hear Paul (25:22); Paul is brought in at Festus's order (25:23).

new.title: Paul asks King Agrippa to hear him patiently
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Agrippa grants leave to speak (26:1).

new.title: Paul proclaims: repent, turn to God, do works worthy of repentance
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: Jews of Damascus, Jerusalem and Judea, and the Gentiles
new.note: Paul's obedience to the vision (AUD-48-26-15); compare AUD-44-3-7 and AUD-48-3-17.

new.title: Paul warns the ship's company against sailing on from Fair Havens
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the centurion, pilot, shipowner and crew
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 27:9–11 outside candidate list; at 27:21 Paul recalls the unheeded advice before AUD-48-27-22.

new.title: Paul calls the leading Jews of Rome together to hear him
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 28:17 and 28:21–23 outside candidate list; they ask to hear his views and appoint a day.

new.title: Do not practise or approve what God's righteous decree condemns
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Vice list (including disobedience to parents) under God's decree that such deserve death; a doctrinal indictment, so borderline.

new.title: Do not teach others the law while breaking it yourself
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the one who bears the name Jew and teaches the law
new.note: 2:21–22 are linked only as commandments (S072, S025); the hypocrisy rebuke and 2:24 (Isaiah 52:5) are unrecorded.

new.title: Do not do evil so that good may come
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul rejects the slogan as slander and calls its proponents' condemnation just; compare 6:1–2.

new.title: Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven
new.speaker: David, quoted by Paul
new.note: Beatitude quoting Greek Psalm 31:1–2, also unrecorded; link there instead if the Psalms review itemizes it.

new.title: As far as it depends on you, live at peace with all
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Also 12:17b: take thought for what is honorable before all people. Compare A093 (Hebrews 12:14).

new.title: Paul asks the Romans to send him onward to Spain
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: 'Sent onward' implies travel support; same request at 1 Corinthians 16:6 and 2 Corinthians 1:16; compare AUD-60-3-13.

new.title: Those who share in spiritual blessings owe service in material things
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Rationale for the Gentile churches' gift to Jerusalem's poor; compare AUD-50-16-1 and A083 (1 Corinthians 9:11).

new.title: Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Includes 8:2–3: one who thinks he knows does not yet know as he ought; one who loves God is known by Him.

new.title: Paul urged Apollos to visit Corinth, but he declined for now
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Reported request; Apollos will come when he has opportunity.

new.title: Comfort others with the comfort you receive from God
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Praise of God stating a principle for conduct (1:4): comfort received equips us to comfort the afflicted.

new.title: Rely on God who raises the dead, and help by prayer
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: 1:9 draws the lesson of trust from affliction; 1:11 counts on the Corinthians' intercession (compare AUD-49-15-30).

new.title: Make it your aim to please the Lord before Christ's judgment seat
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: All must appear before Christ's judgment seat to receive for what they have done (5:10); 5:12–13 needs nothing.

new.title: Regard no one according to the flesh; in Christ is new creation
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Doctrine with a direction on how to regard people; borderline.

new.title: Open your hearts wide to us and make room for us
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On
new.note: AUD-51-6-14 (6:14–7:1) interrupts; 7:2 resumes the appeal. 7:4–7 and 7:12–16 are autobiography.

new.title: Macedonian churches beg Paul to share in the ministry to the saints
new.speaker: the churches of Macedonia
new.note: Reported request (8:4); the rest narrates the Macedonians' example that grounds AUD-51-8-6 (8:6–12).

new.title: Wage spiritual warfare, taking every thought captive to obey Christ
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On
new.note: Paul's appeal (10:1–2) and his non-fleshly warfare (10:3–6); AUD-51-10-7 begins only at 10:7.

new.title: Parents should store up for their children, not children for parents
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
new.note: Maxim Paul applies to his refusal of support; 12:15 adds his readiness to spend and be spent.

new.title: Paul warns unrepentant sinners that he will not spare them
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: the Corinthian church, especially those who sinned before
new.note: Warning before the third visit (12:20–21; 13:2); leads into AUD-51-13-5 (13:5–12). 13:1 is A085.

new.title: The pillars affirm Paul's mission to the nations, Peter's to the circumcised
new.speaker: James, Cephas and John, recognizing God's entrusting
new.note: AUD-52-2-9 (2:9–10) records only the request to remember the poor, not the agreed division of mission.

new.title: Paul cites the rule that a ratified covenant cannot be altered
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Human legal analogy, as the catalogue records Romans 7:1–4 (AUD-49-7-1) as Law; grounds A079 (3:16–19).

new.title: Paul cites the rule that an underage heir is under guardians
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Inheritance-law analogy like AUD-49-7-1 (Romans 7:1–4); 4:3–7 applies it to adoption as sons.

new.title: Boast only in the cross, not in outward circumcision
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Closing warning and the 'rule' of new creation (6:16); no record after 6:10.

new.title: Paul forbids anyone to trouble him further
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Jussive prohibition grounded in his bearing the marks of Jesus.

new.title: Paul rejoices that Christ is proclaimed and magnified, in life or death
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul's example, like AUD-54-4-10 (4:10–13): 'to live is Christ and to die is gain' (1:21).

new.title: Paul plans to send Timothy to learn of the Philippians' state
new.speaker: Paul
new.recipient: Timothy, to be sent to the Philippian church
new.note: Comparable to the Epaphroditus record AUD-54-2-25 (2:25–30) and Timothy's mission in AUD-56-3-1.

new.title: Count all things loss for the surpassing worth of knowing Christ
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul's example between AUD-54-3-1 (3:1–3) and AUD-54-3-12 (3:12–21); 3:17 asks readers to imitate it.

new.title: Gifts for gospel work are a sacrifice pleasing to God
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Paul commends their giving and seeks 'the fruit that increases to your account'; cf. A104 (Hebrews 13:16).

new.title: Continue in the faith, steadfast and not shifting from the gospel's hope
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Conditional exhortation (1:23); 1:23b 'of which I, Paul, became a servant' leads into AUD-55-1-24.

new.title: The trustworthy saying that Christ Jesus came to save sinners
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: The only Pastoral 'trustworthy saying' without a record (cf. A056, AUD-58-3-1, AUD-60-3-8); 1:12 is in AUD-48-26-15.

new.title: Paul writes so Timothy knows how to conduct himself in God's household
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: States the purpose of the church-order directions of chapters 2–3; 3:16 is a confession.

new.title: All who want to live godly lives in Christ will be persecuted
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Timothy followed Paul's conduct and sufferings (3:10–11); leads into AUD-59-3-14 (3:14–17).

new.title: Paul asks Timothy to come quickly, bringing Mark, his cloak and books
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Personal requests with no record; 4:21 repeats 'come before winter'. Compare AUD-60-3-13 (Titus 3:13).

new.title: Paul tells Titus to come to Nicopolis when Artemas or Tychicus arrives
new.speaker: Paul
new.topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
new.note: Also reports the planned sending of Artemas or Tychicus to relieve Titus.

new.title: Paul asks Philemon to prepare a guest room for him
new.speaker: Paul
new.note: Distinct request (lodging) from the Onesimus appeal; Paul hopes to be released through their prayers.

new.title: Angels are sent out to serve those who will inherit salvation
new.speaker: God, as Hebrews states
new.note: Rhetorical question naming the angels' standing commission; cf. AUD-62-1-6 (1:6). The psalms quoted in 1:5–12 have no records.

new.title: An oath by one greater confirms a matter and ends dispute
new.speaker: the author of Hebrews
new.note: Human oath practice used as analogy, as with oaths settling disputes in torah-exodus-22-1 (Exodus 22:11).

new.title: A testament takes effect only at the death of its maker
new.speaker: the author of Hebrews
new.note: Inheritance-law analogy for the new covenant, like AUD-49-7-1 (Romans 7:1–4).

new.title: Abraham, Sarah, Isaac and Jacob as examples of faith
new.speaker: the author of Hebrews
new.note: Matches A072 (11:4–7) and A073 (11:24–27); 11:13–16 adds living as sojourners seeking a heavenly homeland.

new.title: Israel, Rahab, the judges, prophets and martyrs as examples of faith
new.speaker: the author of Hebrews
new.note: Continues A073 (11:24–27); 11:39–40 conclude that all awaited the promise perfected with us.

new.title: The author asks for prayer so he may be restored sooner
new.speaker: the author of Hebrews
new.note: No record after 13:17; compare Paul's prayer requests AUD-57-3-1 and AUD-49-15-30.

new.title: Bear with the word of encouragement
new.speaker: the author of Hebrews
new.topic: Major Teachings: The Word of Christ Handed On
new.note: Closing request to receive the letter's exhortation patiently.

new.title: False teachers will arise among you and exploit you through greed
new.speaker: Peter
new.recipient: those who received a faith of equal honor
new.note: Heads the chapter's warning; cf. Matthew 7:15 (K085), Jude 1:4 (AUD-69-1-3). The catalogue itemizes such apostolic warnings separately (A061, A062).

new.title: False teachers slander glorious beings and follow Balaam's path of greed
new.speaker: Peter
new.recipient: those who received a faith of equal honor
new.note: Portrait of the false teachers (2:10b–16); angels do not slander (2:11). Cf. Jude 1:8–11 (AUD-69-1-3 link, A095); AUD-65-2-17 begins at 2:17.

new.title: Do not be surprised if the world hates you
new.speaker: the writer of 1 John
new.note: Direct prohibition between A094 (3:11–12) and A014 (3:15); cf. John 15:18–19 and 1 Peter 4:12 (A054).

new.title: Keep His commandments and have confidence before God in prayer
new.speaker: the writer of 1 John
new.note: Assurance of the heart, answered prayer and abiding through obedience (3:19–22, 24); 3:23 is A012. Cf. A040 (5:14–15).

new.title: The trumpet-like voice summons John to come up and see
new.speaker: the first voice, like a trumpet (the risen Christ of 1:10)
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: 'Come up hither, and I will show thee…': a summons like AUD-70-11-11 ('Come up here'). 4:2–11 is vision and praise.

new.title: The living creatures call 'Come' as each of four horsemen rides out
new.speaker: the four living creatures
new.note: One record for the four calls (6:1, 3, 5, 7); AUD-70-6-5 holds only the oil-and-wine restraint. Covers P03096 (6:7–8).

new.title: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord
new.speaker: a voice from heaven, confirmed by the Spirit
new.recipient: John and the hearers of the prophecy
new.note: Outside candidate list. AUD-70-14-13 records only the order to write; its note separates the writing order from the beatitude's content.

new.title: A bowl angel summons John to see the great prostitute's judgment
new.speaker: one of the seven angels with the bowls
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: 'Come, I will show thee…'; 21:9 repeats the formula (P03122) and could be linked as Additional Scripture. 17:3–6 is vision.

new.title: Blessed are those called to the Lamb's marriage supper
new.speaker: the angel speaking with John
new.recipient: John and the hearers of the prophecy
new.note: Outside candidate list. AUD-70-19-9 records the order to write; the beatitude itself, like 1:3 and 16:15, could be itemized as Wisdom.

new.title: Blessed and holy is the one who shares in the first resurrection
new.speaker: John, the narrative voice of the revelation
new.note: Revelation's fifth beatitude has no record; origin follows the narrator's sayings AUD-70-13-9 and AUD-70-13-18. 20:4 'judgment was given' is narrative.

new.title: A bowl angel summons John to see the bride, the Lamb's wife
new.speaker: one of the seven angels with the bowls
new.topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
new.note: Same formula as 17:1 (new, P03114); one record with Additional Scripture would also suit. 21:10–26 describe the city.

new.title: Christ comes quickly to repay each according to his work
new.speaker: the risen Christ
new.note: Christ's own words, grounding 22:11 and 22:14; same principle as 2:23 (in AUD-70-2-18). Could instead extend AUD-70-22-14.

extend.title: Pharaoh sends Abram away with Sarai
extend.note: 12:20: Pharaoh commanded men to escort Abram away with his wife and all he had.

extend.title: Lot: bring your household out of Sodom
extend.note: At dawn the angels renew the order: take your wife and two daughters and depart. Add 19:15.

extend.title: Lot: flee to the permitted place of refuge
extend.note: 19:21–22 grants Zoar as the permitted refuge and orders Lot to hurry there.

extend.title: Abraham asks to buy Ephron’s cave
extend.note: The request begins in 23:8: 'hear me, and speak for me to Ephron'.

extend.title: Ephron offers Abraham the field and cave
extend.note: Ephron's renewed offer names the price, four hundred didrachms, and repeats 'Bury your dead'.

extend.title: The servant recounts his prayer for a sign at the well
extend.note: 24:43 ends mid-sentence; 24:44 completes the recounted sign.

extend.title: Abimelech’s party seeks a covenant with Isaac
extend.note: 26:29 states the sworn term they ask for: 'that you shall do us no harm'.

extend.title: Rebekah tells Jacob to bring two young goats
extend.note: 27:10 completes the order: take the food to your father so that he blesses you.

extend.title: Esau cries out for a blessing of his own
extend.note: Esau repeats the plea in 27:38: 'Bless me also, father.'

extend.title: Rebekah tells Jacob to stay with Laban until Esau calms
extend.note: The order opens in 27:43 ('arise and flee... to Laban') and ends in 27:45; 27:44 alone is a fragment.

extend.title: Jacob proposes taking marked animals as wages
extend.note: The proposal opens in 30:31 ('You shall give me nothing') and sets the theft test in 30:33.

extend.title: Jacob prepares his servant for Esau’s questions
extend.note: In this numbering the prescribed answer is 32:18–19; the record's 32:17 holds only the marching order.

extend.title: Jacob tells his servants to announce that he is following
extend.note: The announcement itself ('your servant Jacob comes behind us') is 32:21 in this numbering.

extend.title: Jacob presses Esau to accept his gift
extend.note: 33:10 already makes the request: 'receive the gifts from my hands.'

extend.title: Joseph advises Pharaoh to appoint overseers and store grain
extend.note: 41:36 completes the advice: keep the food for the land against the seven years of famine.

extend.title: Joseph orders one brother to fetch the youngest
extend.note: The test is announced in 42:15: you shall not leave unless your youngest brother comes.

extend.title: Joseph tells his detained brothers how to stay alive
extend.note: 42:19 states the terms of 'Do this': one brother held, the rest carry grain home.

extend.title: Judah asks Jacob to send Benjamin with him
extend.note: 43:9 adds Judah's surety: 'require him from my hand'; 43:10 closes the plea.

extend.title: Joseph sends his steward after his brothers
extend.note: 44:5 completes the words the steward is told to say about the silver cup.

extend.title: Judah recalls Joseph asking to see Benjamin
extend.note: 44:23 completes the recalled demand: without your youngest brother you shall see my face no more.

extend.title: Joseph sends his brothers to bring Jacob to Egypt
extend.note: The message continues: live in Goshen near me, and I will nourish you (45:10–11).

extend.title: Pharaoh assigns Goshen and offers work tending his livestock
extend.note: 47:6 continues: 'settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land'.

extend.title: Jacob asks Joseph to bury him outside Egypt
extend.note: 47:30 completes the request: carry me out of Egypt and bury me in my fathers' tomb.

extend.title: Jacob explains how Joseph’s later children will inherit
extend.note: 48:5 is the main ruling (Ephraim and Manasseh are mine, as Reuben and Simeon); retitle the record accordingly.

extend.title: Pharaoh orders the brickmakers to gather their own straw
extend.note: 5:6 names the order's addressees; extend 5:7 to 5:6–7.

extend.title: The workers are told to find straw without a lower quota
extend.note: The proclamation begins in 5:10: 'Thus says Pharaoh: I will no longer give you straw.'

extend.title: Exclude uncircumcised and otherwise ineligible persons from the Passover meal
extend.note: Rambam N126 (12:45) is not itemized; C0111's 'otherwise ineligible persons' covers it. Extend 12:43 to 12:43–45.

extend.title: Jethro advises Moses to represent the people before God
extend.note: Rationale opening Jethro's counsel; extend 18:19 to 18:17–19.

extend.title: Accept the keeper's exonerating oath without demanding restitution
extend.note: 22:9 states the case whose ruling C0196 (22:10) records; extend to 22:9–10.

extend.title: Make the bronze-covered altar with horns, grating and rings
extend.note: Construction detail of the altar in C0277 (27:1–5); 27:9–18 are covered by C0281.

extend.title: Appointed artisans: make the commissioned sanctuary and priestly furnishings
extend.note: Outside candidate list: Bezalel's appointment precedes C0353 (31:6–11, 'him and Eliab'); extend to 31:2–11.

extend.title: Aaron and sons: remain at the tent entrance through the seven days of consecration
extend.note: 8:35 restates and completes C0459 (8:33), adding 'so that you do not die'; extend to 8:33–35.

extend.title: Priest: inspect skin and scalp lesions and declare their status by the stated diagnostic criteria
extend.note: Extend C0485 (13:3) to 13:3–44: the chronic, total-white, raw-flesh, boil, burn and scalp cases are its stated criteria. / Second-week scalp ruling, spreading patch, white eruption and baldness belong to C0485's criteria (extend to 13:3–44). / Lesion on a bald head or forehead is part of C0485's stated criteria (extend to 13:3–44).

extend.title: Present a suspected or changing skin lesion to the priest
extend.note: C0484's title covers new and changing lesions; its reference (13:2) omits the repeated directions at 13:9, 16 and 19.

extend.title: Isolate suspected skin or scalp lesions for the specified examination periods
extend.note: C0486's title already covers the boil, burn and scalp cases; its reference stops at 13:4–5.

extend.title: Wash garments after clearance of the specified skin or scalp lesion
extend.note: C0487's title names scalp lesions; 13:34 is the scalp-case washing, outside its 13:6 reference.

extend.title: Priest: inspect and classify the affected garment or leather by the stated criteria
extend.note: Re-inspection criteria after washing continue C0496 (13:50–51).

extend.title: Burn the garment or leather article with the persistent or recurring lesion
extend.note: C0498's title already covers the unchanged-after-washing and recurring cases stated at 13:55 and 13:57.

extend.title: Wash the affected garment or leather as prescribed, including the second cleansing wash
extend.note: C0499's title names the second cleansing wash, which is stated at 13:58, not 13:54.

extend.title: Present the prescribed eighth-day purification offerings and oil, with the poverty substitutions
extend.note: C0511's title names the poverty substitutions, but these are stated only at 14:21–23.

extend.title: The house owner: report a suspected house lesion to the priest
extend.note: 14:34 is the setting (entry into Canaan) of C0519's house law; extend to 14:34–35.

extend.title: Priest: inspect and classify the house lesion by the stated criteria
extend.note: Rambam P103 (leprous house) is itemized across C0519–C0532; extend C0521 to the re-inspections at 14:44 and 14:48. / Declaring the replastered house clean is part of C0521's classification; extend its reference.

extend.title: Apply the stated uncleanness periods and contact rules for bodily discharges
extend.note: The saddle rule continues C0533's bed and seat rules (15:4).

extend.title: Wash garments after the specified contact with a discharge or contaminated bedding
extend.note: Carrying his bedding (15:10) and being touched by unwashed hands (15:11) are further specified contacts; extend C0534–C0536 to 15:5–11.

extend.title: Bathe after the specified contact with a discharge or contaminated bedding
extend.note: Bathe after the specified discharge contact

extend.title: Remain unclean until evening after the specified discharge contact
extend.note: Remain unclean until evening after the specified discharge contact

extend.title: Bathe after the stated seminal emission or intercourse
extend.note: C0543's title names intercourse, stated only at 15:18; its reference stops at 15:16.

extend.title: Observe uncleanness until evening after the stated seminal emission or intercourse
extend.note: C0544's title names intercourse, stated only at 15:18; its reference stops at 15:16.

extend.title: Provide the prescribed personal and congregational animals for the Day of Atonement
extend.note: C0548's title names the congregational animals, which are specified only at 16:5.

extend.title: Do not defile yourselves through the prohibited sexual acts
extend.note: Extend C0594 (18:24) to 18:24–30; 18:26 binds natives and resident foreigners alike. / 18:29 states the penalty (cut off); 18:30 repeats the charge not to be defiled.

extend.title: Priests: do not approach or eat holy things while unclean
extend.note: Rambam N75 (unclean priest not to serve) is itemized as C0670 (22:3–7); 22:2 is its heading. / 22:9 is the closing sanction for 22:1–8; it could instead attach to C0672.

extend.title: Do not profane Israel's holy contributions
extend.note: 22:16 completes the sentence begun at 22:15.

extend.title: Do not offer blemished or mutilated animals, including those supplied by foreigners
extend.note: Positive half of the blemish law (22:18–25); compare C0371 (1:2–3).

extend.title: Proclaim God's appointed feasts at their prescribed times
extend.note: 23:4 repeats C0679's charge (23:2) as the heading of the festival calendar.

extend.title: Bring the blasphemer outside the camp for judgment
extend.note: Moses relays the order and Israel carries out C0707–C0709.

extend.title: Set apart the prescribed tithe of produce and livestock as holy to God
extend.note: Rambam P78 (cattle tithe) is named in C0759's title, but its reference stops at 27:30; extend to 27:30–32.

extend.title: Israel: march in the prescribed tribal and tabernacle order
extend.note: The order of setting out continues beyond 2:9; extend C0773 to 2:9–31.

extend.title: Take the Levites and their livestock in place of Israel's firstborn
extend.note: 3:45 repeats C0781 (3:41) after the count; extend to 3:41–45.

extend.title: Register the three Levite divisions within the stated service ages
extend.note: C0784's title names all three divisions, but its reference covers only the Kohathites (4:2–3); add 4:22–23 and 4:29–30. / Merarite census; see the C0784 note at 4:22–23.

extend.title: The priest's role when a husband suspects his wife
extend.note: Legal outcome of the jealousy procedure; extend ot-numbers-v5-30 to 5:30–31.

extend.title: Nazirite: do not incur corpse defilement, even for close relatives
extend.note: 6:8 concludes the corpse-defilement rule (6:6–8).

extend.title: Use the prescribed trumpet calls to assemble the people or leaders
extend.note: 10:7 specifies C0844's assembly call (10:3–4).

extend.title: Moses asks Hobab to stay with Israel in the wilderness
extend.note: The promise completes the request of 10:31.

extend.title: Joshua and Caleb urge Israel to trust God
extend.note: 14:8 is the ground of the exhortation in 14:9.

extend.title: Israel: do not launch the presumptuous ascent after God's refusal
extend.note: 14:43 gives the reason for C0856's prohibition (14:42).

extend.title: Provide the prescribed grain, oil and wine accompaniments for each lamb, ram or bull offering
extend.note: C0857 already names resident foreign offerers (15:14); 15:4–12 lie within its reference.

extend.title: Bring the prescribed congregational bull and goat for the stated inadvertent failure
extend.note: 15:22–23 state the case that C0859 (15:24–26) answers.

extend.title: God entrusts the sacred contributions to Aaron and his line
extend.note: 18:19 closes the grant opened at 18:8; extend to 18:8–19.

extend.title: Do not assign Aaron's and Levi's tribe an ordinary territorial inheritance
extend.note: C0881's title names Levi's tribe; 18:23–24 restate it for the Levites.

extend.title: Set apart the best portion of the gifts due to God
extend.note: 18:32 states the result of C0884's requirement (18:29–30).

extend.title: Observe seven-day uncleanness after the specified human corpse, bone, grave or death-house contact
extend.note: C0895's title already covers death-house, bone and grave contact but cites only 19:11. Rambam P107 is itemized at C0895.

extend.title: Balak asks Balaam to curse Israel
extend.note: 22:5 sends the envoys and opens the message that 22:6 completes.

extend.title: Balak offers Balaam a reward for cursing Israel
extend.note: Opening plea of the same message whose reward offer (22:17) is recorded.

extend.title: Moses: lay hands on Joshua to commission him
extend.note: Fulfilment of the commission ordered at 27:18–19; extend only if the catalogue includes performed commissions.

extend.title: Apply the stated confirmation or timely annulment rules to a wife's vow
extend.note: A wife's vow in her husband's house, including late annulment (30:16); C0932 cites only 30:7–9. 30:17 is a closing summary.

extend.title: Reuben and Gad: cross armed with Israel before returning to your eastern possession
extend.note: Sanction clause of the same terms (32:20–22): 'you shall recognize your sin when evils overtake you.'

extend.title: The blood-avenger: execute the condemned murderer under the prescribed judgment
extend.note: 35:21 repeats the 35:19 avenger clause; its murder criteria belong to the new P00415 record.

extend.title: An inheriting daughter: marry within the father's clan under the tribal-land provision
extend.note: Generalizes the ruling for Zelophehad's daughters (36:6) to every inheriting daughter.

extend.title: Preserve ancestral tribal allotments against transfer to another tribe
extend.note: Restates 36:7.

extend.title: Appoint qualified judges and officers
extend.note: Moses carries out the 1:13 appointment; Exodus 18:25 (the same act) has no itemized record.

extend.title: The eastern tribes must cross armed ahead of Israel
extend.note: Completes the 3:18–19 order.

extend.title: Joshua and Israel: do not fear the coming kingdoms
extend.note: Opening of the same charge to Joshua whose 'do not fear' (3:22) is recorded.

extend.title: Do not destroy food-producing trees for siegeworks
extend.note: Extend C1100 from 20:19 to 20:19–20: the permitted exception completes the tree law.

extend.title: Keep the military camp from evil and indecency
extend.note: C1149's title ('indecency') already draws on 23:15; extend its reference from 23:10 to 23:10, 15.

extend.title: Recite the prescribed ancestral-deliverance declaration when presenting firstfruits
extend.note: Rambam P132 is itemized as C1198, but its reference (26:3) omits the recited declaration itself (26:5–10).

extend.title: Set up and plaster the prescribed covenant stones on Mount Ebal
extend.note: C1203's title already names Mount Ebal, which only 27:4 supplies; extend from 27:2 to 27:2, 4.

extend.title: Write the law clearly on the covenant stones
extend.note: C1204's 'clearly' comes from 27:8 ('very plainly'); extend from 27:3 to 27:3, 8.

extend.title: Moses and the priests call Israel to listen
extend.note: Same speech and verb ('hear… hearken'); M028 duplicates the 27:9 record. Retitle the record (listen and obey) when extending.

extend.title: Station the specified tribes on Gerizim and Ebal for the covenant ceremony
extend.note: Speech formula naming Moses as giver of the station order.

extend.title: Choose the life God sets before you
extend.note: The two-ways appeal (30:15–20) is one unit; extend C1212 from 30:19.

extend.title: Moses tells the Levites to place the law beside the ark
extend.note: Speech formula naming the addressees; M029 duplicates the 31:26 record.

extend.title: Joshua reminds the eastern tribes to cross armed with their brothers
extend.note: 1:15 completes the charge with its time limit and the return home.

extend.title: The eastern tribes pledge obedience and encourage Joshua
extend.note: The pledge begins at 1:16; 1:17's 'let the Lord be with you' is a wish.

extend.title: Rahab asks the spies to spare her household
extend.note: Rahab renews her request after the spies' pledge ('Our life in place of yours').

extend.title: The spies tell Rahab to mark her window with scarlet cord
extend.note: Conditions: keep the household inside; do not disclose the agreement. 2:21 is Rahab's assent.

extend.title: Joshua tells Israel what to say about the Jordan memorial
extend.note: 4:6 holds the children's question that the answer in 4:7 replies to.

extend.title: Joshua tells Israel how to explain the dry crossing to their children
extend.note: The instruction runs from the children's question (4:21) through the words and purpose (4:23–24).

extend.title: The Lord tells Joshua to consecrate Israel and remove what was banned
extend.note: 7:12 already states the condition: 'unless you remove that which is under the ban'.

extend.title: Joshua positions troops in ambush behind Ai
extend.note: 8:3: Joshua selects thirty thousand mighty men and sends them out by night.

extend.title: Joshua orders the troops to rise from ambush and take Ai
extend.note: 8:5–6 (the feigned flight) are the first half of the order completed in 8:7–8.

extend.title: Israel’s leaders decide to spare Gibeon because of their oath
extend.note: 9:19 states the prohibition itself: 'now we cannot touch them.'

extend.title: Israel’s leaders assign the spared Gibeonites to cut wood and carry water
extend.note: 9:27 narrates Joshua's formal appointment, adding service for God's altar.

extend.title: The Lord tells Joshua to divide the remaining land among the tribes
extend.note: 'Only distribute it by lot' (13:6) begins the same allotment command.

extend.title: Achsah asks Caleb for springs to accompany her land
extend.note: 15:18: Achsah tells Othniel she will ask for a field and calls to Caleb; compare first-pass Judges 1:14.

extend.title: Joshua tells Ephraim and Manasseh to clear the woodland allotment
extend.note: Joshua first gives the woodland instruction at 17:15; 17:17–18 repeats and expands it.

extend.title: Joshua tells the surveyors to divide the land into seven portions
extend.note: 18:5 adds the survey rule: Judah keeps the south, Joseph the north.

extend.title: The Lord recalls warning Israel against fearing Amorite gods
extend.note: The prophet’s sending and oracle begin at 6:8 (‘I brought you up from Egypt’); the record cites only its last verse.

extend.title: Gideon asks the messenger to wait for his offering
extend.note: The request for a sign (6:17) opens the same speech; extend the reference to 6:17–18.

extend.title: The Lord has Gideon dismiss the fearful and test the rest
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 7:5 gives the test itself (set apart those who lap like dogs). Candidate 7:13 is narrative.

extend.title: Gideon tells his son Jether to kill the captured kings
extend.note: 8:19’s oath (‘As the Lord lives… I would not kill you’) is the sentence that the recorded order carries out.

extend.title: Jotham warns Shechem that treachery in choosing a ruler leads to ruin
extend.note: Fable verses 9:8–9, 11, 13–15 are uncovered (9:10, 9:12 are Study Context); extending lets the Wisdom record span fable and application.

extend.title: Jephthah’s daughter asks for time to mourn with her companions
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 11:36 ‘do to me according to what has gone out from your mouth’ opens the same speech.

extend.title: Samson states the stakes of his wedding riddle
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 14:12 states Samson’s side of the wager; the recorded 14:13 states theirs.

extend.title: Samson asks Judah’s men to swear they will not kill him
extend.note: 15:13 gives the oath sworn in reply (‘we will only bind you… and surely not kill you’). Other candidates here are threats and narrative.

extend.title: Micah offers the Levite wages to serve as his priest
extend.note: Outside candidate list (17:12 is context). The offer is recorded; 17:11–12 complete it: Micah ‘filled the Levite’s hand’ and he became his priest.

extend.title: The Danite scouts urge their tribe to attack Laish
extend.note: 18:10 completes the scouts’ exhortation (a spacious land; ‘God has delivered it into your hands’).

extend.title: The woman’s father asks the Levite to eat before departing
extend.note: Same fourth-day hospitality: after the meal he presses the Levite to lodge another night (19:6–7).

extend.title: The woman’s father urges the Levite to stay until afternoon
extend.note: The fifth-day urging continues: ‘Lodge here today also… tomorrow you may rise early’ (19:9).

extend.title: The host offers two women to the mob instead of his guest
extend.note: 19:23 (‘please do not act wickedly… do not commit this folly’) opens the plea that 19:24 completes.

extend.title: Israel’s leaders tell the Benjaminites to seize wives at Shiloh
extend.note: 21:22 completes the instruction: the elders will answer the fathers’ complaints (‘Have mercy on them’).

extend.title: Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to return home because she has no sons
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 1:13 (‘No, my daughters’) ends the same appeal; 1:15 is already linked.

extend.title: Ruth asks Naomi to let her stay and pledges loyalty
extend.note: 1:17 completes Ruth’s pledge (‘where you die, I will die’) with her self-curse oath.

extend.title: Naomi prepares Ruth to approach Boaz at the threshing floor
extend.note: 3:1–2 open Naomi’s plan (seeking rest for Ruth; Boaz winnows tonight).

extend.title: Boaz asks Ruth to stay overnight and promises to act if the nearer kinsman declines
extend.note: 3:11 (‘do not be afraid; I will do for you all that you say’) begins the reply recorded at 3:13.

extend.title: Elkanah tells Hannah to stay until Samuel is weaned
extend.note: 1:22 holds Hannah’s proposal (not until the child is weaned; then he stays before the Lord) that Elkanah’s recorded reply approves.

extend.title: Eli rebukes his sons for their misconduct
extend.note: The rebuke opens at 2:23 (‘Why do you act according to this report?’); first-pass P00672 adds the closing maxim (2:25).

extend.title: The Philistine rulers send the ark from Ashdod to Gath
extend.note: 5:7 (‘The ark… must not stay with us’) is the resolution that convenes the rulers in 5:8. 5:5 is narrated custom.

extend.title: The priests prescribe gold mice and tell the Philistines to honor the Lord
extend.note: 6:4 prescribes the five gold seats that the 6:5 record omits; 6:6 warns against hardening hearts like Pharaoh.

extend.title: Israel asks Samuel for a king to judge them
extend.note: 8:5 holds the elders’ actual request (‘Now appoint a king over us’); 8:6 only restates it.

extend.title: Saul suggests going home and his servant proposes consulting a seer
extend.note: 9:7–8 continue the same exchange (what to bring; the servant’s quarter-shekel), between the 9:5–6 and 9:9–10 records.

extend.title: Samuel invites Saul to eat with him at the high place
extend.note: 9:20 continues the reply: ‘do not set your heart on them’. Saul’s question about the seer’s house (9:18) needs nothing.

extend.title: Samuel has Israel assemble before the Lord by tribe and clan
extend.note: 10:17 reports the summons to Mizpah and 10:18 the Lord’s word prefacing the order. The uncle’s question (10:15) needs nothing.

extend.title: Samuel calls Israel to Gilgal to renew the kingship
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 11:15 reports the outcome: Samuel anointed Saul king before the Lord at Gilgal.

extend.title: Samuel asks Israel to testify if he has wronged them
extend.note: 12:4–5 complete the procedure: the people acquit him, and Samuel calls the Lord and his anointed as witnesses (‘Witness’).

extend.title: Samuel asks Israel to witness the sign the Lord will give
extend.note: 12:17 completes the call: ‘Know and see that the evil you have done… is great.’

extend.title: Samuel urges Israel to fear and serve the Lord sincerely
extend.note: 12:25 attaches the warning: if you do evil, you and your king will be swept away.

extend.title: Jonathan sets the condition for remaining in place
extend.note: 14:8 (‘We will cross to the men’) opens the plan of 14:8–10.

extend.title: Saul asks Ahijah to bring the ephod near
extend.note: 14:19: Saul breaks off the inquiry (‘Withdraw your hands’) as the tumult grows.

extend.title: Saul orders slaughter at the stone so Israel will not eat blood
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 14:33 ‘Roll a large stone here to me’ begins the order. Candidates 14:28–29 fall under P00700.

extend.title: Saul gathers Israel’s chiefs to investigate the day’s offense
extend.note: 14:39 binds the inquiry by oath: even Jonathan must die. 14:37 and 14:41 are inquiries addressed to God.

extend.title: Samuel relays the Lord’s order to strike Amalek
extend.note: 15:2 opens the oracle with its ground, Amalek’s ambush on the way from Egypt, executing C1197 (Deuteronomy 25:17–19).

extend.title: Samuel reminds Saul of his mission against Amalek
extend.note: 15:17 and 15:19 frame the recalled mission: anointed though small, why did you not obey?

extend.title: Samuel teaches Saul that obedience is better than sacrifice
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 15:23 completes the saying: divination is sin, and rejecting the Lord’s word costs the kingship.

extend.title: Goliath challenges Israel to send a champion
extend.note: 17:9 sets the terms of the challenge: the loser’s people serve the winner’s.

extend.title: Jonathan warns David to hide from Saul
extend.note: 19:3 completes Jonathan’s instruction: he will speak to Saul in the field and report back.

extend.title: Jonathan urges Saul not to wrong David
extend.note: 19:5 completes the plea; 19:6 records Saul’s oath ‘he shall not die’, soon broken (19:10).

extend.title: Saul orders David brought in on his bed to be killed
extend.note: 19:14 is the first sending to take David, rebuffed by Michal’s ruse; first-pass P00720 covers the earlier watch order (19:11).

extend.title: David asks Jonathan to let him hide during the new moon feast
extend.note: 20:6 gives the excuse Jonathan is to tell Saul (delivered at 20:28–29); 20:7 sets the test of Saul’s reaction.

extend.title: Jonathan asks David to show lasting kindness to his family
extend.note: The request begins at 20:14 (‘you shall show mercy to me’) and closes with Jonathan’s renewed oath (20:16–17).

extend.title: Jonathan explains which arrow signal means it is safe
extend.note: Outside candidate list. 20:22 gives the danger signal: ‘the shaft is beyond you… go’.

extend.title: Jonathan’s call to the boy signals David to hurry away
extend.note: 20:36 ‘Run, find the shafts’ and 20:37 ‘the shaft is beyond you’ belong to the same signal sequence.

extend.title: Saul orders his guards to kill the priests and they refuse
extend.note: 22:16 pronounces the death sentence; 22:18 (outside candidate list) turns the order to Doeg after the guards refuse.

extend.title: Saul asks David to spare his descendants and preserve his name
extend.note: 24:23 records the oath sworn in reply, as first-pass P00634 extends ot-judges-v15-12 to 15:13.

extend.title: David forbids Abishai from striking Saul
extend.note: Adds 26:10–11: David restates the prohibition and orders, ‘take the spear… and the water flask, and let us go.’

extend.title: Saul asks the medium at Endor to summon Samuel
extend.note: Adds 28:8, Saul’s first request (‘divine for me… bring up the one I name’), with his oath of safety in 28:10.

extend.title: The medium urges Saul to eat before leaving
extend.note: 28:23 reports the servants joining the woman’s urging, and Saul yielding.

extend.title: David orders the Amalekite messenger struck down
extend.note: 1:14 states the charge (raising a hand against the Lord’s anointed) and 1:16 the verdict, ‘Your blood is on your own head.’

extend.title: David demands that Michal be returned to him
extend.note: David first sets the condition to Abner (3:13: bring Michal or not see my face); 3:15 reports her being taken from Paltiel.

extend.title: Joab calls his brother to fight courageously for their people
extend.note: Adds 10:11, the mutual-aid order (‘you all shall come to my rescue’). Parallel 1 Chronicles 19:12 could join ot-1-chronicles-v19-13.

extend.title: David orders Joab to expose Uriah to deadly fighting
extend.note: 11:14 reports how the order was delivered: a letter sent by Uriah’s own hand.

extend.title: Tamar resists Amnon and pleads with him to stop
extend.note: Adds 13:13, where her plea continues: ‘Please speak to the king now, for he certainly will not withhold me from you.’

extend.title: Absalom demands that Joab arrange an audience with David
extend.note: The demand is first made at 14:29 (Absalom twice sends for Joab, who refuses); 14:32 restates it after the barley is burned.

extend.title: David asks Hushai to return and counter Ahithophel’s advice
extend.note: 15:33 opens the instruction with its first branch: going with David would make Hushai a burden.

extend.title: David asks Hushai to send reports through the priests’ sons
extend.note: Adds 15:35 (‘Whatever you hear from the king’s house, tell Zadok and Abiathar’), between the 15:34 and 15:36 records.

extend.title: David refuses to let his men stop Shimei’s curses
extend.note: Adds Abishai’s request, which David’s refusal answers, as AUD-10-19-22 includes Abishai’s 19:22 proposal.

extend.title: Absalom summons Hushai for a second opinion
extend.note: Adds 17:6, the request itself (‘Should we act on his proposal? If not, you speak’); Hushai’s answer is first-pass P00793.

extend.title: Ahimaaz asks Joab to let him run after Cushi
extend.note: Adds 18:23, completing the exchange with Joab’s permission: ‘Run.’ 18:24–28 are reports and a blessing.

extend.title: David asks Judah’s elders to bring him back
extend.note: Adds 19:13, the rest of the message: ‘You are my brothers… Why should you be the last to bring the king back?’

extend.title: Barzillai asks to return home and sends Chimham in his place
extend.note: Adds the opening of the same reply: his age, and his offer to cross only a little way (19:35–37).

extend.title: The wise woman of Abel calls for Joab to speak with her
extend.note: Adds 20:17: ‘Hear your handmaid’s words.’

extend.title: David recounts God asking him to speak a parable about fearing God
extend.note: Adds the oracle’s opening (23:1–2: ‘David’s last words… The Spirit of the Lord spoke in me’); 23:2 is context.

extend.title: Nathan advises Bathsheba to remind David of his oath about Solomon
extend.note: Adds 1:14, the last step of Nathan’s plan: he will come in after her and complete her words.

extend.title: David calls on Solomon to be strong as he faces death
extend.note: Adds 2:1, the narrative frame of the charge: ‘he commanded his son Solomon, saying.’

extend.title: David charges Solomon to keep the Lord’s commands in Moses’ law
extend.note: Adds 2:4, completing the sentence with God’s conditional promise: ‘If your sons guard their way, walking before Me in truth.’ 2:5 needs nothing.

extend.title: David tells Solomon to hold Shimei to account
extend.note: Adds 2:8, which names Shimei, his curse and David’s oath; the Greek doublet is 1 Kings 2:35l–35o.

extend.title: David’s charge to Solomon concerning Shimei’s punishment
extend.note: Adds 2:35l–35n: ‘he commanded Solomon’, naming Shimei, his curse and David’s oath. 2:35h is noted at 1 Kings 5:27–30.

extend.title: Solomon asks Hiram to have cedar timber cut in Lebanon
extend.note: Adds the message’s opening (5:16–19), as first pass extended the parallel ot-2-chronicles-v2-6 to 2:2–9; 5:19 also sits on ot-1-chronicles-v28-10.

extend.title: Solomon recounts God appointing David’s son to build the temple
extend.note: Adds 8:18, where the Lord’s word to David begins; first-pass P00998 includes the matching verse in its parallel 2 Chronicles 6:8–10.

extend.title: Asa offers gifts for an alliance and asks Syria to break with Baasha
extend.note: Adds 15:18: Asa sends the temple and palace silver and gold with envoys, ‘saying’. Same gap at 2 Chronicles 16:2.

extend.title: The Lord tells Elijah to hide at the Chorrath wadi
extend.note: Adds 17:4, the rest of the instruction: drink from the wadi; the ravens will feed him there.

extend.title: Elijah asks the widow to make him a small cake first
extend.note: Adds Elijah’s opening requests for water (17:10) and a morsel of bread (17:11), which lead into the cake request.

extend.title: Elijah tells Ahab to gather Israel and the prophets at Carmel
extend.note: Adds 18:18, Elijah’s rebuke of Ahab’s Baal worship that opens the same reply and grounds the summons.

extend.title: Jezebel’s letters order a fast and seat Naboth before the people
extend.note: The letter continues in 20:10: suborn two false witnesses and stone Naboth; the title should name this.

extend.title: Orders concerning the district rulers’ attendants during the siege
extend.note: The order 'take them alive, whether for peace or war' (21:18) opens the order recorded at 21:19.

extend.title: The Syrian advisers propose replacing the kings with governors
extend.note: The counsel runs 21:23-25: fight on level ground and rebuild the lost army horse for horse.

extend.title: Jehoshaphat challenges Ahab’s dismissal of Micaiah and Ahab summons him
extend.note: Adds 22:7, Jehoshaphat’s request for a prophet of the Lord that opens the exchange; parallel 2 Chronicles 18:6–8 reported separately.

extend.title: Micaiah recounts a spirit being permitted to deceive Ahab’s prophets
extend.note: Micaiah's 'Hear the Lord's word' and the Lord's call 'Who will deceive Ahab?' (22:20) begin the commission.

extend.title: Ahaziah sends messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub
extend.note: The grouped record includes the angel's charge to Elijah (1:3); that charge continues in 1:4, ending 'Elijah went and spoke to them.'

extend.title: The prophets press Elisha to let them search for Elijah
extend.note: Elisha's reproach 'Did I not tell you, Do not go?' recalls his prohibition after the failed search.

extend.title: Elisha calls for a musician and gives the Lord’s instruction to dig pits
extend.note: The oracle continues: strike fortified cities, fell good trees, stop springs, spoil fields (3:19; carried out 3:25).

extend.title: Syria’s king sends Naaman to Israel with a letter
extend.note: The letter's demand that Israel's king cure Naaman (5:6) completes the sending.

extend.title: The prophets ask Elisha to let them build by the Jordan
extend.note: Their further request 'Please come with your slaves' (6:3) belongs to the same exchange.

extend.title: A woman recounts a desperate bargain made during the famine
extend.note: Her account and the second demand 'Give your son' continue in 6:29.

extend.title: Four men with leprosy decide to risk entering the Syrian camp
extend.note: Adds 7:3, where the proposal begins: ‘Why are we sitting here until we die?’

extend.title: Elisha tells the young prophet to take Jehu aside privately
extend.note: The instruction begins in 9:1: fasten your belt, take the flask of oil, go to Ramoth-gilead.

extend.title: The prophetic messenger anoints Jehu and charges him to avenge the slain prophets
extend.note: The oracle ends at 9:10 (Jezebel's fate), and the prophet flees as Elisha instructed (9:3).

extend.title: Jehu tells his officer to throw Joram’s body into Naboth’s field
extend.note: The order is completed in 9:26: 'lift him up and throw him into the portion, according to the Lord's word.'

extend.title: Jehu calls to the officials at Jezebel’s window
extend.note: Outside candidate list: the order itself, 'Roll her down!', is in 9:33.

extend.title: Jehu invites Jonadab to witness his zeal
extend.note: 'If it is, give me your hand' (10:15) begins the same invitation.

extend.title: Jehu summons Baal’s worshipers under false pretenses
extend.note: The summons is sent throughout Israel with its threat in 10:21.

extend.title: Jehu orders his men to kill the assembled worshipers of Baal
extend.note: 10:24 posts the eighty men under penalty of life for any who escape.

extend.title: Joash directs the priests to use the silver to repair the temple
extend.note: Outside candidate list: the order begins in 12:5 by naming the silver to be received.

extend.title: Joash answers Amaziah with the story of the thornbush and cedar
extend.note: The fable's application follows in 14:10: enjoy your glory at home; why court disaster?

extend.title: Israel is warned to remember the covenant and reject other gods
extend.note: The positive counterpart follows in 17:39: fear the Lord your God, and He will rescue you.

extend.title: The Assyrian envoy tells Jerusalem not to trust Hezekiah
extend.note: His summons 'Hear the words of the great king' (18:28) opens the warning.

extend.title: Hezekiah asks Isaiah to pray for the remnant
extend.note: Hezekiah's message to Isaiah begins in 19:3.

extend.title: Sennacherib warns Hezekiah against trusting God to save Jerusalem
extend.note: Adds 19:9, where Sennacherib, hearing of Tharaka, sends the messengers ‘saying’; Isaiah 37:9 likewise precedes ot-isaiah-v37-10.

extend.title: The Lord sends Isaiah back with a promise to heal Hezekiah
extend.note: The message continues in 20:6 (fifteen added years, rescue of the city), as in the Isaiah 38:5 record.

extend.title: Josiah sends his scribe to the high priest to account for the silver
extend.note: Adds 22:3: the date and ‘the king sent Sapphan… saying’, which introduces the commission.

extend.title: Josiah asks his officials to seek the Lord about the recovered book
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 22:12 introduces the order ('The king commanded...').

extend.title: Huldah directs the officials to relay the Lord’s answer to Josiah
extend.note: The answer runs to 22:20, with a second 'say this' to the king at 22:18.

extend.title: David proposes bringing the ark back among the people
extend.note: The proposal begins in 13:2: send for the brethren, priests and Levites to gather.

extend.title: Joab urges courage in defending their people and cities
extend.note: The mutual-rescue arrangement (19:12) opens the same charge.

extend.title: David asks to purchase Orna’s threshing floor for an altar
extend.note: Outside candidate list: David insists on full price, refusing a costless offering (21:24).

extend.title: David urges Solomon to keep Moses’ ordinances and take courage
extend.note: 22:11-12 open the charge: build the house, and may the Lord give you wisdom to keep his law.

extend.title: David calls Israel’s leaders to seek the Lord and build the sanctuary

extend.title: Asa asks Syria’s king to make an alliance and drive Baasha away
