extend.note: 22:12 completes 22:11: mourning for the dead lasts seven days, for a fool all his life.

extend.title: Avoid needless argument with a fool
extend.note: 22:14–15 give the reason for 22:13.

extend.title: Learn to control your speech
extend.note: 23:8 is the reason clause of 23:7; the prayer in 23:1–6 is out of scope.

extend.title: Do not make a habit of swearing oaths
extend.note: 23:10–11 give the reasons: habitual swearing fills a house with lawlessness and calamity.

extend.title: A warning against deadly speech among God's people
extend.note: 23:15 closes the unit: one accustomed to abusive words is never instructed.

extend.title: Wisdom invites those who desire her to share her fruit
extend.note: 24:17 names the fruit offered in 24:19; 24:20–21 give the reasons. 24:18 is absent.

extend.title: Sirach's advice to fathers about watching over daughters
extend.note: 26:12 completes the warning of 26:11; extend 26:10–11 to 26:10–12.

extend.title: Listen to a person speak before praising their judgment
extend.note: 27:4–6 (sieve, furnace, fruit images) ground 27:7; extend 27:7 to 27:4–7.

extend.title: Be faithful to a friend and guard their secrets
extend.note: 27:16 states the principle (revealing secrets destroys trust); extend 27:17 to 27:16–17.

extend.title: The image of a friendship lost through betrayal
extend.note: 27:18–19 and 27:21 complete the images around 27:20; extend 27:20 to 27:18–21.

extend.title: Lend to a neighbor in need and repay debts on time
extend.note: 29:1 (mercy lends) and 29:3 (keep faith with the lender) frame 29:2; extend to 29:1–3.

extend.title: The image of giving to the poor as stored treasure
extend.note: 29:13 continues the image (almsgiving fights for you); extend 29:12 to 29:12–13.

extend.title: Remember the favor of someone who guaranteed your debt
extend.note: 29:14, 16 contrast the good guarantor with the ungrateful debtor; extend 29:15 to 29:14–16.

extend.title: Be content with little or much while a guest
extend.note: 29:21–22, 24 give the reasons (own roof better; a guest's life is grievous); extend 29:23 to 29:21–24.

extend.title: Do not surrender to grief and brooding
extend.note: 30:22 is the reason (gladness of heart is life); extend 30:21 to 30:21–22.

extend.title: Take comfort and do not let grief consume you
extend.note: 30:24–25 continue the reason (jealousy and anxiety shorten days); extend 30:23 to 30:23–25.

extend.title: Eat with restraint and know when to stop
extend.note: 31:19–20 give the reasons (a little suffices; moderation brings healthy sleep); extend 31:16–18 to 31:16–20.

extend.title: Do not try to prove your strength through drinking
extend.note: 31:26 is the reason (wine tests hearts in quarrels); extend 31:25 to 31:25–26.

extend.title: A banquet leader should serve without exalting himself
extend.note: 32:5–6 praise the music that 32:3–4 says not to interrupt; extend 32:1–4 to 32:1–6.

extend.title: Speak briefly when you are asked to speak
extend.note: 32:10 is the reason for 32:9's modesty (grace goes before the modest); extend 32:7–9 to 32:7–10.

extend.title: Consider the contrasts among God's works
extend.note: 33:14 states the pairs (good/evil, life/death, sinner/godly) that 33:15 tells the reader to consider.

extend.title: The teacher asks leaders to hear counsel on household affairs
extend.note: 33:22 is the reason for 33:19–21 (better your children ask of you); extend 33:18–21 to 33:18–22.

extend.title: Sirach's ancient household advice on forced labor and punishment
extend.note: 33:25 opens the same counsel (fodder, rod and work); extend 33:26–29 to 33:25–29.

extend.title: Do not put your trust in dreams without grounds
extend.note: 34:5, 7–8 surround 34:6 (omens are vain; dreams mislead; the law proves true); extend 34:6 to 34:5–8.

extend.title: The teacher calls worshipers to bring an offering
extend.note: 35:5–6 give the reason (the righteous one's offering is accepted and remembered); extend 35:4 to 35:4–6.

extend.title: Give generously and offer firstfruits with gladness
extend.note: 35:10 is the reason (the Lord repays sevenfold); extend 35:7–9 to 35:7–10.

extend.title: Consider whose interests an adviser is serving
extend.note: 37:7 (some counsel for themselves) and 37:9 (end of 37:8's sentence) belong to it; extend 37:8 to 37:7–9.

extend.title: Seek counsel from someone godly who shares your concerns
extend.note: 37:14 is the reason for trusting your heart's counsel (37:13); extend 37:12–13 to 37:12–14.

extend.title: Recognize what harms you and refrain from it
extend.note: 37:28 is the reason (not everything benefits everyone); extend 37:27 to 37:27–28.

extend.title: Exercise restraint with food and luxury
extend.note: 37:30–31 give the reasons (illness; many die of insatiability); extend 37:29 to 37:29–31.

extend.title: Honor the physician and recognize the need for care
extend.note: 38:2–3 give the reasons (healing is from the Most High; the physician's honored skill); extend 38:1 to 38:1–3.

extend.title: Mourn the dead and see to their burial
extend.note: 38:18–19 give the reason for limiting mourning (grief brings death); extend 38:16–17 to 38:16–19.

extend.title: Sirach's severe warning about a life of begging
extend.note: 40:29–30 give the reasons (dependence defiles; begging burns within); extend 40:28 to 40:28–30.

extend.title: Remember others who have died and do not fear death
extend.note: 41:4 is the reason (death is the Lord's sentence on all flesh); extend 41:3 to 41:3–4.

extend.title: Guard a good name more than great wealth
extend.note: 41:11, 13 frame 41:12 (sinners' names are blotted out; a good name endures); extend 41:12 to 41:11–13.

extend.title: Sirach's advice to fathers about a daughter's reputation
extend.note: 42:9–10 (a father's sleepless anxieties) lead into 42:11; extend 42:11–12 to 42:9–12 (see P01862).

extend.title: Look at the rainbow and bless its maker
extend.note: 43:12 completes the rainbow sentence (the Most High stretched it out); extend 43:11 to 43:11–12.

extend.title: God's greatness surpasses all the praise we can give
extend.note: 43:27–28 lead into 43:29–30 (we never reach the end; He is greater); with P01864 combined extension is 43:27–33.

extend.title: The Lord calls for justice for the wronged, the orphan and the widow
extend.note: 1:19–20 complete the 1:18 invitation (obey and eat the land's good; refuse and the sword devours); extend 1:17–18 to 1:17–20.

extend.title: Isaiah’s hearers are told to regard the Lord as holy
extend.note: 8:14–15 give the attached promise and warning (sanctuary or stumbling stone); extend 8:13 to 8:13–15. Quoted Romans 9:33; 1 Peter 2:8.

extend.title: Isaiah contrasts seeking mediums with turning to God
extend.note: 8:20 completes the contrast: God gave the law as a help against the mediums’ talk (MT: ‘To the law and the testimony!’).

extend.title: A signal summons forces in Isaiah’s vision against Babylon
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 13:3–4 report the Lord’s command to the mustered army ('I command'; 'the Lord Sabaoth has commanded').

extend.title: The Lord gives Eliakim the robe and authority of the steward
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 22:20 (I will call Eliakim) and 22:22–23 (David’s glory, established ruler) complete the appointment.

extend.title: The Lord tells Isaiah to write the warning for future generations
extend.note: 30:7 ('Announce to them, This consolation of yours is futile') opens the same charge to Isaiah.

extend.title: Isaiah warns the wealthy women about failed crops
extend.note: 32:9 ('rise and hear my voice') opens the address recorded at 32:10–12.

extend.title: The Assyrian envoy challenges Hezekiah’s confidence
extend.note: 36:2 records the sending of the envoy that this Commission record describes.

extend.title: The Assyrian envoy offers security in exchange for surrender
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 36:17 finishes the offer begun in 36:16 (its parallel 2 Kings 18:32 is ot-2-kings-v18-32).

extend.title: Hezekiah’s delegation asks Isaiah to pray for the survivors
extend.note: Hezekiah sends the delegation (37:2) and its message begins at 37:3; first pass likewise extended 2 Kings 19:4 to 19:3–4.

extend.title: Assyria sends Hezekiah a warning against relying on God
extend.note: The sending of the messengers named in the title is in 37:9.

extend.title: Survivors from the nations are called to gather, unlike idol worshippers
extend.note: 45:21 continues the summons ('let them draw near so that they may know together').

extend.title: The servant is appointed to restore Israel and bring salvation to the nations
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 49:2–3 (equipped, and named 'My slave, Israel') begin the commission recorded at 49:5–6.

extend.title: The servant is to call prisoners into freedom and light
extend.note: 49:8 ('I gave you as a covenant for nations… saying to those in bonds') begins the sentence recorded at 49:9.

extend.title: The people who seek the Lord are called to remember their origins
extend.note: 51:2 completes the same directive ('Look at Abraham your father and Sarah').

extend.title: The Lord calls people away from what cannot satisfy
extend.note: 55:1 opens the invitation continued in 55:2; echoed in Revelation 22:17 (AUD-70-22-17) and John 7:37 (AUD-47-7-37).

extend.title: God tells young Jeremiah to go where he is sent and speak His words
extend.note: 1:5 is the appointment ('I have appointed you a prophet to nations'); 1:6 is the objection answered in 1:7.

extend.title: God tells Jeremiah to rise and speak without fear
extend.note: 1:18–19 complete the charge: a fortified city and bronze wall against Judah’s kings, rulers and people.

extend.title: Judah is warned against trusting in slogans about the temple
extend.note: 7:8 repeats 7:4’s warning; 7:9 cites Decalogue prohibitions; 7:11 ('robbers’ cave') is quoted in Mark 11:17.

extend.title: God recalls telling Israel to listen and walk in His ways
extend.note: 7:22 is the contrast half of the same recollection: sacrifice was not the command, hearing was. Cf. 1 Sam 15:22, Hos 6:6.

extend.title: Jeremiah is told to speak the covenant words to Judah
extend.note: 11:3 continues the charge ('you will say to them') with the curse on whoever will not hear; bridges records 11:2 and 11:4.

extend.title: Zedekiah asks Jeremiah to seek the Lord about Babylon’s attack
extend.note: 21:1 records Zedekiah sending the two envoys who carry the request.

extend.title: The oracle calls for Babylon’s storehouses to be opened and destroyed
extend.note: 27:27 continues the same summons: 'Dry up all her fruits, and let them go down to slaughter.'

extend.title: A prayer acknowledges the Lord’s declaration against Babylon
extend.note: 28:61 opens Jeremiah’s charge ('When you arrive in Babylon… read all these words, and say'); consider retitling as the charge to Seraiah.

extend.title: Moab’s neighbors are called to mourn the breaking of its power
extend.note: 31:20 continues the same summons: 'Wail and cry out; announce at Arnon that Moab perished.'

extend.title: The cup pictures nations falling under the sword of judgment
extend.note: 32:28 continues the instruction: if they refuse the cup, say 'You will certainly drink.'

extend.title: The Rechabites recount Jonadab’s rule on houses, crops and tents
extend.note: 42:11 completes their account: the resolve 'Come in, let us enter Jerusalem' explains why they now live in the city.

extend.title: God sends Jeremiah to ask why Judah refuses instruction
extend.note: 42:14 is the message’s content: the Rechabites kept Jonadab’s command, Judah did not listen. 42:15 already has its own record.

extend.title: The survivors ask Jeremiah to seek the Lord’s direction
extend.note: The request begins in 49:2: 'Pray to the Lord your God for these survivors.'

extend.title: God tells Ezekiel to listen and eat what he is given
extend.note: 3:1–3 completes the same directive: 'eat this scroll, then go and speak to the sons of Israel.'

extend.title: Ezekiel is sent to speak the Lord’s words to the exiles
extend.note: 3:10–11 is one charge: 'take into your heart all the words… and go, enter the captivity.'

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to depict Jerusalem under siege
extend.note: 4:1 begins the same sign: take a brick and draw the city Jerusalem on it.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to lie on his side as a sign of Israel’s guilt
extend.note: 4:6 completes the sign: lie on the right side forty days for Judah, a day for a year.

extend.title: Ezekiel announces judgment to the mountains and valleys of Israel
extend.note: 6:2 holds the charge itself: ‘set your face firmly against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them’.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to enter and see the people’s wrongdoing
extend.note: ‘Son of man, dig’ (8:8) opens the way for ‘Go in and see’; one continuous order.

extend.title: Judgment in the vision begins at the sanctuary and spares the marked
extend.note: 9:7 completes the order: defile the house, fill the roads with the dead, go out and strike. Long record AUD-30-9-3 omits it.

extend.title: Ezekiel covers his face and goes out as a sign
extend.note: 12:3–5 hold the rest of the exile sign (ready baggage by day, dig through the wall); 12:7 reports his compliance.

extend.title: God recalls Israel rejecting His ordinances in the wilderness
extend.note: 20:11 recalls giving the commands by which a person lives (Leviticus 18:5), which 20:13 says Israel rejected; 20:12 parallels ot-ezekiel-v20-20.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to wail because the sword has come on Israel
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 21:19 repeats the sign: prophesy and strike hand upon hand.

extend.title: Ezekiel charges Jerusalem with bloodshed and idolatry
extend.note: 22:2 holds the charge itself: 'display all her lawless deeds to her, and say'.

extend.title: The oracle summons a crowd against Oholah and Oholibah
extend.note: 23:47 continues the same imperatives: stone them and pierce them.

extend.title: Ezekiel addresses Tyre as a proud center of maritime trade
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 27:2 holds the charge 'take up a lament over Tyre'.

extend.title: Ezekiel addresses Israel’s land after neighboring peoples dishonor it
extend.note: 36:1 opens the same charge: 'prophesy concerning Israel's mountains and say'.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to speak the Lord’s word over the dry bones
extend.note: 37:5–6 is the word he must speak; 37:7 records that he prophesied as commanded.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to call the breath from the four winds
extend.note: 37:10 records his obedience: 'I prophesied as He commanded me'.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to write Judah and Joseph on two staffs
extend.note: 37:17 'join them as one staff' completes the sign; 37:18–20 tells him how to explain it.

extend.title: Ezekiel is told to deliver the Lord’s warning to Gog
extend.note: 38:2 holds the charge: 'set your face against Gog… and prophesy against him'.

extend.title: The oracle summons birds and beasts to a feast after judgment
extend.note: 39:18–20 continue the same summons ('you will eat… drink').

extend.title: God promises to dwell with Israel when they put away idolatry and bloodshed
extend.note: 43:7–8 states the same requirement: Israel will no longer profane My name by prostitution and murder.

extend.title: A grain and oil offering accompanies the morning sacrifice
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 46:13 prescribes the daily morning lamb itself, now only in broad record ot-ezekiel-v46-1.

extend.title: The decree to execute Babylon’s wise men
extend.note: 2:12 is the king's order itself; 2:14 names Arioch as the one ordered to carry it out.

extend.title: The accusers cite the king’s decree to worship the image
extend.note: 3:11 is the decree's penalty clause (the blazing furnace).

extend.title: Nebuchadnezzar’s letter calls the nations to praise God
extend.note: 4:37c gives the same circular letter's greeting and purpose (to show there is a God) and reports it sent to all nations.

extend.title: Darius orders his kingdom to worship Daniel’s God
extend.note: 6:28 completes the decree with Darius's own pledge and its reason.

extend.title: Gabriel tells Daniel why he came to explain the vision
extend.note: 9:22 opens the same explanation: 'I have just come out to show you understanding.'

extend.title: Daniel challenges the unexamined verdict and separates the witnesses
extend.note: Outside candidate list: 1:54 questions the first elder (cf. the 1:58 record); 1:56 orders the second brought.

extend.title: Hosea calls Israel to return to the Lord with a confession
extend.note: 14:4 continues the words Israel is told to take: Assyria will not save us; no more horses or handmade 'gods'.

extend.title: The Lord calls the people to consider their ways
extend.note: 1:7 repeats the 1:5 call (‘Place your hearts upon your ways’) before the rebuilding order in 1:8.

extend.title: The Lord sends Zerubbabel a message about shaking heaven and earth
extend.note: The message runs to 2:23, where the Lord chooses Zerubbabel and makes him like a signet.

extend.title: The Lord calls the dispersed to flee the northern land
extend.note: 2:11 continues the same call (‘Escape safely to Zion’); AUD-42-2-7’s note already treats 2:10–11 as one unit.

extend.title: Zechariah announces the one called Rising who will build the Lord’s house
extend.note: The message ends with a condition: ‘This will happen if you truly listen to the voice of the Lord your God.’

extend.title: The Lord questions whom the people fasted for
extend.note: 7:6 completes the same question: their eating and drinking, like their fasting, was for themselves.

extend.title: The Lord warns the priests to honor His name
extend.note: 2:1 introduces the same charge: 'And now this command is for you, priests.'

extend.title: Malachi warns against abandoning the wife of one’s youth
extend.note: The charge begins at 2:13–14: offerings are refused because they abandoned the wife of their youth.

extend.title: The Lord calls the people to return after straying from His ordinances
extend.note: The sentence ‘you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain from the injustices of your fathers’ begins in 3:6.

extend.title: The Lord challenges the people to test His provision through the dues
extend.note: 3:8–9 name what is withheld, the tithes and firstfruits ('you are defrauding Me'), which the 3:10 challenge concerns.

extend.title: Jesus calls fishermen to follow him
extend.note: Not a listed candidate: the call of James and John (4:21–22) is uncovered. Mark 1:16–20 is also unlinked.

extend.title: Let your light shine so others glorify the Father
extend.note: 5:14–15 (light of the world, lamp on the stand) lead directly into the command of 5:16.

extend.title: Reconcile with your brother and settle with your accuser
extend.note: 5:26 completes the settlement warning; the linked Luke 12:57–59 already includes its parallel (12:59).

extend.title: Ask, seek, and knock
extend.note: 7:9–11 (the Father gives good things to those who ask) parallel Luke 11:11–13, already linked.

extend.title: Beware of false prophets and recognize them by their fruit
extend.note: Not a listed candidate: 7:17–20 (good and rotten trees) are uncovered and complete the same teaching.

extend.title: Jesus sends the man he healed to the priest with the prescribed offering
extend.note: Linked Mark 1:40–45 already includes the healing word ‘be cleansed’; the Matthew reference starts only at 8:4.

extend.title: Jesus tells his critics to learn why God desires mercy
extend.note: Not a listed candidate: 9:12 (the physician saying) opens the same reply; Mark 2:17 and Luke 5:31–32 are also unrecorded.

extend.title: Jesus sends the Twelve to Israel to proclaim the kingdom and heal freely
extend.note: 10:1’s grant of authority parallels Luke 9:1–2, already linked; Mark 6:7 is also unlinked.

extend.title: Trust what will be given to say when you are handed over
extend.note: 10:17–18 open the same warning; its Mark 13:9 parallel ('they will hand you over to councils') is already linked.

extend.title: Jesus tells his disciples whom to fear
extend.note: 10:29–31 (sparrows, numbered hairs, 'So do not fear') are already linked in their Luke 12:6–7 form.

extend.title: Jesus says it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath
extend.note: 'Stretch out your hand' (12:13) completes the scene; the linked Luke 6:6–11 already includes the same healing order.

extend.title: Jesus warns against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees
extend.note: 16:11–12 repeat the warning of 16:6 and explain it as the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

extend.title: Deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow Jesus
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 16:26–27 (gaining the world, forfeiting life; repaid by conduct) complete the call, as the linked Luke 9:24–26.

extend.title: Jesus directs Peter to pay the temple tax to avoid giving offense
extend.note: 17:24 is the collectors' question that occasions the instruction: 'Does not your Teacher pay the didrachmas?'

extend.title: Jesus calls his disciples to turn and become like children
extend.note: Outside candidate list; the question of greatness (18:1–2) and 'whoever receives one such child receives Me' (18:5) frame 18:3–4.

extend.title: Jesus teaches on marriage and Moses’ permission to divorce
extend.note: The testing question opens the teaching; first pass widened the Mark link to 10:2–12 the same way (B20 P02640).

extend.title: Jesus tells the rich man to keep the commandments
extend.note: The question 'what good thing shall I do?' (19:16) is the occasion of the command in 19:17.

extend.title: Seek greatness through serving others
extend.note: The contrast with the rulers of the nations (20:25) opens the teaching; the ten's indignation (20:24) is its occasion.

extend.title: Give Caesar what is Caesar’s and God what is God’s
extend.note: The tribute question and 'Show Me the coin' (22:17–19) lead directly into the command of 22:21.

extend.title: Jesus warns his disciples against claiming religious titles
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 23:11–12 close the unit (servant greatness, the self-exalted humbled), as K054 and Luke 14:11 (K056).

extend.title: Jesus rebukes neglect of justice, mercy, and faithfulness
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 'straining out the gnat but swallowing the camel' (23:24) completes the tithing woe.

extend.title: Stay watchful because the time is unknown
extend.note: The ten virgins parable (25:1–12) is the illustration whose application, 25:13, the record already holds.

extend.title: Jesus identifies with the least of his brothers
extend.note: The judgment scene (25:31–39) leads to 25:40; 25:41–46 is already linked. Covers candidates 25:37–39 (P02582).

extend.title: Jesus tells the disciples to watch and pray in Gethsemane
extend.note: 'Sit here', 'remain here and keep watch' and 'rise, let us go' frame 26:41; his prayer (26:39) is out of scope. Covers 26:45–46.

extend.title: The chief priests decline to put blood money in the treasury
extend.note: Judas returns the silver and is told 'See to it yourself' (27:4); the ruling on the coins follows in 27:6.

extend.title: Make disciples of all nations, baptize them, and teach them
extend.note: The eleven go to the mountain 'where Jesus had directed them' (28:16; compare 28:10 in AUD-44-28-5), setting the commission.

extend.title: Jesus declares the Son of Man Lord of the Sabbath
extend.note: The Pharisees' charge, 'not lawful on the Sabbath' (2:24), is the occasion; the linked Luke 6:1–5 already includes it.

extend.title: Attend to what you hear
extend.note: Outside candidate list; the lamp on the stand (4:21–22) opens the same unit. Luke 8:16–18 (candidate 8:18) parallels 4:21–25.

extend.title: Jesus tells his disciples not to stop someone acting in his name
extend.note: Outside candidate list; John's report (9:38) is the occasion, as in linked Luke 9:49. The cup-of-water saying (9:41) matches Matthew 10:42 (AUD-47-13-20).

extend.title: Have salt in yourselves and live at peace
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 'everyone will be salted with fire' (9:49) leads into the salt saying of 9:50.

extend.title: Love God with heart, soul, mind, and strength
extend.note: The scribe's question 'Which commandment is first of all?' opens it; first pass linked Matthew 22:34–38 likewise (B20 P02573).

extend.title: Gabriel tells Zechariah to name the child John
extend.note: The same message sets John's abstention from wine and strong drink (1:15; compare C0811 and Judges 13) and his Elijah mission (1:17).

extend.title: Gabriel tells Mary to name her son Jesus
extend.note: Greeting (1:28), question (1:34) and consent (1:38) frame the naming command; compare AUD-44-1-20, which includes Joseph's compliance. Covers P02675.

extend.title: Jesus silences and expels the unclean spirit
extend.note: The crowd's 'With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits' (4:36) reports the same command.

extend.title: Rise, carry the bed, and go home
extend.note: 'Rise and walk' (5:23) introduces the order of 5:24; he obeys in 5:25.

extend.title: Love your enemies, do good, and lend freely
extend.note: The 'what credit is that to you?' contrasts (6:32–34) lead straight into 6:35.

extend.title: Report what Jesus is doing
extend.note: John sends two disciples with the question that Jesus' charge answers; first pass linked Matthew 11:2–6 the same way (B20 P02528).

extend.title: Recognize the connection between forgiveness and love
extend.note: 7:48–50 complete the scene: 'Your sins are forgiven... Your faith has saved you; go in peace.'

extend.title: Hear and hold the word with perseverance
extend.note: Outside candidate list; the sowing itself (8:4–7) precedes the record's 8:8 start.

extend.title: Hear God’s word and do it
extend.note: The report that his mother and brothers stand outside (8:19–20) is the occasion; the linked Matthew and Mark accounts include it.

extend.title: Trust Jesus and care for the restored child
extend.note: The messenger's 'Do not trouble the Teacher any longer' (8:49) is what 'Do not fear; only believe' (8:50) answers.

extend.title: Give the crowd something to eat
extend.note: The Twelve's 'Dismiss the crowd' (9:12) is the request Jesus answers with 'You give them something to eat.'

extend.title: Show mercy as the Samaritan did
extend.note: Record holds only the application (10:36–37); link the parable body, including the care paid for at the inn (10:35).

extend.title: Guard against greed and reliance on possessions
extend.note: Add the inheritance request and the rich fool parable, which illustrate 12:15; parable imperatives need no own record.

extend.title: Choose the lowest place at a feast
extend.note: 14:8–9 gives the same directive negatively: do not take the foremost place.

extend.title: Jesus teaches about using wealth and being faithful in small matters
extend.note: Add the shrewd steward parable (16:1–8), whose lesson 16:9 states; its inner imperatives need no own record.

extend.title: Serve without claiming special credit
extend.note: 17:7–9 is the illustration whose application (17:10) the record already holds.

extend.title: Remember Lot’s wife and do not turn back
extend.note: 17:34–35 (one taken, one left) close the same warning; first pass linked Matthew's form (24:40–41) to K083 (B20 P02579).

extend.title: Jesus teaches persistence in prayer
extend.note: Add the widow and unjust judge parable, including 18:6 'Hear what the unrighteous judge says.'

extend.title: Jesus commissions his witnesses and tells them to wait in the city
extend.note: 24:44–45 opens the same charge: everything written in the Law, Prophets and Psalms must be fulfilled.

extend.title: Jesus teaches Nicodemus about birth from above
extend.note: 3:8–15 continues the same teaching: the Spirit like wind, and belief in the lifted-up Son.

extend.title: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman about worship in spirit and truth
extend.note: 4:20 states the disputed rule about where one must worship, which 4:21–24 answers.

extend.title: Jesus sends his disciples to reap where others have labored
extend.note: 4:31–34 (the disciples' 'Rabbi, eat' and Jesus' saying about his food) opens the same exchange.

extend.title: Honor the Son as the Father is honored
extend.note: 5:25–30 continues the discourse, including 'Do not marvel at this' and judgment by deeds.

extend.title: Jesus explains how his works and the Scriptures bear witness to him
extend.note: 5:31–35 (John's testimony, 'so that you may be saved') opens the same witness teaching.

extend.title: Believe in the one God has sent
extend.note: 6:35–37 restates the call: whoever comes and believes will never hunger or thirst. 6:34 is a request.

extend.title: Jesus teaches about eating his flesh and drinking his blood
extend.note: 6:48–51 is the same bread-of-life teaching that 6:53–56 completes.

extend.title: Judge with righteousness rather than by appearances
extend.note: 7:19 (none of you keeps the Law) and 7:21 (one work, and you all marvel) open the argument; 7:22 begins mid-thought.

extend.title: The authorities threaten synagogue exclusion for confessing Jesus as Christ
extend.note: The 'Give glory to God' adjuration (9:24) and the expulsion (9:34) carry out the threat.

extend.title: Jesus calls his opponents to consider his works
extend.note: 10:25 'the works I do... bear witness' opens the same appeal; 10:33 states the blasphemy charge.

extend.title: Wash one another’s feet as Jesus did
extend.note: The washing itself and 'unless I wash you, you have no share with Me' (13:4–11) precede the command.

extend.title: Remain in Jesus as branches in the vine
extend.note: 15:6 (the branch thrown out) sits between the record's 15:4–5 and its linked 15:7–10; 15:1–3 opens the figure.

extend.title: Ask the Father in Jesus’ name
extend.note: 16:26–27 continues: 'on that day you will ask in My name', for the Father loves you.

extend.title: Jesus’ accusers invoke their law in demanding his death
extend.note: 19:12–15 continues the same demand ('Take Him away! Crucify Him!') with the appeal to Caesar.

extend.title: Follow Jesus without speculating about the other disciple
extend.note: 'Follow Me' (21:19), after the prediction of Peter's death, is the charge repeated in 21:22.

extend.title: Peter connects the outpouring of the Spirit with Joel’s prophecy
extend.note: 2:14–15 ('let this be known to you, and listen closely to my words') opens the same explanation.

extend.title: Salvation is found in Jesus alone
extend.note: 4:10–11 ('let it be known... in the name of Jesus Christ'; the rejected stone) leads into 4:12.

extend.title: Peter tells Simon to repent and pray after trying to buy the gift
extend.note: Simon's request to buy the power (8:18–19) is the occasion of Peter's command.

extend.title: The Jerusalem council sets out four abstentions for Gentile believers
extend.note: James' speech opens at 15:13 with a call to listen and grounds the decree in Amos 9:11–12 (15:16–18).

extend.title: Carry and confirm the Jerusalem council’s decision
extend.note: 15:30–32: the letter delivered and confirmed by word of mouth as charged (15:27); 15:33: the envoys dismissed to their senders.

extend.title: God calls all people to repent in view of the coming judgment
extend.note: 17:27–28 state God's purpose that people seek and find Him; same speech unit leading to the 17:30 command.

extend.title: Paul tells the Ephesian elders to shepherd the flock and watch for threats
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 20:26–27 (clean from all blood, whole purpose declared) is the example 20:31 tells them to remember.

extend.title: Paul urges support for the weak and recalls Jesus’ words on giving
extend.note: Outside candidate list; 20:33–34 is the example that 20:35 'in this way' applies. 20:32 is a commendation, out of scope.

extend.title: Report the plot and secure Paul’s transfer
extend.note: Outside candidate list; the letter (23:25–30) orders accusers to state their case before Felix; soldiers act 'according to their orders' (23:31).

extend.title: Do not let sin reign, and present yourselves to God
extend.note: 6:1–2 rejects continuing in sin, the premise of the 6:11–14 directive; 6:3–4 has study record A006.

extend.title: Put the body’s sinful practices to death by the Spirit
extend.note: 8:5–8 contrasts the two mindsets that ground the 8:12–13 directive; 8:9–11 is doctrine.

extend.title: Do not boast over the branches; remain in God’s kindness
extend.note: 11:25 discloses the mystery so they will not be conceited, extending the 'do not boast' warning.

extend.title: Paul warns against taking vengeance into one’s own hands
extend.note: 12:17a is the same non-retaliation directive as 12:19; compare A018 (1 Peter 3:9).

extend.title: Blessing persecutors and overcoming evil with good
extend.note: A017's title already names overcoming evil with good (12:21), but its reference is only 12:14.

extend.title: Submission to governing authorities and payment of what is owed
extend.note: A050's title names payment of what is owed (13:6–7) but cites only 13:1; compare K078 (render to Caesar).

extend.title: Paul urges believers not to let food harm another’s faith
extend.note: 14:16 lies between A027's 14:13–15 and its linked 14:19–23.

extend.title: Paul contrasts disputes about food with life in God’s kingdom
extend.note: A033's title describes the 14:17 contrast but cites only 14:14.

extend.title: Imitate Paul’s example and hear Timothy’s reminder
extend.note: 4:12–13 describes the conduct Paul then urges them to imitate (4:16); 4:8–10 is ironic rebuke. / Closes the 4:14–17 admonition; 'God's kingdom is in power, not in talk' (4:20).

extend.title: Paul applies the law about the threshing ox to material support for ministry
extend.note: 9:4–7 states the right and its everyday analogies, which 9:8–11 grounds in the threshing-ox law.

extend.title: Paul explains why he limits his own rights while proclaiming the gospel
extend.note: 9:12b states the renunciation that 9:15–23 explains; 9:13–14 is A047.

extend.title: Honor interdependent members and desire the greater gifts
extend.note: 12:7 ('for the common benefit') frames the body teaching of 12:12–31; compare AUD-49-12-3.

extend.title: Look to what is unseen and lasting amid affliction
extend.note: 4:7–15 is the hardship from which 4:16 ('therefore we do not lose heart') draws its conclusion. / 5:1–8 continues 4:16–18 on the unseen and eternal across the chapter break.

extend.title: Do not receive God’s grace in vain
extend.note: 6:3–10 continues the 6:1 appeal, describing ministers' blameless endurance; largely a model to imitate.

extend.title: Giving freely as one has decided in the heart
extend.note: The sowing image of 9:6–7 continues to 9:10–14: God supplies givers, and the gift yields thanksgiving.

extend.title: Reject a gospel contrary to what was received
extend.note: Extend its Additional Scripture 2 Corinthians 11:1–6 to 11:1–15; the warning about rival apostles continues.

extend.title: Paul learns to regard his weakness in light of Christ’s power
extend.note: 12:7 ('because of the surpassing revelations') depends on 12:1–6; 12:5 states the rule of boasting in weakness.

extend.title: Paul challenges pressure on Gentiles to adopt Jewish practice
extend.note: The quoted speech runs 2:14–21 but the record stops at 2:14; includes 2:21 (P02977). A053 covers 2:19–20.

extend.title: Stand firm in freedom rather than seeking justification through circumcision
extend.note: Extend Additional Scripture Galatians 4:8–12 to 4:8–20; 4:18 adds 'good to be zealously sought for good'. / Continues 5:1–6 against the circumcision agitators: 'the one troubling you will bear the judgment' (5:10).

extend.title: Proclaim Christ’s riches among the nations
extend.note: 3:2 'the stewardship of God's grace given to me for you' begins the commission continued in 3:7–13.

extend.title: Truthful speech that builds up others
extend.note: A035's title ('builds up others') is 4:29's content; AUD-53-4-28's note says the speech verse is cited elsewhere.

extend.title: Paul urges his readers to put away anger and bitterness
extend.note: A020's title ('put away anger and bitterness') is 4:31's content, but its reference is only 4:26–27.

extend.title: Husbands are called to love their wives as Christ loved the church
extend.note: Fills the gap inside A049's husbands' instruction (5:25 and 5:28–30). / AUD-53-5-22's note says the husbands' record 'also draws on verses 31–33'; 5:31 quotes Genesis 2:24.

extend.title: Paul’s household instruction to wives
extend.note: 5:33b repeats the direction to wives; the record stops at 5:24.

extend.title: Christ’s self-humbling as the pattern for putting others first
extend.note: 2:2 and 2:3–4 are one sentence; A024 begins mid-exhortation at 2:3. / Completes the Christ hymn whose humbling A024 records (2:3–8); exaltation follows humility.

extend.title: Make God’s message known and present people mature in Christ
extend.note: Paul's labor for maturity in 1:28–29 continues directly into 2:1–3.

extend.title: Walk in Christ and resist teaching that would capture you
extend.note: Same warning as 2:8 ('Watch out that no one carries you off'), stated first at 2:4.

extend.title: Do not be unsettled or deceived by claims that the Lord’s day has arrived
extend.note: Explains 2:1–4: the restrainer, the lawless one's deceptions, and delusion for those refusing the truth.

extend.title: Pray and give thanks for all people, including rulers
extend.note: 2:4 completes the sentence of 2:3; the one mediator and ransom for all ground the prayer for all.

extend.title: Rekindle the gift and share hardship without shame
extend.note: Examples of the charge 'do not be ashamed... of me his prisoner' (1:8); the blessings in 1:16, 18 are out of scope.

extend.title: Consider the soldier, athlete and farmer while enduring hardship
extend.note: 2:9 completes the sentence of 2:8 ('my gospel, for which I suffer hardship'); same call to endure hardship.

extend.title: Turn away from people who deny the power of godliness
extend.note: Describes the people Timothy must turn away from (3:5), likened to Jannes and Jambres.

extend.title: Proclaim the word and fulfill the work of an evangelist
extend.note: 4:6 ('For I am already being poured out') grounds the charge of 4:1–5.

extend.title: Insist that believers devote themselves to good works
extend.note: The 'trustworthy saying' and 'these things' Titus must insist on (3:8) are 3:4–7; 3:3 grounds 3:1–2.

extend.title: Paul appeals to Philemon to welcome Onesimus as a brother and charge any debt to Paul
extend.note: Closes the appeal about Onesimus that A029 records (1:8–20).

extend.title: Hearing God’s voice without hardening the heart
extend.note: Extend its Additional Scripture Hebrews 4:1–11 to 4:1–13; 4:12–13 ground the call to enter the rest (4:11).

extend.title: Continue diligent service and imitate those who inherit the promises
extend.note: Abraham 'waited patiently and obtained the promise' (6:15) illustrates 6:12; 6:18 urges holding fast the hope.

extend.title: Approach and worship, covenant words and blood, ascent for the tablets, and elders' responsibilities
extend.note: Its Additional Scripture Hebrews 9:19–20 should run 9:18–22; 9:21 recalls Leviticus 8, 9:22 Leviticus 17:11.

extend.title: Abel, Enoch, and Noah as examples of faith
extend.note: The definition heading the examples that A072 begins at 11:4; 11:6 (in A072) depends on it.

extend.title: Run with endurance, lay aside sin, and look to Jesus
extend.note: Continues the race and 'consider Jesus' of 12:1–3 and leads into A115 (12:5–11).

extend.title: Heed the One who speaks and worship with gratitude and reverence
extend.note: The Sinai–Zion contrast grounds 12:25 ('See that you do not refuse the One who speaks'); 12:20 is C0140.

extend.title: James warns against favoring the rich in the gathering
extend.note: Extend A028 (2:1–5) through the rebuke (2:6–7) and the verdict on favoritism (2:9); 2:8 is A011, 2:10–12 A089.

extend.title: The need for practical help illustrates faith at work
extend.note: Extend AUD-63-2-14 (2:14–17) to 2:14–20: the objector's reply and 'faith apart from works is idle' lead into A070 (2:21).

extend.title: Friendship with the world puts one at odds with God
extend.note: Scriptural motive for 4:4's warning against friendship with the world; extend AUD-63-4-4 to 4:4–5 (A116 begins at 4:6).

extend.title: James denounces the rich who withhold workers’ wages
extend.note: Extend A045 to 5:1–6 and retype it Wisdom: a woe whose 5:1 summons the rich to weep and howl.

extend.title: Explain the reason for hope with gentleness and a good conscience
extend.note: 'For Christ also suffered' grounds 3:17's maxim on suffering for doing good, as Christ's example does at 2:21 (A052).

extend.title: Build up virtue and confirm your calling
extend.note: 1:5 'for this very reason' rests on the 'since' clause of 1:3–4; extend AUD-65-1-5 to 1:3–11. Doctrinal ground, so low. / 'Remind you of these things' refers to 1:5–11; extend AUD-65-1-5 to 1:5–15. Autobiographical; cf. the same reminding in AUD-65-3-1 (3:1–2).

extend.title: Sodom’s judgment and Lot’s rescue as examples
extend.note: One conditional sentence runs 2:4–10a ('If God did not spare… then the Lord knows'); extend A096 (2:6–9) to 2:4–10a.

extend.title: Remember the prophets and the Lord’s command through the apostles
extend.note: Peter's answer to the scoffers quoted in 3:4; extend AUD-65-3-1 (3:1–4) to 3:1–7, before A120 (3:8).

extend.title: Holy conduct in anticipation of the day of God
extend.note: Completes the 'waiting' of 3:12 and grounds 3:14 ('as you await these things'); extend A059 (3:10–12) to 3:10–13.

extend.title: Walking in the light and confessing sins truthfully
extend.note: 'I write these things so that you may not sin' completes 1:5–10's teaching on sin and confession; extend AUD-66-1-5 to 1:5–2:2.

extend.title: Let the teaching heard from the beginning remain in you
extend.note: 2:24 'As for you' answers 2:18–23, and 2:26 refers back; extend AUD-66-2-24 to 2:18–28. 2:22–23 state A061's confession test.

extend.title: Do not be deceived about who practices righteousness
extend.note: 3:4–6 open the contrast of practicing sin and righteousness that 3:7–10 complete; extend AUD-66-3-7 to 3:4–10.

extend.title: John likens hatred of a brother to murder
extend.note: 'The one who does not love abides in death' is completed by 3:15; extend A014 to 3:14–15.

extend.title: Testing whether spirits confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh
extend.note: 4:6 closes the test begun in 4:1: 'By this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.' Extend A061 to 4:1–6.

extend.title: Belief in Jesus Christ and love for one another
extend.note: Extend A012's Additional Scripture 1 John 4:7–12 to 4:7–16: belief (4:15) and love (4:16), the record's two elements; AUD-66-4-17 starts at 4:17. / 5:1–3 continue 4:21, an A012 link: extend it to 4:21–5:5. 5:3 also echoes K042 (John 14:15); faith overcomes the world (5:4–5).

extend.title: Guard yourselves from idols
extend.note: The closing 'we know' affirmations ground the final command; 5:20's 'true God' sets up 'guard yourselves from idols'. 5:18 restates 3:9.

extend.title: Jude condemns conduct like Cain’s, Balaam’s, and Korah’s
extend.note: The woe of 1:11 continues with the intruders' portrait and Enoch's prophecy of judgment; extend A095 to 1:11–16 (AUD-69-1-17 resumes at 1:17).

extend.title: Remember, repent and return to the first works
extend.note: Extend X009 (2:4–7) to the whole letter 2:1–7, with its 'write' order, as AUD-70-2-12 and AUD-70-2-18 cover theirs.

extend.title: Remain faithful through suffering
extend.note: Extend X010 (2:10–11) to the whole letter 2:8–11, including the order to write, as the Pergamum–Laodicea records do.

extend.title: Become watchful, remember and repent
extend.note: Adds the 'write' order and the rebuke that grounds 3:2–3; with P03091 (3:4–6) X011 becomes the whole letter 3:1–6.

extend.title: Those who wash their robes are blessed with access to the city
extend.note: The elder's answer runs to 7:17; extend AUD-70-22-14's Additional Scripture link 7:13–14 to 7:13–17. Promise rather than direction.

extend.title: The two witnesses receive authority to prophesy
extend.note: The authority granted in 11:3 is spelled out in 11:5–6; extend AUD-70-11-3 to 11:3–6. 11:7–10 narrate their death.

extend.title: Fear God, give Him glory and worship the Creator
extend.note: 14:9–12 (outside candidate list) is linked only to AUD-70-13-11, the beast's own decree; extend AUD-70-14-6 to the three angels' messages, 14:6–12.

extend.title: Discern the meaning of the beast’s seven heads in the vision
extend.note: The explanation announced in 17:7 runs to 17:18; extend AUD-70-17-7 (17:7–10) to 17:7–18.

extend.title: The heavenly voice calls for Babylon to be repaid for her deeds
extend.note: 'For this reason' completes the charge of 18:6–7; extend AUD-70-18-6 to 18:6–8. The laments (18:9–19) and millstone sign (18:21–24) need nothing.

extend.title: Praise God, all His servants and those who fear Him
extend.note: 'Hallelujah' (Praise the Lord) frames the call of 19:5; link 19:1–4 as Additional Scripture beside 19:6–8. Largely doxology, so low.

parallel.title: Abram asks Sarai to say she is his sister
parallel.note: Abraham recounts the standing request: in every place say of me, 'He is my brother.'

parallel.title: Abraham states when his servant’s oath will end
parallel.note: The servant repeats the release clause: if they do not give her, you are free from my oath.

parallel.title: Isaac charges Jacob about where to seek a wife
parallel.note: Narrator restates the charge: 'You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.'

parallel.title: Moses and Aaron: go to Pharaoh and deliver God's demands and warnings
parallel.note: Renewed sending within the same call dialogue; only broad torah-exodus-4-1 covers it. 4:14 is prediction.

parallel.title: Pharaoh keeps the brick quota unchanged
parallel.note: Restates Pharaoh's unchanged quota (5:8, 5:18) as the scribes heard it.

parallel.title: Moses: announce God's identity and promised deliverance to Israel
parallel.note: Renewed charge to announce 'I am the Lord' and promised deliverance, as at 3:14–17; only broad torah-exodus-6-2 covers it.

parallel.title: Moses and Aaron: go to Pharaoh and deliver God's demands and warnings
parallel.note: Renewed commission to go to Pharaoh (3:10); 6:12 is Moses' objection.

parallel.title: Moses and Aaron: bring Israel out of Egypt
parallel.note: Reported charge to both brothers, restating C0064 (3:10).

parallel.title: Aaron: speak as Moses' appointed spokesman
parallel.note: Restates the spokesman arrangement of 4:15–16, now toward Pharaoh; 7:3–6 are prediction and fulfilment.

parallel.title: Moses: communicate God's words to Aaron
parallel.note: Same direction as 4:15 (C0076).

parallel.title: Select an unblemished year-old male lamb or goat for the Passover household, sharing according to the number of eaters
parallel.note: Moses relays C0092 (12:3–5) to the elders; no record covers 12:21.

parallel.title: Slaughter the Passover at the prescribed time and location
parallel.note: Relay of C0094 (12:6).

parallel.title: Apply the Passover blood to the doorposts and lintel with hyssop
parallel.note: Outside candidate list: C0095's hyssop detail comes from 12:22, which is linked only to C0110.

parallel.title: Keep the Passover memorial throughout the generations
parallel.note: Restates C0103 (12:14) and applies it to life in the land.

parallel.title: Teach children the Exodus deliverance, its signs and its observances
parallel.note: C0088's 'its observances' fits, but 12:26–27 is unlinked. 12:28 is fulfilment.

parallel.title: Do not break a bone of the Passover
parallel.note: Outside candidate list: 12:46 (Rambam N123's verse) repeats C0101's ban (12:10) but is linked only to C0112 and C0113.

parallel.title: Keep the Passover memorial throughout the generations
parallel.note: Universal obligation to observe; link to C0103 (12:14).

parallel.title: Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread
parallel.note: Moses' Exodus-day charge restates C0231 (23:15).

parallel.title: Eat unleavened bread during the appointed seven days
parallel.note: Same requirement as C0104 (12:15).

parallel.title: Teach children the Exodus deliverance, its signs and its observances
parallel.note: Rambam P157 is not itemized at 13:8; its substance is in C0088 (10:2, 'its observances'). Link here.

parallel.title: Consecrate the firstborn males to God
parallel.note: Restates C0115 (13:2) for life in the land; 13:13 is already itemized (C0118, C0119).

parallel.title: Teach children the Exodus deliverance, its signs and its observances
parallel.note: Second children's-question formula; link to C0088 with 12:26–27 and 13:8.

parallel.title: Keep the prescribed divine words and deliverance as signs on the hand and before the eyes
parallel.note: Repeats C0117 (13:9) within the same speech.

parallel.title: Joseph's charge about his bones, grounded in God's promised return
parallel.note: Quotes the Genesis 50:25 charge as Moses carries the bones; 13:17 is narrative.

parallel.title: Israel: gather the daily manna allowance for your households
parallel.note: Specifies C0125's daily allowance (16:4); only broad torah-exodus-16-16 covers 16:16.

parallel.title: Israel: remain in your places on the Sabbath instead of going out to gather manna
parallel.note: Moses' form of the no-gathering rule given at 16:29 (C0130).

parallel.title: Do no work on the Sabbath, including household members, servants, resident foreigners and livestock
parallel.note: Rambam P154 is itemized as C0152 (20:10) and C0129 (16:23); link 23:12.

parallel.title: Heed and obey God's commandments
parallel.note: Outside candidate list: 23:13a is unlinked (C0229 and S049 cover only the other-gods clause); same as 34:11.

parallel.title: Make the sanctuary and its furnishings according to the shown pattern
parallel.note: Hebrews 8:5, already on C0252, quotes 25:40 itself; only broad torah-exodus-25-1 covers the verse.

parallel.title: Make the sanctuary and its furnishings according to the shown pattern
parallel.note: Repeats C0252's pattern directive for erecting the tent; 26:15–25 are covered by C0271.

parallel.title: Clothe Aaron and his sons in their appointed garments
parallel.note: Rite steps unitemized between C0303 (29:4) and C0304 (29:10); same directive as 28:41.

parallel.title: Anoint Aaron and his sons for the priesthood
parallel.note: Ordination-rite step matching C0298 (28:41).

parallel.title: Consecrate Aaron and his sons for their ministry
parallel.note: Matches C0299 (28:41); 29:9 also declares a perpetual priesthood.

parallel.title: Anoint Aaron and his sons for the priesthood
parallel.note: Repeats C0298 (28:41); also link C0299 (consecrate).

parallel.title: Consecrate Aaron and his sons for their ministry
parallel.note: Repeats C0299 (28:41).

parallel.title: Aaron asks the people for their gold earrings
parallel.note: Aaron's retelling of his 32:2 order; ot-exodus-v32-22 stops at 32:23.

parallel.title: Moses: resume leading Israel toward the promised land
parallel.note: Outside candidate list: repeats C0358 (32:34); Moses quotes it at 33:12. 33:12–23 are prayer and promise.

parallel.title: Heed and obey God's commandments
parallel.note: Covenant-renewal opening; 34:9–10 are prayer and promise.

parallel.title: Make no covenant with the Canaanite peoples or their gods
parallel.note: Repeats C0244 (23:32); 34:16 is already ot-exodus-v34-16.

parallel.title: Destroy the Canaanite objects of idolatry
parallel.note: Repeats C0242 (23:24).

parallel.title: Do not bow down to other gods
parallel.note: Repeats C0148 (20:5).

Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread
parallel.note: Repeats C0231 (23:15).

parallel.note: Repeats C0104 (12:15).

parallel.title: Consecrate the firstborn males to God
parallel.note: Outside candidate list (context verse); repeats C0115 (13:2).

parallel.title: Redeem the firstborn donkey as prescribed
parallel.note: Rambam P81 is itemized as C0118 (13:13); link 34:20.

parallel.title: Redeem firstborn sons
parallel.note: Repeats C0119 (13:13).

parallel.title: Do not appear before God empty-handed
parallel.note: Repeats C0232 (23:15).

parallel.title: Do no work on the Sabbath, including household members, servants, resident foreigners and livestock

parallel.title: Keep the Feast of Harvest or Weeks
parallel.note: Repeats C0233 (23:16).

parallel.note: Repeats C0234 (23:16).

parallel.note: Rambam N115 is itemized as C0235 (23:18); link 34:25.

Bring the firstfruits of the land to God's house

Receive the willing-hearted sanctuary offerings of the specified materials

parallel.note: Outside candidate list: first half of 40:5 (C0368 covers only the screen); repeats C0336 (30:6).

parallel.note: Flock and bird cases of C0371 (1:2–3), whose title already names birds.

parallel.note: Flock case of C0374 (1:5).
